meta.description: God creates light, sky, land and vegetation, the lights of the dome, the creatures of sea and air, and the animals of the earth, and makes humankind in his image, male and female, giving them dominion.

events.title: God Rests on the Seventh Day

meta.description: On the seventh day God finishes his work and rests, blessing the seventh day and hallowing it.
The LORD God forms the man from the dust of the ground and breathes life into his nostrils, plants a garden in Eden watered by four rivers, and forbids the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
The man names every animal but finds no partner, so God causes a deep sleep to fall on him and makes a woman from his rib, whom the man greets as bone and flesh of his own body.

The serpent persuades the woman that she will not die; she eats and gives to her husband. Their eyes are opened, God curses the serpent and the ground, and they are driven from the garden, guarded by cherubim and a flaming sword.

The LORD has regard for Abel's offering but not Cain's. Cain kills his brother in the field, is cursed from the ground to be a fugitive and a wanderer, and is given a mark so no one who meets him will kill him.
Adam and Eve have another son, Seth, appointed in place of Abel. To Seth is born Enosh, and at that time people begin to invoke the name of the LORD.

events.title: The Line of Cain and the Song of Lamech

meta.description: Cain builds a city named for his son Enoch. His descendants include Jabal, ancestor of herders, Jubal of musicians, and Tubal-cain, maker of bronze and iron tools. Lamech boasts of seventy-sevenfold vengeance.
All the days that Adam lived were nine hundred thirty years; and he died.

events.title: Enoch Walks with God and Is Taken

meta.description: Enoch walks with God three hundred years after the birth of Methuselah; then he was no more, because God took him. All his days were three hundred sixty-five years.

events.title: The Sons of God and the Nephilim

meta.description: The sons of God take wives from the daughters of humans. The LORD limits mortal life to one hundred twenty years, and the Nephilim, heroes of old and warriors of renown, are on the earth in those days.

events.title: God Commands Noah to Build the Ark

meta.description: Seeing that the earth is corrupt and filled with violence, God resolves to blot out all flesh, but Noah finds favor. He is told to build an ark of cypress wood, three hundred cubits long, and to bring two of every kind aboard.

events.title: The Fountains of the Deep Burst Forth

meta.description: In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month on the seventeenth day, all the fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of the heavens are opened. Rain falls forty days, and the waters swell one hundred fifty days.

events.title: The Ark Rests on the Mountains of Ararat

meta.description: God remembers Noah and makes a wind blow over the earth. At the end of one hundred fifty days the waters abate, and in the seventh month on the seventeenth day the ark comes to rest on the mountains of Ararat.
Noah sends out a raven, then a dove three times; the second returns with a freshly plucked olive leaf. In the six hundred first year, in the second month on the twenty-seventh day, the earth is dry.

events.title: Noah Leaves the Ark and Builds an Altar

meta.description: Noah goes out with his family and every living thing and builds an altar. Smelling the pleasing odor, the LORD resolves never again to curse the ground: as long as the earth endures, seedtime and harvest shall not cease.
God blesses Noah, permits the eating of meat but not blood, requires a reckoning for human blood, and sets his bow in the clouds as the sign that never again will a flood destroy the earth.

events.title: Noah's Vineyard and the Curse of Canaan

meta.description: Noah plants a vineyard, becomes drunk, and lies uncovered. Ham sees his father's nakedness while Shem and Japheth cover him walking backward. Noah curses Canaan and blesses Shem and Japheth.
The descendants of Japheth, Ham, and Shem spread into their lands by families and languages. Nimrod becomes a mighty hunter whose kingdom begins at Babel in Shinar, and who builds Nineveh.

The whole earth has one language. Settling in Shinar, the people build a city and a tower with its top in the heavens to make a name for themselves. The LORD confuses their language and scatters them over the face of the earth.
Terah takes Abram, Sarai, and his grandson Lot out from Ur of the Chaldeans to go to Canaan, but they settle in Haran, where Terah dies at two hundred five years.

The LORD tells Abram to leave his country and kindred for a land he will be shown, promising to make of him a great nation in whom all families of the earth will be blessed. Seventy-five years old, he departs Haran and builds altars at Shechem and Bethel.
Driven by famine to Egypt, Abram calls Sarai his sister; she is taken into Pharaoh's house. The LORD afflicts Pharaoh with great plagues, and Pharaoh sends them away with all they have.

Their possessions too great to dwell together, Abram offers Lot his choice. Lot takes the well-watered plain of the Jordan and moves his tent toward Sodom, while Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron.

events.title: Abram Rescues Lot and Meets Melchizedek

meta.description: Four eastern kings defeat the kings of the plain and carry Lot off. Abram leads three hundred eighteen trained men, routs them near Damascus, and is blessed by Melchizedek king of Salem, priest of God Most High, giving him a tenth of everything.

Told to count the stars, Abram believes the LORD, and it is reckoned to him as righteousness. In a deep and terrifying darkness he learns his offspring will be aliens and slaves four hundred years; a smoking fire pot and flaming torch pass between the divided animals.

events.title: Hagar Flees and Ishmael Is Born

meta.description: Sarai gives her Egyptian slave-girl Hagar to Abram. Pregnant and treated harshly, Hagar flees to a spring in the wilderness, where the angel of the LORD sends her back with a promise. She names the LORD El-roi. Abram is eighty-six when Ishmael is born.

When Abram is ninety-nine, God renames him Abraham and Sarai Sarah, promises a son by her, and gives circumcision as the sign of an everlasting covenant. Abraham and Ishmael are circumcised that very day.

events.title: The Three Visitors and Sarah's Laughter

meta.description: Three men appear by the oaks of Mamre in the heat of the day. Abraham hurries to prepare curds, milk, and a calf. Told she will bear a son, Sarah laughs to herself and is asked whether anything is too wonderful for the LORD.
Abraham presses the LORD from fifty righteous down to ten, appealing to him as the judge of all the earth who must surely do what is just. The LORD agrees not to destroy the city for the sake of ten.

events.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah

meta.description: Two angels are sheltered by Lot and besieged by the men of the city, who are struck blind. Lot lingers and is seized by the hand and brought out. The LORD rains sulfur and fire on the cities; Lot's wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt.

events.title: Lot and His Daughters in the Cave

meta.description: Afraid to stay in Zoar, Lot lives in a cave with his two daughters, who make him drink wine and lie with him. Their sons Moab and Ben-ammi become the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.

Residing in Gerar, Abraham again calls Sarah his sister, and King Abimelech takes her. Warned in a dream by night, Abimelech restores her with sheep, oxen, and a thousand pieces of silver, and Abraham prays for his healing.

The LORD does for Sarah as he had promised. Abraham is a hundred years old when Isaac is born, and circumcises him at eight days. Sarah says that God has brought her laughter, and that all who hear will laugh with her.

At the feast for Isaac's weaning Sarah demands the slave woman and her son be cast out. In the wilderness of Beer-sheba, when the water is gone, God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
Abimelech and Phicol swear an oath with Abraham over a disputed well. Abraham sets apart seven ewe lambs as witness that he dug it, names the place Beer-sheba, and plants a tamarisk tree there.

God tests Abraham, telling him to offer Isaac in the land of Moriah. On the third day he builds the altar and binds his son, but the angel of the LORD stops him, and he offers a ram caught in a thicket. He names the place for the LORD's provision.

events.title: The Death of Sarah and the Cave of Machpelah

meta.description: Sarah dies at a hundred twenty-seven at Kiriath-arba. Abraham, a stranger and alien among the Hittites, weighs out four hundred shekels of silver to Ephron for the field and cave of Machpelah as a burying place.

events.title: A Wife for Isaac: Rebekah at the Well

meta.description: Abraham's servant swears not to take a Canaanite wife for Isaac and goes to the city of Nahor. He asks for a sign, and Rebekah offers to water his ten camels. Laban receives him, Rebekah agrees to go, and Isaac brings her into Sarah's tent.

events.title: The Birth of Jacob and Esau

meta.description: Rebekah is barren until Isaac prays. The children struggle in her womb and she is told two nations are within her, the elder to serve the younger. Esau comes out red and hairy, Jacob gripping his heel. Isaac is sixty years old.

Abraham takes Keturah as wife and sends the sons of his concubines eastward with gifts. He dies at a hundred seventy-five, an old man and full of years, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him with Sarah at Machpelah.
Esau comes in from the field famished and sells his birthright to Jacob for bread and lentil stew. Thus Esau despised his birthright.

events.title: Isaac in Gerar and the Wells

meta.description: Famine drives Isaac to Gerar, where he calls Rebekah his sister. He sows and reaps a hundredfold and grows rich. Quarrels over wells give the names Esek and Sitnah before he digs Rehoboth, and he swears an oath with Abimelech at Beer-sheba.

Isaac, old and dim-sighted, sends Esau to hunt game. Rebekah dresses Jacob in Esau's garments with kidskins on his hands and neck. Isaac says 'The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau,' and blesses him. Esau cries out bitterly.

Fleeing Esau's anger toward Haran, Jacob dreams of a ladder set on earth reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending. He wakes astonished that the LORD was in that place without his knowing it, sets up the stone as a pillar, and names it Bethel.

Jacob rolls the stone from the well for Rachel and serves Laban seven years for her, which seem but a few days. In the evening Laban gives him Leah instead; he completes her week and serves another seven years for Rachel.
Leah bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah; Bilhah bears Dan and Naphtali; Zilpah bears Gad and Asher; Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah. Then God remembers Rachel, and she bears Joseph.

Jacob agrees to take the speckled and spotted animals as his wages. He peels white streaks in rods of poplar, almond, and plane and sets them in the watering troughs, and the stronger of the flock become his; he grows exceedingly rich.

Told by the LORD to return, Jacob leaves secretly; Rachel steals her father's household gods and hides them in a camel's saddle. Laban overtakes him in Gilead, searches in vain, and they raise a heap of stones called Galeed and Mizpah as a witness.

Hearing Esau approaches with four hundred men, Jacob divides his company and sends droves ahead as a present. Left alone at the ford of the Jabbok, he wrestles till daybreak, his hip is put out of joint, and he is renamed Israel.

Bowing seven times, Jacob approaches his brother. Esau runs to meet him, embraces him, and they weep. Jacob presses his gift on him, likening his brother's welcome to seeing the face of God, then journeys to Succoth and camps before Shechem.

events.title: Dinah and the Slaughter at Shechem

meta.description: Shechem son of Hamor seizes Dinah. Jacob's sons answer deceitfully, requiring every male be circumcised; on the third day, while they are in pain, Simeon and Levi kill all the males and plunder the city. Jacob fears he has been made odious in the land.
Jacob buries the foreign gods under the oak near Shechem and goes up to Bethel to build an altar. God appears again, confirms the name Israel, and renews the promise of land and descendants.

events.title: The Birth of Benjamin and the Death of Rachel

meta.description: On the way from Bethel, Rachel has hard labor near Ephrath. As her soul departs she names the child Ben-oni, but his father calls him Benjamin. She is buried on the way to Ephrath, and Jacob sets a pillar at her grave.

Joseph, seventeen years old and wearing the long robe with sleeves his father made him, dreams of sheaves bowing to his sheaf and of the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him. His brothers hate him and his father keeps the matter in mind.

Sent to his brothers at Dothan, Joseph is stripped of his robe and thrown into a dry pit. At Judah's suggestion he is sold for twenty pieces of silver to traders bound for Egypt. His robe is dipped in goat's blood, and Jacob mourns, refusing comfort.

Judah's sons Er and Onan die, and he withholds Shelah from Tamar. Veiled at the entrance to Enaim, she takes Judah's signet, cord, and staff as pledge. Told she is pregnant, he orders her burned until she produces them, then acknowledges that she has been more in the right than he.

The LORD is with Joseph and he is made overseer of Potiphar's house. His master's wife propositions him day after day and at last seizes his garment; he flees, leaving it in her hand, and is accused and imprisoned, where the chief jailer again puts everything in his care.

events.title: The Dreams of the Cupbearer and the Baker

meta.description: Imprisoned with Joseph, Pharaoh's chief cupbearer and chief baker each dream. Joseph interprets the three branches and three baskets as three days: the cupbearer is restored and the baker hanged. Yet the cupbearer forgets him.
Jacob comes to his father at Mamre. Isaac dies at a hundred eighty years, old and full of days, and his sons Esau and Jacob bury him.

events.title: The Descendants of Esau in Edom

meta.description: Esau moves to the hill country of Seir because their possessions are too great for them to live together. His clans and the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites are recorded.

After two whole years Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows devoured by seven lean ones, and seven full ears swallowed by seven blighted ears. Brought from the dungeon, Joseph declares seven years of plenty followed by seven of famine, and urges storing a fifth.

Pharaoh gives Joseph his signet ring, fine linen, and a gold chain, names him Zaphenath-paneah, and gives him Asenath as wife. Thirty years old, he stores grain like the sand of the sea, and his sons Manasseh and Ephraim are born before the famine.

events.title: The Brothers' First Journey to Egypt

meta.description: Ten brothers come to buy grain and bow before Joseph, who recognizes them but speaks harshly, charging them as spies. He keeps Simeon bound, demands Benjamin, and secretly returns their money in their sacks, dismaying them.

Judah offers himself as surety and Jacob sends Benjamin with a present of balm, honey, gum, resin, pistachio nuts, and almonds. Joseph, overcome at the sight of his brother, weeps in a private room, then seats them in order of birth and gives Benjamin five portions.

events.title: The Silver Cup and Judah's Plea

meta.description: Joseph hides his silver cup in Benjamin's sack. When it is found the brothers tear their clothes and return. Judah offers to remain as a slave in the boy's place rather than see his father's gray hairs brought down to Sheol in sorrow.

Unable to control himself, Joseph sends everyone out and weeps so loudly the Egyptians hear. He tells his brothers who he is — the one they sold into Egypt — and insists it was God who sent him ahead to preserve life. Pharaoh invites the family to the best of the land.

At Beer-sheba God tells Jacob not to fear going down to Egypt. Seventy persons of his house come; Joseph meets him in Goshen and weeps on his neck. Jacob, a hundred thirty years old, blesses Pharaoh and the family settles in the land of Rameses.

As the famine deepens Joseph collects all the money, then the livestock, then the land itself for Pharaoh, and makes the people servants, giving them seed and setting a statute that a fifth of the harvest goes to Pharaoh. Only the priests' land is not bought.

Jacob makes Joseph swear not to bury him in Egypt. Claiming Ephraim and Manasseh as his own, he crosses his hands to lay his right hand on the younger, refusing Joseph's correction and declaring that the younger brother will become the greater.

Jacob tells his sons what will happen in days to come: Reuben unstable as water, Simeon and Levi scattered for their violence, Judah a lion's whelp from whom the scepter shall not depart, Joseph a fruitful bough, Benjamin a ravenous wolf.

events.title: The Death and Burial of Jacob

meta.description: Charging his sons to bury him at Machpelah, Jacob draws up his feet and dies. The physicians embalm him forty days and Egypt weeps seventy. A great company goes up to Canaan, mourning seven days at the threshing floor of Atad.

Fearing Joseph now bears a grudge, the brothers fall down before him as slaves. He weeps and reassures them that though they intended harm, God intended it for good, to preserve a numerous people alive.

Joseph lives a hundred ten years and sees Ephraim's children of the third generation. He makes the Israelites swear to carry up his bones when God comes to them, and is embalmed and placed in a coffin in Egypt.
The seventy who came with Jacob die, but the Israelites are fruitful and prolific; they multiply and grow exceedingly strong, so that the land is filled with them.

events.title: A New King Who Did Not Know Joseph

meta.description: Fearing the Israelites will join his enemies in war, Pharaoh sets taskmasters over them and they build the supply cities Pithom and Rameses. The more they are oppressed the more they multiply, and the Egyptians come to dread them.

events.title: The Midwives Shiphrah and Puah Defy Pharaoh

meta.description: Ordered to kill the Hebrew boys at the birthstool, the midwives fear God and let them live, telling Pharaoh the Hebrew women give birth before they arrive. God deals well with them and gives them families.

events.title: Pharaoh Orders the Boys Thrown into the Nile

meta.description: Pharaoh commands all his people: every boy born to the Hebrews shall be thrown into the Nile, but every girl shall live.

A Levite woman hides her son three months, then places him in a papyrus basket sealed with bitumen and pitch among the reeds. Pharaoh's daughter takes pity on him, his own mother is hired to nurse him, and she names him Moses.

events.title: Moses Kills an Egyptian and Flees

meta.description: Grown up, Moses sees an Egyptian beating a Hebrew, looks this way and that, and kills him, hiding him in the sand. The next day two Hebrews reveal the deed is known; Pharaoh seeks to kill him and Moses flees.

events.title: Moses in Midian and the Birth of Gershom

meta.description: Sitting by a well in Midian, Moses defends the seven daughters of the priest against shepherds and waters their flock. He stays with Reuel, marries Zipporah, and names his son Gershom to mark his life as an alien in a foreign land.

After a long time the king of Egypt dies. The Israelites groan under their slavery and cry out; God hears their groaning, remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and takes notice of them.

Keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush blazing yet not consumed. Told to remove his sandals on holy ground, he is sent to Pharaoh to bring Israel out to a land flowing with milk and honey.

Asked what name to give the Israelites, God answers with the name I AM — the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses is told Pharaoh will not let them go unless compelled by a mighty hand, and that Israel will plunder the Egyptians.

The staff becomes a snake, Moses' hand turns leprous and is restored, and Nile water will become blood. Pleading that he is slow of speech, Moses asks God to send someone else; the LORD's anger is kindled and Aaron is appointed his mouth.

This month becomes the first month of the year. On the tenth day each household takes a year-old lamb without blemish, keeping it until the fourteenth, when it is slaughtered at twilight. Blood on the lintel and doorposts marks the houses the LORD will pass over.

At midnight the LORD strikes down all the firstborn of Egypt, and there is not a house without someone dead. Pharaoh summons Moses and Aaron in the night and drives them out. The people take their dough unleavened and plunder the Egyptians of silver, gold, and clothing.

About six hundred thousand men on foot besides children journey from Rameses to Succoth, with a mixed crowd and great herds. The text records that Israel had lived in Egypt four hundred thirty years, and that on that very day all the companies of the LORD went out.

Jethro sends Moses in peace. On the way the LORD meets him and seeks to kill him until Zipporah circumcises their son and calls him a bridegroom of blood. Aaron meets him at the mountain of God, and the people believe and bow down and worship.

events.title: Consecration of the Firstborn and Unleavened Bread

meta.description: All that first opens the womb is consecrated to the LORD, every firstborn donkey redeemed with a sheep. Seven days of unleavened bread are to be kept in the month of Abib as a sign on the hand and an emblem on the forehead.

events.title: The Pillar of Cloud and Fire

meta.description: God leads them by the roundabout way of the wilderness rather than the land of the Philistines, lest they face war and return. Moses takes the bones of Joseph. The LORD goes before them in a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

Pharaoh pursues with six hundred picked chariots and overtakes them at Pi-hahiroth. Moses stretches out his hand; a strong east wind divides the sea and Israel walks through on dry ground. At dawn the waters return and cover the entire army; not one remains.

Moses and the Israelites sing of the LORD's glorious triumph, of horse and rider thrown into the sea. Miriam the prophet takes a tambourine in her hand, and all the women go out after her with tambourines and dancing.

events.title: Bitter Water at Marah and the Springs of Elim

meta.description: Three days in the wilderness of Shur without water, they cannot drink at Marah because it is bitter. The LORD shows Moses a piece of wood that sweetens it. They come to Elim, with twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

events.title: The First Audience with Pharaoh Fails

meta.description: Pharaoh dismisses the LORD as a god he does not know and refuses, ordering that straw no longer be given while the quota of bricks stands. The Israelite supervisors are beaten and blame Moses and Aaron for putting a sword in Pharaoh's hand.

events.title: Water from the Rock at Massah and Meribah

meta.description: At Rephidim there is no water and the people are almost ready to stone Moses. Told to strike the rock at Horeb with the staff that struck the Nile, he does so and water comes out. He names the place Massah and Meribah for their quarrelling and their testing of whether the LORD was among them.

events.title: Manna and Quails in the Wilderness of Sin

meta.description: On the fifteenth day of the second month the people complain of the fleshpots of Egypt. Quails cover the camp at evening; in the morning a fine flaky substance appears that no one can identify, and their puzzled question at the sight gives manna its name. Twice as much falls on the sixth day, and none on the sabbath.

Joshua fights Amalek at Rephidim while Moses holds up the staff of God on the hilltop. Whenever his hands drop Amalek prevails, so Aaron and Hur hold them steady until sunset. Moses builds an altar and names it for the LORD as his banner.

events.title: God Renews His Promise of Deliverance

meta.description: The LORD promises to redeem Israel with an outstretched arm and mighty acts of judgment, but they will not listen because of their broken spirit and cruel slavery. Moses is eighty years old and Aaron eighty-three when they speak to Pharaoh.

events.title: Jethro's Visit and the Appointment of Judges

meta.description: Jethro brings Zipporah and her two sons and rejoices at all the LORD has done. Seeing Moses judge alone from morning to evening, he warns that what he is doing is not good and counsels appointing able men as officers over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.

On the third new moon after leaving Egypt they camp before the mountain. If they obey his voice they shall be a priestly kingdom and a holy nation; the people answer as one that they will do everything the LORD has spoken. They consecrate themselves for the third day.

events.title: The LORD Descends on Mount Sinai

meta.description: On the morning of the third day there is thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, and a trumpet blast so loud the people tremble. Sinai is wrapped in smoke like a kiln and the whole mountain shakes violently as the LORD descends in fire.

God speaks all these words: no other gods, no idol, no wrongful use of the name, remember the sabbath, honor father and mother, and the prohibitions of murder, adultery, theft, false witness, and coveting.

events.title: Aaron's Staff Swallows the Magicians' Staffs

meta.description: Aaron throws down his staff before Pharaoh and it becomes a snake. The magicians of Egypt do the same by their secret arts, but Aaron's staff swallows up theirs; still Pharaoh's heart is hardened.

events.title: The People Ask Moses to Mediate

meta.description: Witnessing the thunder, trumpet, and smoking mountain, the people stand at a distance and beg Moses to speak instead of God, lest they die. Moses draws near to the thick darkness where God was.

The ordinances set before Israel: the rights of Hebrew slaves, laws of homicide and bodily injury, restitution for theft and damage, protection of the alien, widow, and orphan, the sabbatical year, the three annual festivals, and the promise of an angel to guard the way.

Moses builds an altar with twelve pillars and dashes half the blood against it. Reading the book of the covenant, he dashes the rest on the people as the blood of the covenant the LORD has made with them. Then seventy elders go up, see the God of Israel on a pavement of sapphire, and eat and drink.

events.title: Moses Forty Days on the Mountain

meta.description: Summoned to receive the tablets of stone, Moses goes up with Joshua. The cloud covers the mountain six days, and on the seventh the LORD calls to him out of it. The glory appears like a devouring fire, and Moses is on the mountain forty days and forty nights.

events.title: First Plague: Water Turned to Blood

meta.description: Moses strikes the Nile in the sight of Pharaoh and all its water turns to blood. The fish die, the river stinks, and the Egyptians dig along the Nile for water. Seven days pass after the LORD strikes the river.

events.title: Instructions for the Ark, Table, and Lampstand

meta.description: An offering is to be taken from all whose hearts prompt them. The ark of acacia wood is overlaid with gold with a mercy seat and two cherubim, along with the table for the bread of the Presence and the lampstand of hammered gold.

events.title: Instructions for the Tabernacle and Its Curtains

meta.description: Ten curtains of fine twisted linen with blue, purple, and crimson yarns, coverings of goats' hair and tanned rams' skins, frames of acacia wood, and the veil separating the holy place from the holy of holies.

events.title: Instructions for the Altar and the Court

meta.description: The bronze altar of burnt offering with horns at its corners, the hangings of the court, and the command that pure beaten olive oil be brought so a lamp may burn regularly from evening to morning.

Aaron and his sons are set apart as priests. The ephod, the breastpiece of judgment with twelve engraved stones and the Urim and Thummim, the robe with pomegranates and bells, and the rosette engraved as holy to the LORD are described.

events.title: Instructions for the Ordination of Priests

meta.description: The seven-day rite of ordination: the bull of sin offering, the two rams, the blood placed on ear, thumb, and toe, and the daily offering of two lambs, so that the LORD may dwell among the Israelites and be their God.

Frogs come up and cover the land, entering palace, bedchamber, ovens, and kneading bowls. Pharaoh asks Moses to pray and names the next day; the frogs die and are gathered in heaps until the land stinks, but seeing a respite Pharaoh hardens his heart.

events.title: The Incense Altar, the Basin, and the Anointing Oil

meta.description: The altar of incense, the census half-shekel as atonement money, the bronze basin for washing, and the holy anointing oil and fragrant incense, neither of which may be reproduced for ordinary use.

The LORD fills Bezalel of Judah with divine spirit, skill, and knowledge in every craft, and appoints Oholiab of Dan with him. The sabbath is given as a perpetual sign, and Moses receives the two tablets written with the finger of God.

Seeing Moses delay, the people gather around Aaron, who collects their gold rings and casts an image of a calf, which they hail as the gods that brought them up out of Egypt. They rise early to offer sacrifices, then sit down to eat and drink and rise up to revel.
Aaron strikes the dust of the earth and it becomes gnats on humans and animals throughout Egypt. The magicians try and fail, and tell Pharaoh that the finger of God is at work.

events.title: Moses Intercedes and Breaks the Tablets

meta.description: Moses implores the LORD to remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and the LORD changes his mind about the disaster. Coming down and seeing the calf and the dancing, Moses breaks the tablets, burns the calf, grinds it to powder, and makes the people drink it. Three thousand fall by the Levites' swords.

events.title: Moses Asks to See God's Glory

meta.description: Moses pitches the tent of meeting outside the camp, where the LORD speaks with him face to face as one speaks to a friend. Promised that the divine presence will go with him, Moses asks to see God's glory and is placed in a cleft of the rock to see only his back.

events.title: The Covenant Renewed and the Second Tablets

meta.description: Moses cuts two new tablets and goes up. The LORD passes before him proclaiming himself merciful and gracious, slow to anger. Moses is again on the mountain forty days without bread or water, and comes down with his face shining, so that he veils it.
Great swarms of flies ruin the land, but the LORD sets apart Goshen where his people live. Pharaoh offers to let them sacrifice within the land, then not far away, then deals falsely once more.

events.title: The Freewill Offering for the Tabernacle

meta.description: All whose hearts are stirred bring gold, yarn, linen, skins, and acacia wood, and skilled women spin. They bring so much more than enough that Moses must issue a command restraining the people from bringing anything further.

events.title: Fifth Plague: Death of the Livestock

meta.description: The LORD sets a time, and the next day all the livestock of the Egyptians die while not one of Israel's dies. Pharaoh inquires and finds it so, but his heart is hardened.

events.title: The Tabernacle and Its Furnishings Are Made

meta.description: Bezalel and the skilled workers make the curtains and frames, the ark and mercy seat, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the basin from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance, and the court, with an accounting of all the metal used.
Moses throws handfuls of soot from the kiln into the air, and it becomes fine dust causing festering boils on humans and animals. The magicians cannot even stand before Moses because of the boils.

The heaviest hail ever to fall in Egypt strikes with fire flashing in its midst, shattering every tree, though not in Goshen. Pharaoh admits that this time he has sinned, but hardens his heart when the thunder ceases. Flax and barley are ruined; wheat and spelt survive.

Pharaoh's officials demand to know how long this will go on, warning that Egypt is already ruined. An east wind brings locusts that blacken the land and eat all the hail has left. A strong west wind drives them into the Red Sea, but Pharaoh will not let Israel go.

events.title: Ninth Plague: Darkness That Can Be Felt

meta.description: Dense darkness covers Egypt three days; no one can see another or move, but the Israelites have light. Pharaoh tells Moses that on the day he sees his face again he will die, and Moses answers that he will not see it.

About midnight every firstborn in Egypt shall die, from Pharaoh's to the slave's behind the handmill, and there will be a loud cry such as has never been. But not a dog shall growl at any of the Israelites. In hot anger Moses leaves Pharaoh.

On the first day of the first month in the second year the tabernacle is set up. Moses places the ark behind the veil, sets out the bread, lights the lamps, and anoints everything, and the court is raised around it.

events.title: The Glory of the LORD Fills the Tabernacle

meta.description: The cloud covers the tent of meeting and the glory of the LORD fills the tabernacle, so that Moses cannot enter. Whenever the cloud lifts Israel sets out; if it does not lift they remain, for the cloud was on it by day and fire by night in the sight of all Israel.

events.title: The Ordination of Aaron and His Sons

meta.description: Moses assembles the congregation, washes and vests Aaron, anoints the tabernacle and the altar, and offers the bull and the two rams. Aaron and his sons remain at the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days.

events.title: Offerings of the Twelve Tribal Leaders

meta.description: On the day Moses finishes setting up the tabernacle, the leaders of the twelve tribes bring wagons and oxen, and present identical dedication offerings for the altar, one leader on each of twelve days.

events.title: The Vestments Completed and the Work Inspected

meta.description: The ephod, breastpiece, robe, and the rosette of pure gold are finished as the LORD commanded Moses. All the work is brought to Moses, who sees that they have done it just as commanded, and he blesses them.
On the eighth day Aaron draws near to the altar and sacrifices the sin offering, burnt offering, grain offering, and offering of well-being for himself and for the people.

events.title: Fire from the LORD Consumes the Offering

meta.description: Aaron blesses the people, the glory of the LORD appears to all of them, and fire comes out from the LORD and consumes the burnt offering; the people shout and fall on their faces.

events.title: The Death of Nadab and Abihu

meta.description: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu offer unholy fire that the LORD had not commanded; fire comes out from the presence of the LORD and consumes them. Aaron is silent, and is forbidden to mourn.
Priests are forbidden strong drink in the tent of meeting and charged to distinguish holy from common. Moses is angry that the sin offering was burned, but accepts Aaron's answer.

events.title: The Passover Kept in the Wilderness of Sinai

meta.description: Israel keeps the passover in the first month of the second year after leaving Egypt. For those unclean or on a journey, a second passover is appointed in the second month on the fourteenth day.

events.title: The Law of the Burnt Offering

meta.description: The LORD calls to Moses from the tent of meeting and gives the prescriptions for the burnt offering from the herd, the flock, and birds.

events.title: The Lampstand and the Dedication of the Levites

meta.description: Aaron sets up the seven lamps to give light in front of the lampstand, and the Levites are cleansed, presented as an elevation offering, and given to Aaron in place of the firstborn of Israel.

events.title: The Law of the Grain Offering

meta.description: Regulations for the grain offering of choice flour with oil and frankincense, unleavened and salted with the salt of the covenant.
On the first day of the second month of the second year, the LORD commands a census of all Israelite men twenty years and older able to go to war; the total is 603,550.

events.title: The Levites Set Apart for the Tabernacle

meta.description: The Levites are not enrolled with the other tribes but appointed over the tabernacle of the covenant, to carry it, care for it, and camp around it.
The tribes are assigned positions around the tent of meeting by standard and ancestral house — Judah east, Reuben south, Ephraim west, Dan north — and the order of march is set.
The Levites are counted from a month old and upward and taken by the LORD in place of the firstborn of Israel, with the surplus firstborn redeemed at five shekels each.

events.title: The Law of the Offering of Well-Being

meta.description: Regulations for the sacrifice of well-being from herd or flock, with a perpetual statute that Israel eat neither fat nor blood.

events.title: The Duties of the Levitical Clans

meta.description: The Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites are counted from thirty to fifty years old and assigned their loads for carrying the sanctuary and its furnishings.

events.title: Purity of the Camp and Restitution

meta.description: The unclean are put outside the camp, and those who wrong a neighbor must confess and make full restitution with a fifth added.

events.title: The Ordeal for a Suspected Wife

meta.description: The ritual of the water of bitterness, by which a husband's suspicion of his wife is brought before the priest for decision.
Those who separate themselves to the LORD abstain from wine, leave the hair uncut, and avoid contact with the dead, with offerings prescribed for completing or interrupting the vow.
On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year the cloud lifts from the tabernacle and Israel sets out from the wilderness of Sinai toward the wilderness of Paran, tribe by tribe.

events.title: The Law of the Sin Offering

meta.description: Graded sin offerings for unintentional sin by the anointed priest, the whole congregation, a ruler, or an ordinary person.
Aaron and his sons are given the words with which to bless Israel, invoking the LORD's blessing and keeping, the shining of his face, and the gift of peace.
A cloud covers the tabernacle by day and the appearance of fire by night; Israel sets out or remains in camp only as the cloud lifts or settles.
Moses makes two trumpets of hammered silver for summoning the congregation, breaking camp, sounding the alarm in war, and marking festivals.

events.title: The Law of the Guilt Offering

meta.description: Offerings graded by means for those who withhold testimony, touch what is unclean, or defraud a neighbor, with restitution plus a fifth.
The priests' handling of each offering: the perpetual fire on the altar, the priestly portions, and the prohibition of fat and blood.
The dietary laws distinguishing clean from unclean land animals, water creatures, birds, and swarming things, and the impurity conveyed by carcasses.
The period of a mother's impurity and the offerings she brings at its completion, with a lesser offering permitted to those who cannot afford a lamb.
The priest's examination and quarantine of surface afflictions in skin, hair, garments, and leather, and the pronouncement of clean or unclean.
The ritual of the two birds, cedar, crimson yarn, and hyssop for one healed of a skin disease, and the procedure for an infected house.
Impurity arising from male and female discharges, the washing required, and the offerings that restore cleanness.

After the death of Aaron's sons, the LORD sets the one day each year when the high priest enters the holy of holies, and appoints the two goats — one for the LORD, one sent into the wilderness for Azazel.

events.title: Slaughter at the Sanctuary and the Blood Prohibition

meta.description: All sacrifice is centralized at the tent of meeting, and eating blood is forbidden, for the life of the flesh is in the blood.
Israel is forbidden the practices of Egypt and Canaan, with a catalogue of forbidden degrees of kinship, lest the land vomit them out.
Laws on reverence for parents, gleaning for the poor, honest weights, impartial justice, and the command to love your neighbor as yourself.
Capital and other penalties for child sacrifice to Molech, consulting mediums, cursing parents, and the forbidden sexual unions.
Rules for priestly mourning, marriage, and bodily wholeness, and the requirement that offerings be without blemish.
The appointed festivals: sabbath, Passover and unleavened bread, first fruits, weeks, trumpets, the day of atonement, and booths.

events.title: The Lamp and the Bread of the Presence

meta.description: Pure oil is brought for the lamp that burns regularly, and twelve loaves are set in two rows on the table of pure gold every sabbath.
The son of an Israelite woman and an Egyptian father blasphemes the Name during a fight and is held in custody; at the LORD's word he is taken outside the camp and stoned.
Every seventh year the land rests, and every fiftieth year liberty is proclaimed: property returns to its family and Israelite slaves go free.

events.title: Blessings and Curses of the Covenant

meta.description: Rain, harvest, and peace are promised for obedience; disease, defeat, famine, and exile among the nations are threatened for disobedience, with a promise to remember the covenant.
Valuations for persons, animals, houses, and fields dedicated to the LORD, the redemption price of a fifth added, and the tithe of the land as holy to the LORD.
The people complain in the hearing of the LORD, fire burns among them and consumes the outskirts of the camp, and the place is named Taberah.

events.title: Craving for Meat and the Complaint of Moses

meta.description: The rabble crave meat and remember the fish of Egypt, weary of the manna; Moses protests to the LORD that he cannot carry this people alone.

events.title: The Seventy Elders Receive the Spirit

meta.description: The LORD takes some of the spirit on Moses and puts it on seventy elders, who prophesy. Eldad and Medad prophesy in the camp, and Moses wishes that all the LORD's people were prophets.

events.title: The Quail and the Plague at Kibroth-hattaavah

meta.description: A wind brings quail from the sea in vast quantity; while the meat is still between their teeth the LORD strikes the people with a great plague, and the place is called Kibroth-hattaavah, the graves of craving.

events.title: Miriam and Aaron Speak Against Moses

meta.description: Miriam and Aaron object to Moses' Cushite wife and to his unique standing. The LORD vindicates Moses; Miriam becomes leprous and is shut outside the camp for seven days at Hazeroth.

One leader from each tribe is sent from the wilderness of Paran to scout Canaan. They go up through the Negeb to Hebron and cut a branch with a single cluster of grapes at the Wadi Eshcol, returning after forty days.
The scouts report a land flowing with milk and honey but fortified cities and the descendants of Anak. Caleb urges going up at once, while the others spread a bad report of the land.

events.title: The People Refuse to Enter the Land

meta.description: The congregation weeps and demands a captain to return to Egypt. Joshua and Caleb tear their clothes and plead with the people, who threaten to stone them.

events.title: Forty Years in the Wilderness Decreed

meta.description: Moses intercedes and the LORD pardons, but decrees that no one counted in the census over twenty years old will enter the land except Caleb and Joshua; Israel will wander forty years, a year for each day the scouts spent in the land.
Presuming to go up without Moses or the ark, the people are beaten down by the Amalekites and Canaanites as far as Hormah.

events.title: Laws of Offerings in the Land

meta.description: Grain and drink offerings to accompany sacrifices when Israel enters the land, provision for unintentional sin by the congregation or an individual, and the penalty for sinning high-handedly.
A man found gathering sticks on the sabbath is held in custody until the LORD's decision, then stoned outside the camp.
Israel is commanded to make fringes with a blue cord on the corners of their garments, to look at and remember all the commandments of the LORD.

events.title: The Rebellion of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram

meta.description: Korah with 250 leaders challenges the authority of Moses and Aaron. The earth opens and swallows Dathan and Abiram with their households, and fire consumes the 250 men offering incense.

events.title: The Plague Stopped by Aaron's Censer

meta.description: The censers of the dead are hammered into a covering for the altar. When the congregation blames Moses and a plague breaks out, Aaron runs among the people with incense and stands between the dead and the living.
A rod for each ancestral house is placed in the tent of meeting; Aaron's rod for the house of Levi sprouts, buds, blossoms, and bears almonds, confirming his priesthood.

events.title: The Dues of Priests and Levites

meta.description: Aaron's house bears responsibility for the sanctuary. The priests receive the offerings, the Levites receive the tithe as their inheritance in place of land, and the Levites tithe in turn.

events.title: The Red Heifer and Corpse Impurity

meta.description: A red heifer without defect is burned outside the camp and its ashes kept for the water for cleansing, which purifies anyone who has touched a corpse.

events.title: The Death of Miriam at Kadesh

meta.description: In the first month the congregation comes into the wilderness of Zin and stays at Kadesh, where Miriam dies and is buried.

events.title: The Death of Aaron on Mount Hor

meta.description: At Mount Hor, Aaron's vestments are stripped from him and put on his son Eleazar. Aaron dies on the mountain top, and Israel mourns him thirty days.

events.title: Moses Strikes the Rock at Meribah

meta.description: With no water, the people quarrel with Moses. Told to command the rock, Moses strikes it twice; water comes out, but the LORD tells Moses and Aaron they will not bring the assembly into the land.
Moses sends messengers to the king of Edom asking to pass along the King's Highway. Edom comes out with a heavy force, and Israel turns away.
The priests carrying the ark step into the Jordan at flood stage; the waters coming down stand in a heap far off at Adam, and all Israel crosses over on dry ground opposite Jericho.
One man from each tribe carries a stone from the riverbed, and Joshua sets them up at Gilgal as a memorial, so that when children ask in time to come what the stones mean, the crossing will be told.

events.title: Victory Over the King of Arad

meta.description: The Canaanite king of Arad takes some Israelites captive. Israel vows to devote their towns to destruction, the LORD gives them victory, and the place is named Hormah.

events.title: Circumcision at Gilgal and the Passover

meta.description: The generation born in the wilderness is circumcised at Gibeath-haaraloth. Israel keeps the passover on the fourteenth day on the plains of Jericho, and the manna ceases the day after they eat the produce of the land.
After the death of Moses the LORD tells Joshua to cross the Jordan, promising every place the sole of his foot treads, and charging him three times to be strong and courageous.
Joshua commands the officers to ready provisions for crossing in three days, and reminds Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh to cross over armed ahead of their kindred.
The people speak against God and Moses on the way around Edom; poisonous serpents bite them, and Moses makes a serpent of bronze on a pole so that those who look at it live.

events.title: The Spies and Rahab at Jericho

meta.description: Two spies sent from Shittim lodge with Rahab, who hides them under stalks of flax on her roof and lets them down by a rope, asking to be spared for the crimson cord in her window.

events.title: The Commander of the Army of the LORD

meta.description: Near Jericho Joshua sees a man with a drawn sword who declares himself commander of the army of the LORD, and tells Joshua to remove his sandals, for the place is holy.

events.title: Through Moab and the Song of the Well

meta.description: Israel journeys by Oboth, Iye-abarim, and the Wadi Zered to the wilderness east of Moab, singing at Beer the song of the well that the leaders dug.

events.title: The Defeat of Sihon King of the Amorites

meta.description: Sihon refuses passage and attacks Israel at Jahaz. Israel defeats him and takes possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, settling in Heshbon and its villages.

events.title: The Defeat of Og King of Bashan

meta.description: Israel turns north toward Bashan; Og comes out against them at Edrei and is struck down with his sons and all his people, and Israel takes possession of his land.

Camped on the plains of Moab across the Jordan from Jericho, Israel alarms Balak son of Zippor, who sends elders of Moab and Midian with fees for divination to bring Balaam son of Beor to curse Israel.
As Balaam rides to Moab, his donkey sees the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword and turns aside three times. The LORD opens the donkey's mouth, and then Balaam's eyes.
At Bamoth-baal and the field of Zophim, seven altars are built and bulls and rams offered. Twice Balaam blesses Israel instead of cursing them, to Balak's fury.
The spirit of God comes upon Balaam and he blesses Israel a third time, praising the beauty of their tents and encampments, then prophesies a star coming out of Jacob before returning home.

events.title: Apostasy at Baal-Peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

meta.description: Israel joins itself to the Baal of Peor through the women of Moab. A plague kills twenty-four thousand and is stopped when Phinehas son of Eleazar spears an Israelite man and a Midianite woman.

events.title: The Second Census on the Plains of Moab

meta.description: After the plague, a new census counts 601,730 men of war. Not one remains of those counted at Sinai except Caleb and Joshua, and the land is to be apportioned by lot according to these numbers.
Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah ask for their father's inheritance since he left no son. The LORD grants their request and establishes it as a statute of judgment for Israel.
Moses is told to view the land from the mountains of Abarim, since he will not enter it. He lays his hands on Joshua son of Nun before Eleazar and the congregation, giving him some of his authority.
The daily, sabbath, new moon, and festival offerings are set out in full for passover, weeks, trumpets, the day of atonement, and the seven days of booths.
A man who makes a vow must keep it; the vows of a daughter or wife stand unless annulled by her father or husband on the day he hears of it.
A thousand from each tribe go out against Midian and kill its five kings and Balaam son of Beor. The spoil is divided between the warriors and the congregation, with a levy for the LORD.

events.title: Reuben, Gad, and Half of Manasseh Settle in Transjordan

meta.description: Seeing good grazing land at Jazer and Gilead, Reuben and Gad ask to settle east of the Jordan. Moses agrees on condition that their fighting men cross over armed until Israel takes possession of Canaan.

events.title: The Record of the Wilderness Journey

meta.description: Moses writes down the stages of the journey from Rameses, set out on the fifteenth day of the first month, through forty-two encampments to the plains of Moab by the Jordan.

events.title: The Boundaries of Canaan and the Tribal Leaders

meta.description: Israel is commanded to drive out the inhabitants and destroy their idols. The borders of the land are drawn, and Eleazar, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe are named to apportion it.

events.title: Levitical Cities and Cities of Refuge

meta.description: Forty-eight towns with pasture lands are assigned to the Levites, six of them cities of refuge where one who kills without intent may flee from the avenger of blood until the death of the high priest.
So that no inheritance passes from tribe to tribe, heiresses must marry within their father's tribe; Zelophehad's daughters marry sons of their father's brothers in Manasseh.

For six days Israel marches once around the shut-up city with seven priests blowing rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day they march seven times, the people shout, and the wall falls flat. Only Rahab's household is spared.

events.title: Achan's Sin and the First Defeat at Ai

meta.description: Israel is routed at Ai because Achan took devoted things from Jericho. Chosen by lot, he confesses to a mantle from Shinar, silver, and a bar of gold hidden in his tent, and is stoned in the Valley of Achor.
Joshua sets an ambush behind the city, draws its defenders out by feigning flight, and takes Ai; its king is hanged on a tree until evening and buried under a heap of stones at the gate.

events.title: Moses Begins to Expound the Law

meta.description: In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, in the land of Moab beyond the Jordan, Moses begins to expound this law to all Israel.
Moses recalls the command to leave Horeb and take the land, and the appointment of wise leaders as commanders and judges over thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens.
Moses recounts the sending of the scouts, the people's refusal to go up, the LORD's oath that none of that generation would see the land, and their defeat by the Amorites at Hormah.

events.title: Recalling the Route Around Edom, Moab, and Ammon

meta.description: Moses recalls the thirty-eight years until the warrior generation had died, and the command not to harass Esau, Moab, or Ammon, whose lands were given to them as possessions.

events.title: Recalling the Defeat of Sihon and Og

meta.description: Moses recounts the victories over Sihon of Heshbon and Og of Bashan, the last of the Rephaim, whose iron bedstead was nine cubits long.

events.title: The Transjordan Allotment and Joshua's Charge

meta.description: The conquered land is given to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh; Joshua is charged not to fear; and Moses' plea to cross over and see the good land is refused.
Moses warns against adding to or taking from the commandments, against making any idol since Israel saw no form at Horeb, and promises that the LORD is merciful to those who return to him.

events.title: Cities of Refuge East of the Jordan

meta.description: Moses sets apart Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan east of the Jordan as places of refuge for one who kills a neighbor unintentionally.

events.title: The Altar on Mount Ebal and the Reading of the Law

meta.description: Joshua builds an altar of unhewn stones on Mount Ebal, writes a copy of the law of Moses on the stones, and reads all the blessings and curses before the whole assembly, including women, children, and the aliens among them.
Moses declares that the covenant at Horeb was made not with the ancestors but with the living generation, and repeats the ten commandments spoken from the fire.

events.title: The Shema and the Great Commandment

meta.description: Israel is called to hear that the LORD their God is one, and to love him with all their heart, soul, and might, teaching these words to their children at home and on the way.

events.title: The Command to Destroy the Nations of Canaan

meta.description: Israel must make no covenant or marriage with the seven nations and must tear down their altars, being a people holy to the LORD, chosen not for their numbers but because he loved them.
The forty years of manna taught that one does not live by bread alone. In a good land Israel must not credit its wealth to its own power and forget the LORD.

events.title: Recalling the Golden Calf and Moses' Intercession

meta.description: Israel is warned that it is not their righteousness that wins the land. Moses recalls breaking the tablets over the calf, lying prostrate forty days, and the second tablets placed in the ark.
To fear the LORD, walk in his ways, and love him; to circumcise the heart and love the stranger. Blessing and curse are set before Israel on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal.
The Canaanite places of worship are to be destroyed and sacrifice brought only to the place the LORD chooses. Meat may be slaughtered locally for food, but the blood must be poured out on the ground.

events.title: Laws Against Enticement to Other Gods

meta.description: A prophet, a family member, or a whole town that entices Israel to serve other gods must not be spared, even if the prophet's sign comes true.
The permitted and forbidden animals, birds, and fish, and the yearly tithe eaten before the LORD, with the third-year tithe stored in the towns for Levites, aliens, orphans, and widows.

events.title: The Year of Remission and Release of Slaves

meta.description: Every seventh year debts are remitted and Hebrew slaves are set free, not empty-handed but provided liberally from flock, threshing floor, and wine press.
Passover, the festival of weeks, and the festival of booths are to be kept at the place the LORD chooses, and no one shall appear before the LORD empty-handed.

The Gibeonites come with worn sacks, patched sandals, and dry crumbling bread, claiming to be from a far country. Israel makes a treaty without asking direction from the LORD, and afterward makes them hewers of wood and drawers of water.

events.title: Judges, Courts, and the Law of the King

meta.description: Judges are appointed in every town and justice pursued without bribes. A king, if appointed, must be chosen by the LORD, must not multiply horses, wives, or silver, and must write and read a copy of the law.

events.title: The Levitical Priests and the Prophet Like Moses

meta.description: The priests' portion is set, divination and sorcery are forbidden, and the LORD promises to raise up a prophet like Moses; a prophet whose word does not come true has spoken presumptuously.

events.title: Cities of Refuge, Boundaries, and Witnesses

meta.description: Three cities of refuge are set apart, boundary markers must not be moved, and a charge stands only on the evidence of two or three witnesses, with a malicious witness receiving the penalty he intended.
Exemptions are granted to those with a new house, vineyard, or bride, and to the fainthearted. Distant towns are offered terms first, and fruit trees must not be cut down in a siege.

events.title: Laws on Homicide, Family, and Property

meta.description: Atonement for an unsolved murder, the rights of a captive wife and of a firstborn son, the rebellious son, the return of lost property, and the requirement of a parapet on a new roof.

events.title: Admission to the Assembly and Camp Purity

meta.description: Who may be admitted to the assembly of the LORD, the holiness of the war camp, the harboring of an escaped slave, the ban on cult prostitution and on interest charged to fellow Israelites.
Divorce, the pledge taken from a poor man, prompt payment of wages, gleanings left for the alien and widow, limits on flogging, levirate marriage, honest weights, and the command to blot out Amalek.

The worshiper brings the first of the ground in a basket and recites the creed that traces Israel's descent from a wandering Aramean ancestor, declaring the tithe given to Levite, alien, orphan, and widow.

events.title: The Ceremony Commanded at Ebal and Gerizim

meta.description: Israel is to set up large plastered stones with the law written on them, build an altar of unhewn stones on Mount Ebal, and pronounce twelve curses to each of which the whole people assent
Blessings in city and field for obedience, and an extended catalogue of curses for disobedience — disease, siege, defeat, and scattering among all the peoples from one end of the earth to the other.
Moses summons all Israel to enter the covenant, made not with them alone but with those not present that day, warning against a root sprouting poisonous and bitter growth.

events.title: The Amorite Coalition Defeated at Gibeon

meta.description: Five Amorite kings besiege Gibeon; Joshua marches all night from Gilgal, the LORD throws down huge hailstones, and Joshua calls on the sun to stand still over Gibeon — it stops in midheaven for about a whole day.

events.title: The Promise of Restoration and the Choice of Life

meta.description: Even after exile, if Israel returns the LORD will gather them and circumcise their hearts. The commandment is not too hard nor far off: life and death are set before them, and they are urged to choose life.

events.title: Joshua Commissioned and the Law Written Down

meta.description: Moses, a hundred and twenty years old, charges Joshua to be strong and bold, writes down the law and gives it to the priests to be read every seventh year at the festival of booths.

events.title: The Five Kings in the Cave at Makkedah

meta.description: The five kings hide in a cave at Makkedah and are shut in with large stones. After the pursuit, Joshua has them brought out, has his commanders put their feet on their necks, and hangs them on five trees until evening.
Moses recites the song calling heaven and earth to witness — the Rock whose work is perfect, Israel's desertion, and the LORD's judgment and final vindication of his people.

events.title: The Blessing of the Twelve Tribes

meta.description: Before his death Moses blesses each tribe in turn, closing with praise of Israel's incomparable God and of the everlasting arms beneath his people.

events.title: The Conquest of the Southern Cities

meta.description: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron, and Debir, defeating the whole land of the hill country, the Negeb, the lowland, and the slopes, because the LORD fought for Israel.

events.title: The Death of Moses on Mount Nebo

meta.description: Moses goes up Mount Nebo to Pisgah, sees the whole land, and dies there in Moab at a hundred and twenty, his sight unimpaired. He is buried in a valley, and no one knows his grave; Israel mourns thirty days.

events.title: The Northern Coalition Defeated at Merom

meta.description: Jabin king of Hazor gathers a great army with horses and chariots at the waters of Merom. Israel falls on them suddenly, hamstrings their horses, burns their chariots, and burns Hazor itself.

Joshua takes the whole land — hill country, Negeb, Goshen, lowland, Arabah — making war a long time with all those kings. The Anakim are cut off except in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod, and the land has rest from war.
A register of the kings defeated east of the Jordan under Moses — Sihon and Og — and the thirty-one kings west of the Jordan defeated under Joshua.

events.title: The Land Still to Be Possessed

meta.description: Joshua is now old and advanced in years, yet very much of the land remains: the regions of the Philistines and Geshurites, Lebanon, and the territory of the Sidonians.

events.title: The Inheritance East of the Jordan

meta.description: The allotments of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh east of the Jordan are recorded. To the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance: the offerings to the LORD are their inheritance.
Caleb, eighty-five years old and as strong as the day Moses sent him, claims the hill country promised him forty-five years earlier, and Joshua gives him Hebron as an inheritance.
Judah's borders and towns are recorded. Othniel takes Kiriath-sepher and wins Achsah, who asks her father for springs of water. The Jebusites remain in Jerusalem alongside Judah.

events.title: The Allotment of Ephraim and Manasseh

meta.description: The tribes of Joseph receive their territory. The daughters of Zelophehad receive an inheritance among their father's brothers, and the Josephites, complaining of a single lot, are told to clear the forested hill country.

events.title: The Assembly at Shiloh and the Survey of the Land

meta.description: The tent of meeting is set up at Shiloh. Joshua rebukes the seven tribes still without an inheritance and sends three men from each to write a description of the land in seven divisions, then casts lots for them.

events.title: The Allotments of the Seven Remaining Tribes

meta.description: Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and Dan receive their territories by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, Simeon's lying within the portion of Judah.
When the land is finished being apportioned, Israel gives Joshua the town he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, which he rebuilds and settles in.
Kedesh, Shechem, Kiriath-arba, Bezer, Ramoth, and Golan are set apart so that anyone who kills a person without intent may flee there and stand trial before the congregation.
Forty-eight towns with their pasture lands are given to the Levites out of the tribal inheritances. Not one word of all the good promises of the LORD to Israel has failed.

events.title: The Altar of the Eastern Tribes

meta.description: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh return home and build a great altar by the Jordan. Israel gathers for war until Phinehas learns the altar is a witness, not for sacrifice, and they name it as a witness between them.
Long afterward, old and advanced in years, Joshua summons the elders and judges to hold fast to the LORD, warning that if they intermarry with the remaining nations they will be a snare and a trap.

Joshua recounts Israel's history from Terah onward and calls them to choose whom they will serve, pledging that he and his household will serve the LORD. He makes a covenant and sets up a great stone under the oak.

events.title: The Death of Joshua and the Burial of Joseph's Bones

meta.description: Joshua dies at a hundred and ten and is buried at Timnath-serah. Joseph's bones, brought up from Egypt, are buried at Shechem, and Eleazar son of Aaron dies and is buried in the hill country of Ephraim.

events.title: Judah and Simeon Campaign in the South

meta.description: After Joshua's death, Judah and Simeon defeat Adoni-bezek and campaign against Jerusalem, Hebron, Debir, Zephath, and the cities of the plain. Othniel captures Debir and marries Achsah, while Benjamin fails to expel the Jebusites from Jerusalem.

events.title: The House of Joseph Takes Bethel

meta.description: The house of Joseph gains entrance to Bethel with the help of a man leaving the city. His family is spared, and he later builds another city named Luz in Hittite territory.

events.title: The Tribes Fail to Expel the Inhabitants

meta.description: Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, and Naphtali leave Canaanite populations in their territories, sometimes subjecting them to forced labor. Amorite pressure confines Dan to the hill country.

events.title: The Angel of the LORD at Bochim

meta.description: The angel of the LORD indicts Israel for making covenants with the land's inhabitants and leaving their altars intact. The people weep and sacrifice at the place consequently called Bochim.

Joshua's generation dies, and those who follow abandon the LORD for the Baals and Astartes. Israel enters a recurring pattern of apostasy, oppression, deliverance through judges, and relapse after each judge's death.
Micah returns silver stolen from his mother, and part of it becomes a cast idol for his private shrine. He first installs his son and then hires a wandering Levite from Bethlehem as his priest.
Five Danites seeking territory visit Micah's house and ask his Levite priest about their mission. They discover Laish to be prosperous, isolated, and unsuspecting, and urge their kinsmen to seize it.

events.title: The Danites Seize Micah's Idols and Priest

meta.description: Six hundred armed Danites stop at Micah's house on their migration north. They take his idol, ephod, household gods, and priest, and Micah abandons pursuit when he sees that they outnumber him.

The Danites destroy isolated Laish, rebuild it, and rename it Dan. They establish Micah's idol there, with Jonathan and his descendants serving as tribal priests while the sanctuary remains at Shiloh.

events.title: A Levite and His Concubine Lodge at Gibeah

meta.description: A Levite retrieves his concubine from Bethlehem and begins the return journey late in the day. Passing Jebus, the party chooses Israelite Gibeah for the night, where an elderly Ephraimite finally takes them in.

Men of Gibeah surround the host's house and abuse the Levite's concubine throughout the night, leaving her dead at the threshold. The Levite divides her body into twelve pieces and sends them throughout Israel as a summons to respond.
The tribes assemble at Mizpah and resolve to punish Gibeah. Benjamin refuses to surrender the offenders and musters for war against the united Israelite force.

events.title: Benjamin Wins the First Two Battles

meta.description: Israel inquires at Bethel but suffers severe losses in two assaults on Gibeah. The people weep, fast, offer sacrifices, and inquire again before the ark, where Phinehas ministers.
On the third day Israel uses an ambush to capture and burn Gibeah, then overwhelms Benjamin's army. Only six hundred men escape to the rock of Rimmon as Israel destroys Benjaminite towns.

Regretting Benjamin's impending extinction yet bound by an oath not to give it wives, the assembly attacks Jabesh-gilead for failing to attend at Mizpah. Four hundred surviving young women are given to the Benjaminites at Rimmon.

events.title: The Women of Shiloh Are Abducted

meta.description: To provide wives for the remaining Benjaminites without formally breaking their oath, Israel's elders permit them to seize women dancing at Shiloh's festival. Benjamin rebuilds its towns, and the tribes disperse to their inheritances.
Several peoples remain in the land to test and teach later Israelites. Israel lives among them, intermarries with them, and serves their gods.
After Israel serves the Baals and Asherahs, King Cushan-rishathaim of Aram-naharaim subjugates the people for eight years.
The spirit of the LORD comes upon Othniel, who defeats Cushan-rishathaim and judges Israel. The land then rests for forty years until Othniel's death.
Eglon of Moab joins with Ammon and Amalek, defeats Israel, and occupies the city of palms. Israel serves him for eighteen years.

During a famine in the time of the judges, Elimelech and Naomi leave Bethlehem with their sons and settle in Moab. Elimelech dies, the sons marry Ruth and Orpah, and after about ten years the sons also die.

Hearing that food is again available in Judah, Naomi sets out for home with her daughters-in-law. Orpah eventually returns to Moab, but Ruth binds her future to Naomi, Naomi's people, and Naomi's God.

events.title: Naomi and Ruth Arrive in Bethlehem

meta.description: Naomi and Ruth reach Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. The town is stirred by Naomi's return, while she describes the contrast between the fullness of her departure and the emptiness of her homecoming.

Ruth goes out to glean and happens upon a field belonging to Boaz, a wealthy relative of Elimelech. Having heard of her loyalty to Naomi, Boaz protects her, welcomes her at his meal, and orders his workers to leave extra grain for her.

Ruth returns with an abundant quantity of barley and food left from Boaz's table. Naomi identifies Boaz as one of their family redeemers, and Ruth continues with his workers through the barley and wheat harvests.

events.title: Ruth Appeals to Boaz at the Threshing Floor

meta.description: Following Naomi's instructions, Ruth approaches Boaz privately at the threshing floor and asks him to act as family redeemer. Boaz commends her loyalty and promises to settle the matter after first consulting a nearer relative.

events.title: Boaz Redeems the Family Property and Marries Ruth

meta.description: At Bethlehem's gate, Boaz presents Naomi's property before the nearer redeemer and ten elders. When the other man relinquishes his right with the customary sandal exchange, Boaz acquires the land and takes Ruth as his wife to preserve the dead man's family line.

Ehud, a left-handed Benjaminite, conceals a short double-edged sword while delivering tribute. Alone with Eglon in the roof chamber, he kills the Moabite king, locks the doors, and escapes while the servants delay.
Ehud rallies Israel in Ephraim, seizes the Jordan fords, and defeats about ten thousand Moabites. Moab is subdued and the land rests for eighty years.
Ruth bears a son named Obed, and Naomi embraces the child as her family's life and future. Obed later becomes the father of Jesse and grandfather of David.
Shamgar son of Anath delivers Israel by killing six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
After Ehud's death, King Jabin of Hazor and his commander Sisera oppress Israel for twenty years with nine hundred iron chariots.

Deborah the prophet and judge summons Barak to gather ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun at Mount Tabor. Barak agrees to go only with Deborah, and she warns that a woman will receive the honor over Sisera.
Sisera brings his chariots to the Wadi Kishon, while Barak descends from Mount Tabor with his force. The LORD throws Sisera's army into panic, and Barak pursues it to Harosheth-ha-goiim.
Sisera flees to Jael's tent, where she gives him milk and covers him. Once he is asleep, she drives a tent peg through his temple; Israel afterward presses King Jabin until he is destroyed.

events.title: Deborah and Barak Sing of the Victory

meta.description: Deborah and Barak celebrate the tribes that volunteered, recount the battle at the Kishon, praise Jael's deed, and rebuke those who stayed away. The land rests for forty years.

For seven years Midianite, Amalekite, and eastern raiders consume Israel's crops and livestock, driving the people into mountain refuges. When Israel cries for help, a prophet reminds them that they have disregarded the LORD.

An angel finds Gideon threshing wheat in a winepress and commissions him to deliver Israel. Fire consumes Gideon's offering on a rock, and he builds an altar after being assured that he will survive the encounter.

At night Gideon demolishes his father's altar to Baal and its sacred pole, then offers a bull on a new altar to the LORD. His father challenges Baal to defend his own cause, and Gideon receives the name Jerubbaal.

events.title: Gideon Receives the Signs of the Fleece

meta.description: As an eastern coalition gathers in the Jezreel Valley, Gideon summons troops from northern tribes. He asks for two signs, and dew appears first only on a fleece and then only on the surrounding ground.

events.title: Gideon's Army Is Reduced to Three Hundred

meta.description: Gideon sends home the fearful and then retains only three hundred men selected at the water. A Midianite's dream of barley bread overturning a tent, interpreted as Gideon's victory, reassures him before the attack.

Three companies surround Midian's camp with trumpets, jars, and concealed torches. The sudden noise and light send the enemy fleeing and fighting one another, while Ephraim seizes the crossings and captures Oreb and Zeeb.
Gideon placates Ephraim but punishes Succoth and Penuel for refusing bread to his exhausted force. He captures the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna and kills them for the deaths of his brothers.

Gideon refuses hereditary rule but gathers gold from the spoils and fashions an ephod that becomes a snare at Ophrah. Midian remains subdued during forty years of rest, but after Gideon's death Israel returns to the Baals.
After Israel again turns to evil, the Philistines dominate the people for forty years.

events.title: The Birth of Samson Is Announced

meta.description: The angel of the LORD announces to Manoah's childless wife that her son will be a Nazirite from birth and begin to deliver Israel from Philistine rule. The angel ascends in the altar flame, and the promised child Samson is born and blessed.

At the family's yearly sacrifice in Shiloh, childless Hannah weeps and vows to dedicate a son to the LORD. Eli initially mistakes her silent prayer for drunkenness, then sends her away with a blessing.
Hannah conceives and names her son Samuel. After weaning him, she brings him with an offering to Eli at Shiloh and gives him to lifelong service before the LORD.
Hannah prays in celebration of God's holiness and his reversal of human fortunes, anticipating strength for his king and anointed one. Samuel remains at Shiloh to minister under Eli.

Hophni and Phinehas seize sacrificial meat and abuse women serving at the sanctuary, ignoring Eli's rebuke. In contrast, Samuel ministers in a linen ephod, receives a robe from Hannah each year, and grows in favor.

events.title: Abimelech Is Made King at Shechem

meta.description: Abimelech obtains silver from Shechem, hires followers, and kills his brothers on one stone, though Jotham escapes. Shechem makes Abimelech king, and Jotham answers with a fable warning that ruler and city will consume one another.

Samson seeks a Philistine wife at Timnah, kills a lion on the journey, and later finds honey in its carcass. His wedding companions obtain the answer to his riddle through his bride, so he kills thirty men at Ashkelon to pay the wager and departs in anger.

Finding that his wife has been given to another man, Samson releases three hundred foxes with torches among Philistine grain, vineyards, and olive groves. The Philistines burn the woman and her father, and Samson retaliates with a great slaughter.

Judah binds Samson and hands him to the Philistines, but he breaks the ropes and kills a thousand men with a fresh donkey jawbone. God provides water when he cries out in thirst, and Samson judges Israel for twenty years.

After three years, Shechem turns against Abimelech and supports Gaal. Abimelech defeats Gaal's faction, razes and salts the city, and burns the stronghold where about a thousand people have taken refuge.

While Abimelech tries to burn Thebez's tower, a woman drops an upper millstone that crushes his skull. He orders his armor-bearer to finish him, bringing Jotham's warning against Abimelech and Shechem to fulfillment.
Tola of Issachar lives at Shamir in Ephraim, delivers Israel, and judges for twenty-three years before his death.

events.title: The House of Eli Is Condemned

meta.description: A man of God condemns Eli for honoring his sons above the LORD and announces the fall of his priestly house. The deaths of Hophni and Phinehas on one day will confirm the judgment.

Samuel repeatedly hears his name at night and runs to Eli, who finally recognizes that the LORD is calling the boy. Samuel receives and faithfully reports a judgment against Eli's house, and all Israel comes to recognize him as a prophet.
Surrounded in Gaza, Samson rises at midnight, tears the city gates from their posts, and carries them to a hill facing Hebron.

events.title: The Ark Is Captured at Ebenezer

meta.description: After an initial defeat by the Philistines, Israel brings the ark from Shiloh into battle as Hophni and Phinehas accompany it. Israel suffers a devastating second defeat, the priests are killed, and the ark is captured.

events.title: Eli Dies at the News of the Ark
