meta.description: A messenger carries news of the defeat to Shiloh. Eli falls backward and dies when he hears that the ark has been captured, and the wife of Phinehas dies giving birth to Ichabod amid the calamity.

events.title: The Ark Afflicts the Philistine Cities

meta.description: At Ashdod, the image of Dagon twice falls before the ark and is found broken the second morning. Tumors and panic follow the ark as the Philistines move it from Ashdod to Gath and Ekron.

After seven months the Philistines send the ark away on a new cart with golden guilt offerings. Two untrained cows carry it directly to Beth-shemesh, where the people sacrifice and the five Philistine rulers observe its return.

events.title: The Ark Is Taken to Kiriath-jearim

meta.description: After deaths at Beth-shemesh, the people ask Kiriath-jearim to receive the ark. It is placed in Abinadab's house under Eleazar's care, and twenty years pass while Israel laments before the LORD.

events.title: The Genealogy from Perez to David

meta.description: The book closes with a ten-generation lineage running from Perez through Hezron, Ram, Amminadab, Nahshon, Salmon, Boaz, Obed, and Jesse to David.

Philistine rulers pay Delilah to discover Samson's vulnerability. After three false answers he reveals his Nazirite consecration; she has his hair shaved, and the Philistines blind, shackle, and imprison him at Gaza.

events.title: Samson Destroys the Temple of Dagon

meta.description: The Philistine rulers bring Samson from prison to entertain a crowd assembled in Dagon's temple. He prays for strength, pushes apart the central pillars, and dies with the gathered rulers and people when the building collapses.
Jair the Gileadite judges Israel for twenty-two years. His thirty sons ride thirty donkeys and possess thirty towns in Gilead.

events.title: Samuel Leads Israel to Victory at Mizpah

meta.description: Israel puts away the Baals and Astartes and gathers to confess at Mizpah. As the Philistines attack, the LORD thunders against them; Samuel sets up the Ebenezer stone after Israel's victory and the recovery of lost towns.
Samuel judges Israel throughout his life, traveling annually among Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah before returning to his home and altar at Ramah.

Israel serves the gods of surrounding peoples and suffers Philistine and Ammonite pressure, including eighteen years of oppression in Gilead. The people confess, put away foreign gods, and gather at Mizpah to confront Ammon.

When Samuel's sons pervert justice, Israel's elders demand a king like those of other nations. Samuel warns that a king will conscript their children, appropriate their produce and property, and tax their flocks, but the people persist.

While searching for his father's lost donkeys, Saul goes to consult Samuel in the land of Zuph. Forewarned of Saul's arrival, Samuel gives the Benjaminite the place of honor at a sacrificial meal and prepares to reveal his calling.

Samuel pours oil on Saul's head and gives him several confirming signs. Each occurs that day, including Saul joining a band of prophets when the spirit of God comes upon him, though he does not tell his uncle about the kingship.

events.title: Saul Is Chosen by Lot at Mizpah

meta.description: Samuel assembles Israel and the lot identifies Saul, who is found hiding among the baggage. Samuel presents him to the people, records the rights and duties of kingship, and sends the assembly home.

Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead and threatens to mutilate its men. The spirit of God comes upon Saul, who summons Israel by sending pieces of oxen through the land and routs the Ammonites at the morning watch.

events.title: The Kingship Is Renewed at Gilgal

meta.description: Israel publicly makes Saul king at Gilgal and celebrates with sacrifices. Samuel vindicates his own leadership, recounts the LORD's deliverances, and calls down thunder during the wheat harvest as a sign of the people's fault in demanding a king.

Jonathan strikes the Philistine garrison at Geba, provoking a massive force to assemble at Michmash. Israelite troops hide or flee across the Jordan while Saul waits at Gilgal with a trembling remnant.

As his troops scatter and Samuel delays, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives immediately afterward and announces that Saul's dynasty will not continue; meanwhile Philistine control of metalworking leaves Israel almost without weapons.

Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb the crags to the Philistine outpost and kill about twenty men. Panic and an earthquake throw the camp into confusion, allowing Saul's force, returning defectors, and hidden Israelites to join the rout.

Saul forbids the troops to eat until evening, leaving them exhausted. Jonathan unknowingly tastes honey and is marked by lot for violating the oath, but the people ransom the victor and prevent Saul from killing him.
Saul fights Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, Amalek, and the Philistines. Hard warfare with the Philistines continues, and Saul draws every strong warrior he sees into royal service.

events.title: The Transjordan Tribes Defeat the Hagrites

meta.description: In Saul's reign, warriors from Reuben, Gad, and eastern Manasseh fight the Hagrites and their allies. They call on God during the battle, capture large herds and many prisoners, and occupy the conquered territory until the exile.
Previously driven from home by his brothers, Jephthah lives as a raider in Tob. When Ammon attacks, Gilead's elders recall him and make him their head and commander at Mizpah.

Jephthah exchanges messages with Ammon's king, recounting Israel's route around Edom and Moab and its conquest of Amorite territory from Sihon. The king rejects his argument that Israel has held the land for three hundred years.

Jephthah vows to offer to the LORD whoever first comes from his house if he returns victorious, then defeats Ammon across twenty towns. His only daughter greets him, mourns her virginity for two months, and returns for him to carry out the vow.

Ephraim confronts Jephthah for fighting without them, and Gilead defeats them. At the Jordan fords, pronunciation of a password identifies fleeing Ephraimites; Jephthah judges six years before his death.

events.title: Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon Judge Israel

meta.description: Ibzan judges seven years, Elon ten years, and Abdon eight years. Their notices record large households, marriages, and descendants riding donkeys.

events.title: Saul Spares Agag and the Best Spoil

meta.description: Samuel commissions Saul to execute judgment against Amalek. Saul defeats them from Havilah to Shur but preserves King Agag and the best livestock rather than carrying out the command fully.

Samuel confronts Saul at Gilgal, where the surviving animals expose Saul's claim of obedience. Samuel announces the loss of the kingdom, executes Agag, and departs from Saul for the last time while continuing to grieve for him.

Samuel goes to Jesse's household under cover of a sacrifice and passes over seven older sons. The youngest, David, is summoned from the sheep and anointed, and the spirit of the LORD comes powerfully upon him.
As a harmful spirit torments Saul, his servants seek a skilled musician. David enters the royal service as armor-bearer and relieves Saul's distress by playing the lyre.

The Philistines and Israel face one another across the Valley of Elah while Goliath challenges Israel for forty days. David arrives with provisions for his brothers and questions why the Philistine is permitted to defy Israel's God.

David declines Saul's unfamiliar armor and approaches Goliath with a staff, sling, and five stones. One stone strikes the champion's forehead, David kills him with his own sword, and Israel pursues the fleeing Philistines.

events.title: Jonathan Makes a Covenant with David

meta.description: Jonathan binds himself to David in covenant loyalty and gives him his robe and weapons. David succeeds in every assignment Saul gives him and is placed over the army.

Songs celebrating David's greater victories provoke Saul's jealousy. Saul twice hurls his spear at David and then sends him away as a military commander, but David's success only increases Saul's fear and Israel's affection.

Saul tries to expose David to Philistine danger through marriage negotiations, first involving Merab and then Michal. David supplies the dangerous bride-price for Michal and becomes Saul's son-in-law, while his fame and Saul's hostility grow.
Jonathan warns David of Saul's order to kill him and reminds his father of David's faithful service and victory. Saul temporarily swears not to kill David, who returns to court.
After another victory, David evades Saul's spear and flees home. Michal lowers him through a window, disguises a household idol in his bed, and delays Saul's agents while David escapes.
David takes refuge with Samuel at Naioth. Three groups sent to arrest him fall into prophetic frenzy, and when Saul comes himself the spirit of God also overwhelms him before Samuel.

events.title: Jonathan Warns David at the New Moon

meta.description: David and Jonathan renew their covenant and devise an arrow signal to test Saul's intentions. Saul's rage at David's absence confirms the danger, and the friends part after pledging lasting loyalty between their households.

events.title: David Receives Holy Bread at Nob

meta.description: David deceives the priest Ahimelech about his mission and receives the bread of the Presence and Goliath's sword. Doeg the Edomite, one of Saul's officials, witnesses the encounter.
David flees to King Achish at Gath but fears recognition as Israel's celebrated warrior. He pretends insanity at the city gate until Achish dismisses him.
David's family and about four hundred distressed, indebted, and discontented men join him at the cave of Adullam. He places his parents in Moab and, at Gad's direction, returns to Judah.

events.title: The Priests of Nob Are Massacred

meta.description: Doeg reports Ahimelech's aid to David, and Saul orders the priests killed despite Ahimelech's defense. Doeg kills eighty-five priests and destroys Nob; only Abiathar escapes to David with news of the massacre.

After twice inquiring of the LORD, David defeats Philistine raiders and saves Keilah. When he learns that Saul is approaching and the town would surrender him, David leaves with about six hundred men for wilderness strongholds.
Jonathan finds David in the Wilderness of Ziph and strengthens him in God, acknowledging that David will be king. They renew their covenant before separating for the last time.
The Ziphites disclose David's position, and Saul nearly encloses him on a mountain in the wilderness of Maon. A report of a Philistine raid abruptly draws Saul away, and David escapes to En-gedi.

events.title: David Spares Saul in the Cave

meta.description: Saul enters a cave at En-gedi where David and his men are hidden. David cuts a corner from Saul's cloak but refuses to harm the anointed king, then proves his restraint and receives Saul's acknowledgment that he will reign.
Samuel dies and all Israel gathers to mourn him. He is buried at his home in Ramah.

events.title: Abigail Prevents David from Killing Nabal

meta.description: Nabal insults David's messengers and refuses provisions despite David's protection of his shepherds. Abigail intercepts the armed company with a generous gift and persuades David not to incur bloodguilt through personal vengeance.

events.title: Nabal Dies and David Marries Abigail

meta.description: After Abigail tells Nabal what happened, he becomes unresponsive and dies about ten days later. David then marries Abigail and also takes Ahinoam as wife, while Saul gives Michal to another man.

events.title: David Spares Saul in His Camp

meta.description: David and Abishai enter Saul's camp at night while the army sleeps. David refuses to let Abishai kill Saul, takes the spear and water jar beside the king's head, and from a distant hill again demonstrates that he means Saul no harm.

David crosses to Achish of Gath with six hundred men and their households, ending Saul's pursuit. Given Ziklag, David raids southern peoples while misleading Achish about his targets during a stay of one year and four months.
Skilled fighters from Benjamin, Gad, Judah, and Manasseh join David while Saul still threatens him. Their numbers grow daily, and David appoints trusted arrivals as officers of his forces.

events.title: Saul Consults the Medium at Endor

meta.description: Facing the Philistine army at Shunem without an answer from dreams, Urim, or prophets, Saul visits a medium in disguise. Samuel appears and announces that Israel will be defeated and Saul and his sons will die the next day.

Although Achish trusts David, the other Philistine commanders refuse to let him accompany their army against Israel. David and his men are ordered back to Philistine territory while the army advances toward Jezreel.

Returning on the third day, David finds Ziklag burned and its families taken captive. Though his embittered men speak of stoning him, David seeks direction through Abiathar's ephod and sets out in pursuit.

An abandoned Egyptian servant guides David to the Amalekite camp, which he attacks from twilight into the next evening. David recovers every captive and possession, grants equal shares to those left with the baggage, and sends spoil to Judah's elders.

events.title: Saul and His Sons Die at Gilboa

meta.description: The Philistines rout Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. Badly wounded and fearing capture, Saul falls on his sword, and nearby Israelite towns are abandoned to Philistine occupation.

The Philistines display Saul's body and those of his sons at Beth-shan after placing his armor in Astarte's temple. Warriors from Jabesh-gilead travel through the night to recover the bodies, burn them, bury the bones, and fast seven days.

events.title: David Hears of Saul and Jonathan's Deaths

meta.description: An Amalekite arrives at Ziklag with Saul's crown and claims to have killed the wounded king. David and his men mourn until evening, after which David executes the messenger for saying that he killed the LORD's anointed.
David composes a lament for Saul and Jonathan and orders Judah to learn it. The song grieves Israel's fallen warriors and David's profound loss of Jonathan.

At the LORD's direction David moves his household and followers to Hebron, where Judah anoints him king. He commends the people of Jabesh-gilead for burying Saul and asks them to remain loyal and courageous.

events.title: Abner Makes Ishbaal King over Israel

meta.description: Abner takes Saul's son Ishbaal to Mahanaim and establishes him over the northern tribes, while Judah follows David. Ishbaal reigns two years amid David's seven-and-a-half-year rule from Hebron.

events.title: Saul and His Sons Die on Mount Gilboa

meta.description: The Philistines rout Israel on Mount Gilboa and kill Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua. Wounded and fearing capture, Saul falls on his own sword, and the Israelites abandon nearby towns to the Philistines.

events.title: The People of Jabesh Bury Saul

meta.description: The Philistines display Saul's head and armor after stripping the fallen, but warriors from Jabesh recover the bodies of Saul and his sons. They bury the bones and fast for seven days, while the account attributes the transfer of the kingdom to Saul's unfaithfulness.

events.title: The Houses of Saul and David Fight at Gibeon

meta.description: Forces led by Abner and Joab meet beside Gibeon's pool, where a contest between twelve men from each side becomes a fierce battle. Asahel pursues Abner and is killed, planting the cause of Joab's later vengeance.

As David's house grows stronger, Ishbaal accuses Abner concerning Saul's concubine Rizpah. Offended, Abner arranges to transfer Israel's allegiance to David, who requires the return of Michal before receiving him at Hebron.

Joab recalls Abner after David has dismissed him in peace and kills him at Hebron to avenge Asahel. David publicly disavows the murder, mourns at Abner's grave, and refuses food, convincing Israel that he had no part in the killing.
Rechab and Baanah murder Ishbaal during his midday rest and carry his head to David. Instead of rewarding them, David executes the assassins and buries Ishbaal's head in Abner's tomb.

events.title: David Becomes King over All Israel

meta.description: All Israel's tribes come to Hebron, acknowledge David as their kin and shepherd, and anoint him king. David is thirty years old at his accession and reigns forty years in Hebron and Jerusalem.
David captures the Jebusite stronghold of Zion and makes it the City of David. He builds up Jerusalem, receives a cedar house through Hiram of Tyre, and establishes a growing royal household.

events.title: David Defeats the Philistines in Rephaim

meta.description: The Philistines twice spread through the Valley of Rephaim after David's anointing. David inquires of the LORD before both battles, breaking through them at Baal-perazim and then striking from Geba to Gezer.

events.title: All Israel Anoints David at Hebron

meta.description: Representatives and armed divisions from every tribe gather at Hebron and acknowledge David as Israel's shepherd and ruler. The elders make a covenant with him, anoint him king, and celebrate together for three days.
David and Israel take the Jebusite stronghold of Zion. Joab leads the first attack and becomes commander, while David settles in the stronghold and develops the city around it.

A register preserves the names and exploits of the warriors who helped establish David's kingdom. It recalls exceptional victories, the dangerous retrieval of water from Bethlehem, and David's refusal to treat his men's lives lightly.
Hiram of Tyre sends cedar, masons, and carpenters to build David a house in Jerusalem. David recognizes that his kingdom has been established, and his household grows in the capital.

events.title: David Defeats the Philistines in Rephaim

meta.description: The Philistines twice raid the Valley of Rephaim after learning of David's accession. David seeks God's direction before each engagement, defeats them at Baal-perazim, and drives the second force from Gibeon to Gezer.

David gathers Israel to bring the ark from Abinadab's house on a new cart. When Uzzah reaches out as the oxen shake it, he dies beside the ark, and David leaves it for three months at the house of Obed-edom.

Hearing that Obed-edom has prospered, David brings the ark into Jerusalem with sacrifices, shouting, and dancing. Michal despises his exuberance and confronts him afterward, remaining childless for the rest of her life.

events.title: The LORD Promises David a Dynasty

meta.description: David proposes building a house for the ark, but Nathan receives a different word: David's offspring will build the temple, while the LORD will build David a lasting house and establish his throne.

events.title: David Prays over the Dynastic Promise

meta.description: David sits before the LORD in wonder at the promise to his house, praises God's uniqueness and Israel's redemption, and asks that the promised blessing endure forever.

events.title: Uzzah Dies during the First Ark Procession

meta.description: David gathers Israel to bring the ark from Kiriath-jearim on a new cart. Uzzah dies after reaching toward it when the oxen stumble, so David leaves the ark in Obed-edom's house for three months.

events.title: The Ark Is Brought to Jerusalem

meta.description: David prepares a tent and directs consecrated Levites to carry the ark with poles, accompanied by singers, instruments, sacrifices, and public rejoicing. The ark is placed in its tent, offerings are made, and gifts of food are distributed throughout Israel.

events.title: David Appoints Ministers before the Ark

meta.description: David appoints Asaph and other Levites to lead regular praise and remembrance before the ark. He maintains a second priestly ministry under Zadok at Gibeon, ordering worship at both sanctuaries before the assembly returns home.

events.title: God Promises David an Enduring Dynasty

meta.description: David proposes replacing the ark's tent with a temple, but Nathan receives a message that David will not build it. Instead, David's son will build the house, and God promises to establish that son's throne and David's dynasty.

events.title: David Responds to the Dynastic Promise

meta.description: David marvels that God has promised a future to his household. He praises Israel's redeemer and asks that the blessing spoken over his dynasty be firmly established.

David subdues Philistines, Moabites, Arameans, and Edomites, placing garrisons and receiving tribute. He dedicates captured silver, gold, and bronze to the LORD as his power extends toward the Euphrates.

David subdues Philistia, Moab, Zobah, Damascus, and Edom, installing garrisons and receiving tribute. He dedicates captured precious metals for sacred use, including bronze later used in Solomon's temple furnishings.

events.title: David Makes Expiation for Saul's Attack on Gibeon

meta.description: A three-year famine is attributed to Saul's bloodshed against the Gibeonites. David hands over seven of Saul's descendants while sparing Jonathan's son; after Rizpah guards the bodies, David gathers their bones with those of Saul and Jonathan for burial at Zela.

In several battles David and his warriors defeat four descendants of the giants from Gath. After Abishai saves an exhausted David from Ishbi-benob, the troops no longer permit the king to enter battle with them.

David administers justice and equity throughout Israel. Joab commands the army, Jehoshaphat serves as recorder, Zadok and Ahimelech as priests, Seraiah as secretary, and Benaiah leads the royal guard.

For Jonathan's sake David seeks a survivor of Saul's house and summons Jonathan's disabled son Mephibosheth. He restores Saul's lands to him, assigns Ziba's household to cultivate them, and gives Mephibosheth a permanent place at the royal table.
David governs Israel with justice and equity. The account names the commanders, recorder, priests, secretary, royal guard leader, and chief officials serving his kingdom.

David sends condolences to Hanun after the death of his father, Nahash. Suspecting espionage, Ammon's leaders shave half the envoys' beards and cut their garments, and David lets the humiliated men remain at Jericho until their beards regrow.

events.title: Joab Defeats Ammon and Its Aramean Allies

meta.description: The Ammonites hire a large Aramean force and confront Joab from two directions. Joab and Abishai divide the army between the threats, and both enemy forces retreat.

events.title: David Defeats the Arameans at Helam

meta.description: Hadadezer gathers Arameans from beyond the Euphrates, but David crosses the Jordan and defeats them at Helam. Their subject kings make peace with Israel and refuse further aid to Ammon.

David sends envoys to console Hanun after the death of his father Nahash. Ammonite officials accuse them of espionage, and Hanun shaves them and cuts their garments, forcing the disgraced men to wait at Jericho before returning.

events.title: Joab Defeats Ammon and Its Allies

meta.description: The Ammonites hire a large allied force from Aramean territories. Surrounded on two fronts, Joab divides Israel's army with Abishai, and both the Arameans and Ammonites retreat before them.

Aramean forces arrive from beyond the Euphrates under Shophach, but David gathers Israel and defeats them after crossing the Jordan. Hadadezer's subjects make peace with David and cease supporting Ammon.
While Joab besieges Rabbah in the spring, David remains in Jerusalem, sees Bathsheba bathing, and has her brought to him. She later sends word that she is pregnant.
Unable to induce Uriah to go home from the siege, David sends him back carrying orders that expose him to death in battle. After Bathsheba mourns, David marries her and she bears his son.

Nathan tells David of a rich man who took a poor man's beloved lamb, drawing the king's own condemnation before identifying his guilt. David confesses, and Nathan announces forgiveness alongside continuing consequences within his house.

David fasts and lies on the ground while the child is gravely ill, but the boy dies on the seventh day. David then washes, worships, and eats, explaining that his fasting can no longer bring the child back.
David comforts Bathsheba, and she gives birth to Solomon. The LORD loves the child and sends word through Nathan, who gives him another name expressing that favor.
Joab captures Rabbah's water supply and summons David to complete the conquest. David takes the royal city, its crown, and extensive spoil, then subjects the Ammonite population to forced labor.
Joab ravages Ammon and overthrows Rabbah while David remains in Jerusalem. David takes the royal crown and extensive spoil, imposes labor on the inhabitants, and returns with the army.

events.title: David's Warriors Defeat the Giants of Gath

meta.description: During successive Philistine conflicts at Gezer and Gath, Sibbecai, Elhanan, and Jonathan defeat prominent descendants of the giants. These victories complete the brief record of David's later Philistine wars.

On Jonadab's advice Amnon feigns illness to isolate his half-sister Tamar, then assaults and expels her despite her pleas. Tamar lives desolate in Absalom's house, David is angry but does not punish Amnon, and Absalom conceals his hatred.

Two years after Tamar's assault, Absalom invites the royal sons to a sheep-shearing feast and orders his servants to kill Amnon. Absalom flees to his grandfather Talmai in Geshur and remains there three years.

events.title: The Wise Woman of Tekoa Appeals for Absalom

meta.description: Joab sends a wise woman to tell David a fabricated case about her endangered surviving son. She turns the king's judgment toward his banished son, and David permits Joab to bring Absalom back to Jerusalem without admitting him to court.

After two years in Jerusalem without seeing David, Absalom burns Joab's barley field to force his attention. Joab carries his demand to the king, and Absalom is summoned, bows before David, and receives his kiss.

Absalom cultivates public favor at Jerusalem's gate for four years, presenting himself as a better source of justice. He then goes to Hebron under cover of a vow, proclaims himself king, and recruits David's counselor Ahithophel.

David evacuates his household and loyal forces as Absalom's conspiracy grows, crossing the Kidron toward the wilderness. He returns the ark and priests to Jerusalem as informants and sends Hushai back to frustrate Ahithophel's advice.

events.title: Ziba and Shimei Meet the Fugitive King

meta.description: Ziba supplies David's party and accuses Mephibosheth of remaining behind to recover Saul's kingdom, prompting David to award him the estate. At Bahurim, Shimei curses and stones David, who refuses to let Abishai kill him.

Hushai presents himself as Absalom's servant while Ahithophel advises Absalom to take David's concubines publicly. Absalom follows the counsel on the palace roof, asserting his complete break with his father.

Hushai persuades Absalom to reject Ahithophel's plan for an immediate strike against David. The priests' sons carry warning through danger to David, who crosses the Jordan, while Ahithophel returns home and takes his own life.

David reaches Mahanaim and receives abundant provisions from allies as Absalom crosses the Jordan. David divides his army under Joab, Abishai, and Ittai but remains at the city after charging them to spare Absalom.

David's troops defeat Absalom's army in the forest of Ephraim. Absalom is caught by the head in an oak while his mule continues on, and Joab ignores David's order by killing him and ending the pursuit.

Ahimaaz and a Cushite race to report the victory, but David asks only about his son and collapses in grief on learning of Absalom's death. Joab rebukes him for shaming the troops, and David returns to the city gate to receive them.

David secures Judah's invitation to return and promises Amasa command of the army. At the Jordan he pardons Shimei, hears Mephibosheth's answer to Ziba's accusation, rewards Barzillai through Chimham, and crosses toward Jerusalem.

events.title: Sheba Leads Israel Away from David

meta.description: A fierce dispute between Israel and Judah over escorting the king gives Sheba the opportunity to call the northern tribes away. When Amasa delays mustering Judah, David sends Abishai and the royal troops in pursuit.
Joab meets Amasa at Gibeon, takes him by the beard as if to greet him, and kills him with a concealed sword. The pursuing force then resumes following Joab after Sheba.

Joab besieges Sheba at Abel of Beth-maacah until a wise woman negotiates the city's safety. The inhabitants execute Sheba and throw his head over the wall, ending the revolt and restoring Joab to command.

David praises the LORD as his refuge and rescuer from Saul and every enemy. He recounts divine intervention in his distress, strength in battle, victory over hostile peoples, and enduring loyalty to the anointed king and his descendants.
David's final oracle describes just rule in the fear of God as morning light and affirms the secure covenant made with his house, while comparing the godless to thorns destined for fire.

A register honors the deeds of David's Three and Thirty, including the defense of a field, a hazardous retrieval of water from Bethlehem, and the exploits of Abishai and Benaiah. Uriah the Hittite closes the list of thirty-seven.

Despite Joab's objection, David orders the commanders to number Israel and Judah from Dan to Beer-sheba. They return after nine months and twenty days, and David is stricken with remorse after hearing the count.

events.title: David Orders a Census of Israel

meta.description: David commands Joab to count Israel despite the commander's objection. Joab omits Levi and Benjamin, and David confesses his guilt after receiving the totals.

Through Gad, David must choose among famine, flight, and pestilence as consequences for the census. He chooses to fall into divine mercy; seventy thousand die before the destroying angel is halted beside Araunah's threshing floor.

events.title: David Builds an Altar on Araunah's Threshing Floor

meta.description: At Gad's direction David buys Araunah's threshing floor rather than accepting it as a gift. He builds an altar and presents sacrifices there, after which the plague is averted from Israel.

As David's strength fails, Adonijah presents himself as king with support from Joab and Abiathar and holds a sacrificial feast. Nathan and Bathsheba alert David that Solomon and his supporters face danger unless the succession is settled.

David confirms Solomon as successor and sends him to Gihon on the royal mule, where Zadok and Nathan anoint him. Adonijah's feast collapses at the news, and Solomon conditionally spares him when he seeks refuge at the altar.

events.title: David Gives His Final Charge and Dies

meta.description: David charges Solomon to keep the law of Moses, preserve loyalty toward Barzillai's family, and deal wisely with Joab and Shimei. David dies after forty years of rule and is buried in his city, leaving Solomon on the throne.
Adonijah asks Bathsheba to obtain Abishag as his wife, and she carries the request to Solomon. Solomon interprets it as another claim to the kingdom and orders Benaiah to execute his brother.

events.title: Abiathar Is Banished and Joab Is Killed

meta.description: Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood but spares his life because he shared David's hardships. Joab takes refuge at the altar, yet Benaiah executes him for the blood of Abner and Amasa and succeeds him over the army.

Gad offers David a choice among three judgments, and David places himself in God's mercy. A three-day pestilence kills seventy thousand before the destroying angel is halted at Ornan's threshing floor outside Jerusalem.

At Gad's instruction David buys Ornan's threshing floor at full price, builds an altar, and offers sacrifices. Fire answers from heaven, the plague ends, and David identifies the site as the future location of the temple and its altar.

events.title: David Prepares Materials for the Temple

meta.description: Knowing that Solomon is young, David gathers stonecutters and amasses dressed stone, iron, bronze, and cedar. He intends the future temple to be renowned even though he will not build it himself.

events.title: David Charges Solomon to Build the Temple

meta.description: David tells Solomon that his wars and bloodshed prevent him from building the temple, while his son has been chosen for the work during a reign of peace. He transfers extensive resources and urges Solomon and Israel's leaders to begin construction faithfully.
As David reaches old age, he makes Solomon king over Israel. The brief accession notice introduces David's final organization of the nation's worship and administration.

David counts the Levites and assigns divisions to temple work, civil offices, gatekeeping, and music. Their responsibilities are adapted for a permanent sanctuary in Jerusalem rather than a portable tabernacle.

David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and other leaders assign priestly households to twenty-four courses by lot. Musicians descended from Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun are likewise arranged into twenty-four trained groups for sanctuary service.
Levitical families receive gate assignments by lot, while others oversee sacred treasuries and dedicated gifts. David also appoints officers and judges for regions west and east of the Jordan.

Twelve rotating military divisions are assigned to serve one month each, and leaders are named for Israel's tribes. Other stewards manage the crown's lands, produce, herds, property, counselors, and army.

events.title: David Presents Solomon and the Temple Plan

meta.description: Before Israel's assembled leaders, David identifies Solomon as the chosen successor and temple builder. He charges both people and son to remain faithful, then gives Solomon detailed plans, service divisions, and specifications for the sanctuary furnishings.

events.title: Israel's Leaders Give for the Temple

meta.description: David dedicates royal resources and his personal gold and silver to the future temple, then invites Israel's leaders to contribute. They respond with large voluntary gifts of metals and precious stones, producing widespread rejoicing.

David blesses God before the assembly, acknowledging that power, wealth, and the people's offerings all come from God. He asks that Israel retain its willing devotion and that Solomon receive an undivided heart for obedience and temple building.

events.title: Solomon Is Anointed a Second Time

meta.description: After abundant sacrifices and a communal feast, the assembly again makes Solomon king and anoints Zadok as priest. Israel's leaders, warriors, and David's sons pledge allegiance, and Solomon assumes the throne with broad support.

events.title: David Dies and Solomon Succeeds Him

meta.description: David dies after a forty-year reign, including seven years at Hebron and thirty-three at Jerusalem. Solomon succeeds him, and the chronicler points to prophetic records for the fuller account of David's reign.

Solomon leads Israel's leaders to the ancient sanctuary at Gibeon and offers abundant sacrifices. God grants his request for wisdom and knowledge and promises him extraordinary wealth and honor as well.

events.title: Solomon Asks for Wisdom at Gibeon

meta.description: After marrying Pharaoh's daughter, Solomon sacrifices at Gibeon and receives a divine invitation in a dream. He asks for discernment to govern Israel and is promised exceptional wisdom together with riches and honor.

Two women each claim the same living infant after another child dies. Solomon proposes dividing the boy, revealing the true mother through her willingness to surrender him alive, and Israel recognizes divine wisdom in the judgment.

Solomon appoints high officials and twelve regional governors who provision the court in monthly rotation. His rule extends from the Euphrates toward Egypt, and Judah and Israel live securely amid royal abundance.

Solomon's wisdom surpasses that of celebrated sages in Egypt and the east. He composes thousands of proverbs and songs, speaks about the natural world, and receives visitors sent by rulers from many nations.

events.title: Solomon Prepares to Build the Temple

meta.description: Solomon organizes a large labor force and arranges with King Huram of Tyre for timber and a master artisan. He presents the planned sanctuary as a place of worship for the God whom no building can contain.

events.title: Shimei Breaks His Restriction and Is Executed

meta.description: Solomon confines Shimei to Jerusalem under penalty of death. Three years later Shimei travels to Gath after runaway servants, and Benaiah executes him when he returns, completing Solomon's consolidation.

events.title: Solomon and Hiram Prepare for the Temple

meta.description: Solomon arranges with Hiram of Tyre for cedar and cypress from Lebanon in exchange for provisions. A large levy of laborers, stonecutters, carriers, and supervisors prepares dressed stone and timber for the sanctuary.

In Solomon's fourth year, 480 years after the exodus, work begins on the house of the LORD. Stone dressed at the quarry, cedar paneling, gold overlay, carved cherubim, and an inner sanctuary are completed after seven years.
In Solomon's fourth year, work begins on Mount Moriah at the site David had designated. The builders complete the sanctuary, its courts, bronze furnishings, golden vessels, and monumental cherubim.

The bronze worker Hiram fashions the pillars, capitals, sea, wheeled stands, basins, and utensils for the temple. Solomon also provides golden furnishings and stores David's dedicated treasures in the completed sanctuary.
Over thirteen years Solomon builds his palace, the House of the Forest of Lebanon, halls of pillars and judgment, and a residence for Pharaoh's daughter, using costly dressed stone and cedar.

events.title: The Ark Is Brought into the Temple

meta.description: During the seventh-month festival, Israel's leaders assemble as the priests carry the ark into the inner sanctuary beneath the cherubim. A cloud fills the house, preventing priestly service, and Solomon blesses the assembly for the fulfilled promise to David.

events.title: Solomon Prays at the Temple Dedication

meta.description: Before the altar Solomon asks God to hear prayers directed toward the temple in cases of injustice, defeat, drought, famine, war, exile, and repentance. He includes the foreigner and concludes by calling Israel to wholehearted obedience.
Solomon and the great assembly dedicate the temple with an immense number of sacrifices. After the festival the people depart joyfully because of the good shown to David and Israel.

events.title: The Ark Is Brought into the Temple

meta.description: At the seventh-month festival, priests and Levites bring the ark and sacred objects into the completed temple. Unified music and praise accompany the ceremony, and a cloud of divine glory fills the building so that the priests cannot continue ministering.

Solomon blesses the assembly and prays that God will hear petitions directed toward the temple, including prayers made in defeat, drought, exile, or by foreigners. Fire consumes the offerings, the people worship, and a fourteen-day national celebration follows.

events.title: God Answers Solomon after the Dedication

meta.description: God appears to Solomon and accepts the temple as a place for sacrifice and prayer. He promises restoration when a chastened people turn back, while warning that royal unfaithfulness would bring national ruin and make the temple an object of astonishment.

events.title: The LORD Appears to Solomon Again

meta.description: After the temple and palace are complete, Solomon receives assurance that his prayer has been heard and the temple consecrated. The promise of dynasty remains conditional on faithfulness, while apostasy will bring exile and the ruin of the house.
At the end of twenty years of construction, Solomon gives Hiram twenty towns in Galilee in return for timber and gold. Hiram finds the towns unsatisfactory and gives the district a disparaging name.

events.title: Solomon's Building Program and Forced Labor

meta.description: Solomon uses forced labor to build the temple, palace, Jerusalem's defenses, Hazor, Megiddo, Gezer, and numerous storage and chariot cities. The remaining non-Israelite populations supply the permanent labor force.

After twenty years of construction, Solomon fortifies cities, administers subject labor, orders temple service according to David's arrangements, and completes his palace. His wife is moved from David's city because places associated with the ark are holy.
Solomon builds a fleet at Ezion-geber on the Red Sea. Experienced sailors supplied by Hiram join Solomon's servants in bringing a large shipment of gold from Ophir.

events.title: Solomon Sends a Fleet to Ophir

meta.description: With sailors supplied by Huram, Solomon launches a fleet from the Red Sea ports of Ezion-geber and Eloth. The expedition returns from Ophir with a great quantity of gold.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon

meta.description: The queen of Sheba comes to Jerusalem with spices, gold, precious stones, and difficult questions. Solomon answers her fully, and she marvels at his wisdom, court, prosperity, and worship before exchanging lavish gifts with him.

Gold pours into Solomon's court from tribute, trade, and fleets, furnishing shields, vessels, and an ivory throne. He also amasses chariots and horses and becomes a broker of imported military equipment to neighboring kings.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon

meta.description: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with difficult questions and is overwhelmed by his wisdom, prosperity, court, and worship. She exchanges lavish gifts with the king before returning home.

Solomon's many foreign wives turn his heart toward their gods in his old age, and he builds high places around Jerusalem. The LORD announces that most of the kingdom will be torn from his son, though one tribe will remain for David's sake.
Hadad the Edomite returns from Egyptian refuge as an adversary to Solomon, while Rezon establishes himself at Damascus and opposes Israel from the north.

events.title: Ahijah Promises Ten Tribes to Jeroboam

meta.description: The prophet Ahijah tears a new garment into twelve pieces and gives ten to Jeroboam, promising him Israel if he walks faithfully. Solomon seeks Jeroboam's death, and Jeroboam flees to Shishak in Egypt.
Solomon's forty-year reign ends with his death and burial in the City of David. His son Rehoboam succeeds him.
At Shechem the assembly asks Rehoboam to lighten Solomon's heavy service. He rejects the elders' advice to serve the people and instead follows younger counselors who urge an even harsher answer.

The northern tribes reject David's house, stone the forced-labor official, and make Jeroboam king, while Judah remains with Rehoboam. Shemaiah prevents Rehoboam's army from attacking Israel by declaring that the division comes from God.

events.title: A Man of God Condemns Bethel's Altar

meta.description: A man of God from Judah predicts that Josiah will desecrate Bethel's altar. The altar splits and Jeroboam's outstretched hand withers, then is restored at the prophet's intercession.

events.title: The Man of God Is Killed by a Lion

meta.description: An old Bethel prophet deceives the man of God into returning for a meal contrary to his command. A lion kills him on the road without consuming the body, and the old prophet buries him while affirming his word against the shrines.

Fearing that worship in Jerusalem will restore allegiance to Rehoboam, Jeroboam builds shrines at Bethel and Dan with golden calves. He appoints non-Levitical priests and devises his own eighth-month festival.
The account surveys Solomon's immense revenues, golden furnishings, international trade, military resources, wisdom, and dominion. After forty years as king, he dies and Rehoboam succeeds him.

Rehoboam rejects the elders' counsel and answers Israel's request for lighter service with threats of greater severity. The northern tribes rebel against David's house, leaving Rehoboam to rule Judah and Benjamin.

Rehoboam gathers an army to recover the northern kingdom, but the prophet Shemaiah declares that the division has come from God. Judah and Benjamin obey and abandon the campaign against their kindred.

Rehoboam strengthens a network of fortified cities and stocks them with supplies and weapons. Priests, Levites, and worshipers displaced by Jeroboam move south and strengthen his kingdom for three years.

Judah practices idolatry under Rehoboam, and in his fifth year Shishak of Egypt takes the temple and palace treasures, including Solomon's golden shields. Rehoboam replaces them with bronze as war with Jeroboam continues.

After Rehoboam and Judah abandon the law, Shishak of Egypt captures fortified cities and advances on Jerusalem. The leaders humble themselves at Shemaiah's warning, so the city is spared destruction, though its temple and palace treasures are taken.
Abijam reigns three years in Jerusalem and continues his father's sins, yet David's line retains a lamp in the city. War with Jeroboam continues until Asa succeeds him.

Surrounded by Jeroboam's larger force, Abijah appeals to the Davidic covenant and Judah's temple worship. Judah cries out, the priests sound their trumpets, and Abijah wins a decisive victory and captures several towns.

Jeroboam sends his disguised wife to the blind prophet Ahijah regarding their sick son. Ahijah recognizes her, announces the destruction of Jeroboam's dynasty and the child's death, and the boy dies as she reaches Tirzah.
Asa removes cult prostitutes and idols and deposes the queen mother Maacah for her Asherah image. Though the high places remain, he stays devoted and brings dedicated gifts into the temple.
Asa removes foreign worship sites, directs Judah to seek God, and uses a decade of peace to strengthen fortified cities. He also organizes a large army from Judah and Benjamin.

After two years of Nadab's reign, Baasha assassinates him during the siege of Gibbethon and destroys every member of Jeroboam's house. Baasha then rules from Tirzah while perpetuating Jeroboam's sins.
Zerah advances to Mareshah with an enormous army, and Asa appeals to God rather than Judah's strength. The invaders are routed toward Gerar, and Judah returns with extensive plunder.

events.title: Asa Buys an Alliance against Baasha

meta.description: When Baasha fortifies Ramah to blockade Judah, Asa sends temple and palace silver and gold to Ben-hadad of Damascus. Aramean attacks draw Baasha away, and Asa dismantles Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah.

Encouraged by Azariah's prophecy, Asa removes idols, repairs the altar, and gathers Judah with migrants from the northern tribes. In his fifteenth year the assembly sacrifices and enters a solemn covenant to seek God wholeheartedly.
The prophet Jehu announces that Baasha's dynasty will meet the same destruction it inflicted on Jeroboam's house because Baasha led Israel in the same sins.

events.title: Zimri Kills Elah and Baasha's House

meta.description: While Elah drinks himself drunk in Tirzah, the chariot commander Zimri assassinates him and takes the throne. Zimri immediately eliminates Baasha's whole family, fulfilling Jehu's word.
The army at Gibbethon proclaims Omri king and besieges Tirzah. After only seven days on the throne, Zimri burns the palace over himself rather than be captured.
Israel divides between supporters of Omri and Tibni until Omri's faction prevails. Omri buys the hill of Samaria, fortifies it, and establishes the new northern capital there.

events.title: Asa Buys an Alliance with Aram

meta.description: When Baasha fortifies Ramah, Asa sends temple and palace treasure to Ben-hadad of Aram, inducing him to attack northern Israel. The seer Hanani rebukes Asa for relying on Aram, and the angry king imprisons him and oppresses others.

events.title: Ahab and Jezebel Establish Baal Worship

meta.description: Omri exceeds his predecessors in evil, and his son Ahab goes further after marrying Jezebel of Sidon. Ahab builds a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria, while Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost Joshua had foretold.

Jehoshaphat follows Asa's generally faithful course, removes remaining cult prostitutes, and makes peace with Israel, though high places persist. His attempted Ophir fleet is wrecked at Ezion-geber before Jehoram succeeds him.
In his final years Asa develops a severe foot disease but seeks physicians without seeking God. He dies in the forty-first year of his reign and receives an elaborate royal burial.

Jehoshaphat strengthens Judah, removes illicit worship sites, and sends officials, Levites, and priests through the towns with the book of the law. Neighboring peoples fear Judah, while the king accumulates tribute, fortifications, and troops.

Elijah tells Ahab that rain and dew will cease except at his word. He then hides east of the Jordan at the Wadi Cherith, drinking from the stream and receiving food brought by ravens until it dries up.

events.title: Elijah Is Fed by the Widow of Zarephath

meta.description: Elijah asks a destitute widow at Zarephath for food as she prepares a final meal for herself and her son. Her small supply of meal and oil then continues without failing throughout the drought.
When the widow's son stops breathing, Elijah carries him to the upper room and cries to the LORD. The child's life returns, confirming to his mother that Elijah is a man of God whose word is true.

In the third year of severe drought Elijah meets Obadiah, who has hidden a hundred prophets from Jezebel, and sends him to summon Ahab. Elijah rejects Ahab's accusation of troubling Israel and calls king, people, and Baal's prophets to Carmel.

Baal's prophets call and cut themselves from morning into afternoon without receiving an answer. Elijah repairs the LORD's altar with twelve stones, drenches the offering, and prays; fire consumes sacrifice, altar, and water, and the people seize Baal's prophets.
Elijah prays on Carmel and sends his servant seven times to look toward the sea. A tiny cloud grows into a heavy storm, while Elijah runs ahead of Ahab's chariot to Jezreel.

Threatened by Jezebel, Elijah flees into the wilderness and asks to die, but an angel feeds him for the journey to Horeb. After wind, earthquake, and fire, he encounters the LORD in quiet and receives new commissions concerning Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha.
Elijah finds Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and throws his mantle over him. Elisha sacrifices his oxen, feeds the people, and leaves to become Elijah's servant.

Ben-hadad of Aram besieges Samaria with thirty-two allied kings and escalates his demands beyond Ahab's initial submission. Directed by a prophet, a small Israelite force attacks at noon while the allied kings drink and drives the Arameans away.

events.title: The Arameans Are Defeated at Aphek

meta.description: Believing Israel's God is limited to the hills, Aram returns in spring to fight on the plain at Aphek. Israel wins another overwhelming victory, but Ahab makes a treaty with Ben-hadad and releases him.

A wounded and disguised prophet presents Ahab with a story that draws the king into judging himself. He then announces that Ahab's life and people are forfeit because he released a man devoted to destruction.

events.title: Naboth Is Killed for His Vineyard

meta.description: Naboth refuses to surrender his ancestral vineyard to Ahab. Jezebel arranges false accusations and his execution by stoning, after which Ahab goes down to take possession of the property.

Elijah confronts Ahab in Naboth's vineyard and announces violent judgment on his dynasty and Jezebel. Ahab humbles himself in sackcloth and fasting, so the disaster on his house is deferred to his son's reign.

Ahab recruits Jehoshaphat to retake Ramoth-gilead, while hundreds of prophets promise success. Micaiah alone describes Israel scattered without a shepherd and reveals that the favorable prophecies are leading Ahab toward disaster.
Ahab enters battle in disguise while Jehoshaphat wears royal robes. A randomly shot arrow penetrates Ahab's armor; he dies that evening, and dogs lick his blood from the washed chariot as foretold.
Ahab's son Ahaziah reigns briefly at Samaria and continues the worship and policies of Ahab, Jezebel, and Jeroboam, provoking the LORD as his father had done.

Linked to Ahab by marriage, Jehoshaphat joins his campaign despite Micaiah's warning of disaster. Jehoshaphat is rescued when he cries out in battle, while a stray arrow mortally wounds the disguised Ahab.

The prophet Jehu condemns Jehoshaphat's alliance with the wicked but acknowledges the good found in him. The king then appoints judges across Judah and establishes a Jerusalem court for religious and royal cases.

events.title: Elijah Condemns Ahaziah's Appeal to Ekron

meta.description: After being injured in a fall, Ahaziah sends messengers to consult the god of Ekron about his recovery. Elijah intercepts them, survives the king's attempts to seize him, and announces that Ahaziah will die from the injury.

Elisha follows Elijah from Gilgal through Bethel and Jericho and across the divided Jordan. A fiery chariot separates them, Elijah ascends in a whirlwind, and Elisha returns across the river with his master's mantle as the prophetic communities recognize his succession.
Elisha uses salt to make Jericho's harmful spring wholesome. On the road to Bethel he curses a group that jeers at him, and two bears maul forty-two of them.

events.title: Israel, Judah, and Edom Campaign against Moab

meta.description: Jehoram of Israel joins Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom to suppress Moab's revolt. Elisha promises water and victory, but after the allies devastate Moab the besieged king sacrifices his heir on the wall and Israel withdraws.
A prophet's widow faces the enslavement of her sons for debt. At Elisha's direction her small supply of oil fills every borrowed vessel, enabling her to pay the creditor and support her household.

events.title: Judah Is Delivered from a Coalition Army

meta.description: Faced with Moabite, Ammonite, and allied forces, Jehoshaphat proclaims a fast and leads Judah in prayer at the temple. A prophetic message directs them to march without fighting, and singers lead the procession before the enemy coalition destroys itself.

A woman at Shunem provides Elisha a room and later bears the son he foretells. When the child suddenly dies, she seeks the prophet at Carmel, and Elisha returns to stretch himself over the boy until life returns.
During famine Elisha renders a poisoned stew harmless for the prophetic company. He then distributes a modest gift of firstfruits among a hundred people, and food remains after all have eaten.

Jehoshaphat's generally faithful reign remains incomplete because high places persist. After he partners with Israel's Ahaziah to build trading ships, a prophet condemns the alliance and the fleet is wrecked before sailing.

events.title: Naaman Is Healed in the Jordan

meta.description: Naaman, commander of Aram's army, comes to Israel seeking relief from a skin disease. After resisting Elisha's simple direction, he washes seven times in the Jordan, is healed, and acknowledges Israel's God while Elisha refuses payment.

events.title: Gehazi Is Punished for Taking Naaman's Gifts

meta.description: Gehazi secretly pursues Naaman and obtains silver and clothing by inventing a request from Elisha. When he conceals the act, Elisha exposes his greed and Naaman's disease comes upon him.
Jehoram rules Judah in alliance with Ahab's house and follows its practices. Edom and Libnah revolt during his reign, but Judah's Davidic dynasty is preserved and his son Ahaziah succeeds him.

events.title: Jehoram Secures His Throne by Bloodshed

meta.description: Jehoram kills his brothers and some officials after becoming king and follows the practices of Ahab's house. Edom and Libnah revolt during his reign, while he promotes illicit worship in Judah.

events.title: Elisha Recovers a Borrowed Axe Head

meta.description: While the prophetic community cuts timber beside the Jordan, a borrowed iron axe head falls into the water. Elisha causes it to rise to the surface so its borrower can retrieve it.

events.title: Elisha Leads the Arameans into Samaria

meta.description: Elisha repeatedly reveals Aramean military plans and is surrounded at Dothan. The attacking force is struck with impaired sight and led into Samaria, where Elisha persuades Israel's king to feed and release the captives rather than kill them.

events.title: The Siege and Famine of Samaria End

meta.description: Ben-hadad's siege produces desperate famine in Samaria, and the king blames Elisha. The Arameans abandon their camp after hearing an imagined army, four outcasts discover the flight, and the city's food supply is restored as Elisha predicted.

A letter from Elijah announces judgment for Jehoram's idolatry and murder of his brothers. Philistine and Arab raiders carry off his household, and after two years of painful disease he dies without honor.

After living in Philistia through a seven-year famine foretold by Elisha, the Shunammite woman returns to petition for her property. Her arrival coincides with Gehazi recounting her son's restoration, and the king orders her land and revenues returned.

events.title: Hazael Kills Ben-hadad and Becomes King

meta.description: At Damascus Elisha tells Hazael that Ben-hadad's illness is survivable but that the king will nevertheless die, and he weeps over the harm Hazael will bring Israel. Hazael suffocates Ben-hadad the next day and succeeds him.
Ahaziah of Judah joins Joram of Israel in battle against Hazael at Ramoth-gilead. Joram is wounded and returns to Jezreel, where Ahaziah visits him.
Elisha sends a young prophet to anoint the commander Jehu at Ramoth-gilead and commission him against Ahab's dynasty. Jehu's fellow officers spread their garments before him and proclaim him king.
Jehu races to Jezreel and confronts the wounded Joram and his ally Ahaziah. He kills Joram on Naboth's former property and his forces fatally wound Ahaziah as the Judean king flees.
As Jehu enters Jezreel, palace eunuchs throw Jezebel from a window at his command. Horses trample her, and dogs consume most of her body before burial can be arranged, fulfilling Elijah's judgment.

Jehu challenges Samaria's guardians to defend Ahab's seventy sons, and they instead execute the princes and send their heads to Jezreel. Jehu also kills Ahab's remaining supporters and relatives of Ahaziah on his way to Samaria.

events.title: Jehu Destroys Baal Worship in Israel

meta.description: Pretending great devotion to Baal, Jehu gathers the cult's worshipers into its temple and has them killed. The temple is demolished, though Jehu retains Jeroboam's calf shrines, and Hazael begins cutting away Israelite territory during his reign.
After Ahaziah's death, Athaliah attempts to destroy the royal family and rules Judah for six years. Jehosheba secretly rescues the infant Joash and hides him with his nurse in the temple.

events.title: Ahaziah Is Killed during Jehu's Revolt

meta.description: Guided by Ahab's family, Ahaziah joins Joram of Israel in war and later visits him while he recovers. The visit brings Ahaziah into Jehu's purge, and he is captured and killed.
Athaliah seizes power and attempts to destroy Judah's royal family. Jehoshabeath rescues the infant Joash and hides him with his nurse in the temple for six years.

events.title: Joash Is Crowned and Athaliah Is Killed

meta.description: In Joash's seventh year Jehoiada organizes guards around the hidden heir, crowns him, and renews covenant commitments among king and people. Athaliah is seized and killed, and the people destroy Baal's temple before seating Joash on the throne.

events.title: Joash Is Crowned and Athaliah Is Killed

meta.description: In Athaliah's seventh year, Jehoiada organizes priests, Levites, commanders, and family heads to guard and crown Joash at the temple. Athaliah discovers the coronation and is taken outside the sanctuary and executed.
Jehoiada binds king and people to renewed covenant loyalty. The people tear down Baal's temple, kill its priest, restore ordered service at the temple, and install Joash on the royal throne.
Joash directs priests and Levites to repair damage done under Athaliah. When collection lags, a public chest produces abundant funds for artisans, restoration, and new sacred vessels.

Jehoahaz continues Jeroboam's religious practices, and Hazael and Ben-hadad reduce Israel's army to a small remnant. When Jehoahaz seeks the LORD, Israel receives relief from Aramean domination, though its idolatry persists.

When earlier collection methods fail to repair the temple, Joash and Jehoiada establish a chest for contributions. The money is weighed and paid directly to trustworthy supervisors and craftsmen who restore the building.

events.title: Joash Pays Hazael to Spare Jerusalem

meta.description: After capturing Gath, Hazael turns toward Jerusalem. Joash sends him sacred gifts and treasury wealth to avert the attack, and later two royal servants assassinate Joash.
After Jehoiada dies, Joash yields to officials who abandon temple worship for idols. When Jehoiada's son Zechariah publicly warns the people, they stone him in the temple court at the king's command.

events.title: Elisha Gives Joash a Final Prophecy

meta.description: As Elisha lies dying, Joash of Israel visits him and is promised victories over Aram. Because Joash strikes the ground only three times, Elisha says the victories will be limited; after Elisha's death, contact with his bones revives a dead man.

events.title: Aram Invades and Joash Is Assassinated

meta.description: A small Aramean force defeats Judah, destroys its officials, and leaves Joash badly wounded. His servants then kill him because of Zechariah's blood, and he is denied burial in the royal tombs.
After Hazael's death, Joash defeats Ben-hadad three times and recovers towns that Aram had taken from Jehoahaz, matching Elisha's final prediction.

Jeroboam II continues the northern kingdom's established sins but recovers Israelite territory from Lebo-hamath to the Dead Sea. This restoration fulfills a word delivered through the prophet Jonah amid Israel's severe distress.

events.title: Azariah Reigns while Afflicted with Disease

meta.description: Azariah rules Judah for fifty-two years and generally follows his father's faithful course, though the high places remain. A lasting skin disease confines him to a separate house while his son Jotham governs the palace and people.
Amaziah executes the servants who killed his father but spares their children in accordance with the law of Moses. He defeats Edom in the Valley of Salt and captures Sela.

Emboldened by victory over Edom, Amaziah challenges Joash of Israel despite a warning against pride. Judah is routed, Jerusalem's wall is breached, and Joash carries temple and palace treasures to Samaria; Amaziah is later killed in a conspiracy.
Amaziah dismisses hired Israelite soldiers at a prophet's instruction and leads Judah to victory over Edom in the Valley of Salt. The discharged troops retaliate by raiding towns in Judah.
Returning from victory, Amaziah installs and worships the defeated Edomites' gods. He silences a prophet who challenges this act and is warned that his refusal has fixed his downfall.

Amaziah challenges Joash of Israel despite a warning against pride. Judah is routed, Jerusalem's wall is breached, temple and palace treasures are seized, and Amaziah is eventually killed by conspirators after fleeing to Lachish.
Uzziah seeks God during Zechariah's lifetime and prospers in war, agriculture, construction, and military organization. His fame spreads as he fortifies Jerusalem and equips a powerful army.
The LORD directs Jonah son of Amittai to warn Nineveh about its wickedness. Jonah instead travels to Joppa, pays passage on a ship bound for Tarshish, and attempts to flee in the opposite direction.

A violent storm threatens to break apart the ship while Jonah sleeps below deck. The frightened sailors cast cargo overboard and then cast lots, which identify Jonah after he admits that he is fleeing the God who made sea and land.

events.title: Jonah Is Thrown into the Sea

meta.description: The sailors initially struggle to row back to land rather than harm Jonah, but finally throw him overboard at his direction. The sea becomes calm, the sailors sacrifice to the LORD, and a great fish swallows Jonah for three days and nights.

From inside the fish Jonah gives thanks for being heard in mortal distress and recalls sinking into the deep before his life was rescued. The LORD then directs the fish to release Jonah onto dry land.

Called a second time, Jonah travels to the vast city of Nineveh and announces its overthrow in forty days. The people believe God and proclaim a fast, with residents of every rank putting on sackcloth.
Nineveh's king leaves his throne for sackcloth and ashes and orders a citywide fast for people and animals. When the city turns from its violence, God does not bring the announced calamity.

Jonah resents Nineveh's deliverance and explains that his expectation of divine compassion motivated his flight. He asks to die, then builds a shelter east of the city and waits to see what will happen.

events.title: The Bush and Worm Expose Jonah's Priorities

meta.description: God provides a bush to shade Jonah, then a worm and hot east wind that destroy the plant and leave him faint. Jonah's grief over the short-lived bush becomes the occasion for contrasting his concern with God's compassion for Nineveh's vast population and animals.
Shallum publicly assassinates Zechariah after a six-month reign, ending Jehu's dynasty in its fourth generation. One month later Menahem kills Shallum and takes Israel's throne.
Menahem secures power with brutal violence and continues Israel's idolatry. When Pul of Assyria invades, Menahem taxes the wealthy to pay a large tribute and obtain imperial support for his rule.
Jotham follows a faithful course while leaving the high places in use and builds the temple's upper gate. Late in his reign Aram and Israel begin pressuring Judah.

Made proud by strength, Uzziah enters the temple to burn incense despite the priests' opposition. A skin disease appears on his forehead, and he lives in isolation while Jotham governs until his death.
Jotham governs faithfully without intruding into the temple, though the people remain corrupt. He expands defenses, defeats Ammon, and grows powerful through his ordered conduct before God.

The officer Pekah assassinates Pekahiah in Samaria and seizes the northern throne. During Pekah's reign Tiglath-pileser captures much of northern Israel and deports its inhabitants before Hoshea kills Pekah.
Ahaz rejects the pattern of David and adopts the religious practices of surrounding nations. He even offers his son by fire and sacrifices throughout the high places.

events.title: Ahaz Leads Judah into Idolatry and Defeat

meta.description: Ahaz promotes images, Baal worship, and child sacrifice. Aram and Israel inflict severe losses on Judah and carry away many captives as the kingdom suffers for its abandonment of God.

events.title: Ahaz Appeals to Assyria against Aram and Israel

meta.description: When Rezin and Pekah attack Jerusalem, Ahaz sends temple and palace treasure to Tiglath-pileser and submits to Assyria. The Assyrian king captures Damascus, deports its population, and kills Rezin.

The Reubenites, Gadites, and eastern half of Manasseh abandon Israel's God for the gods of neighboring peoples. Assyria carries them away to settlements in the empire, ending their occupation east of the Jordan.

The prophet Oded confronts Israel's returning army and warns against enslaving their Judean kindred. Ephraimite leaders support him, and the captives are clothed, fed, treated, and escorted to Jericho.

Ahaz sends Uriah the priest a model of an altar he sees in Damascus and has it installed before he returns. He shifts temple offerings to the new altar and alters other furnishings in deference to Assyria.

Under attack from Edom and Philistia, Ahaz asks Assyria for help, but the alliance brings distress rather than rescue. He plunders and closes the temple, multiplies foreign altars, and dies without burial in the royal tombs.
Hoshea initially pays tribute to Assyria but secretly seeks Egyptian support and withholds payment. The Assyrian king imprisons him and begins a three-year siege of Samaria.

events.title: Samaria Falls and Israel Is Exiled

meta.description: Assyria captures Samaria and deports Israel's population to imperial territories. The narrator traces the northern kingdom's fall to persistent idolatry, rejection of prophetic warnings, and abandonment of the covenant.

The Assyrian king settles people from several conquered regions in Samaria. After lion attacks, an exiled Israelite priest teaches them local worship, but the communities combine reverence for the LORD with service to their ancestral gods.

events.title: Hezekiah Cleanses and Reopens the Temple

meta.description: In his first year Hezekiah summons priests and Levites to remove defilement from the closed temple. After sixteen days of cleansing, sacrifices, music, and congregational worship restore its service.

Because the temple was not ready in the first month, Hezekiah invites Judah and the northern remnant to a second-month Passover. Some mock the couriers, but a great assembly comes to Jerusalem, removes illicit altars, celebrates for two weeks, and receives priestly blessing.

Hezekiah removes high places, breaks sacred pillars, cuts down the Asherah, and destroys the bronze serpent that had become an object of offerings. He resists Assyria and wins successes against the Philistines.

events.title: Simeonite Clans Expand in Hezekiah's Reign

meta.description: Simeonite leaders seek pasture near Gedor during Hezekiah's reign, defeat the inhabitants, and settle their land. Another group moves to Mount Seir and destroys a surviving Amalekite community there.

The worshipers destroy unauthorized cult sites throughout Judah and neighboring territories. Hezekiah reestablishes priestly and Levitical divisions, and abundant contributions are carefully administered for temple servants and their families.

Isaiah tells the gravely ill Hezekiah to prepare for death, but the king prays and weeps. He receives a promise of fifteen additional years, recovers after a fig poultice is applied, and sees the shadow retreat as a confirming sign.

events.title: Hezekiah Shows His Treasures to Babylon

meta.description: Hezekiah welcomes Babylonian envoys and displays all the wealth and armaments of his kingdom. Isaiah announces that the treasures and some royal descendants will eventually be carried to Babylon.
Sennacherib captures Judah's fortified cities in Hezekiah's fourteenth year. Hezekiah submits and strips silver and gold from the temple and palace to meet the Assyrian king's demanded payment.

Assyrian officers confront Hezekiah's delegation at Jerusalem and publicly ridicule reliance on Egypt, Hezekiah, or the LORD. Speaking where the people can hear, the Rabshakeh urges surrender and promises deportation to another productive land.

Hezekiah mourns the Assyrian threats and sends officials to consult Isaiah, who promises that the invader will withdraw. After receiving a further threatening letter, Hezekiah spreads it before the LORD in the temple and prays for deliverance.

Isaiah announces that Assyria's arrogance will be rebuked and Jerusalem preserved for David's sake. An angel strikes the Assyrian camp, Sennacherib returns to Nineveh, and years later his sons assassinate him.

Sennacherib invades Judah and besieges its fortified cities, while Hezekiah blocks outside water, repairs Jerusalem's defenses, and encourages the people. Assyrian envoys mock Hezekiah's trust and compare Judah's God to conquered nations' gods.
Hezekiah and Isaiah pray in response to the Assyrian threats. An angel destroys the invading army's leaders, Sennacherib returns home in disgrace, and many nations thereafter honor Judah's king.

Hezekiah becomes gravely ill, prays, and receives both healing and a sign. His pride later provokes wrath, but he and Jerusalem humble themselves, and he dies after years of wealth, building, and honor.

events.title: Manasseh Fills Judah with Idolatry and Bloodshed

meta.description: Manasseh reverses Hezekiah's reforms, rebuilds high places, installs foreign worship in the temple, practices divination, and sheds much innocent blood. Prophets announce that Jerusalem will suffer disaster like Samaria because Judah has surpassed the nations in evil.

Manasseh reverses Hezekiah's reforms, promotes occult and foreign worship, places idols in the temple, and sheds innocent blood through child sacrifice. When warnings go unheeded, Assyrian commanders bind him and take him to Babylon.

In distress Manasseh humbles himself and prays, and God restores him to Jerusalem. He fortifies the city, removes foreign gods from the temple, restores its altar, and commands Judah to worship Israel's God.
After two years of continuing Manasseh's idolatry, Amon is killed by servants in his palace. The people execute the conspirators and make his young son Josiah king.
Amon follows Manasseh's earlier idolatry without sharing his later humility. His servants assassinate him after two years, but the people kill the conspirators and make Josiah king.

Josiah begins seeking God in his eighth year and four years later destroys unauthorized altars, images, and cult objects. His purge extends beyond Judah into territories of the former northern kingdom.
Josiah assigns priests and Levites their duties and supplies offerings for a national Passover at Jerusalem. The carefully ordered celebration surpasses every Passover since Samuel's time.

events.title: The Book of the Law Is Found

meta.description: In Josiah's eighteenth year, temple repairs are funded through collected offerings. Hilkiah finds the book of the law, Shaphan reads it to the king, and Josiah tears his clothes upon realizing Judah's failure to obey it.
Josiah's delegation consults the prophet Huldah about the discovered book. She confirms that Jerusalem faces disaster for its idolatry but promises that the penitent king will die before seeing it.
Josiah gathers Judah's leaders and people at the temple, reads the covenant book publicly, and pledges wholehearted obedience. The assembled people join him in renewing the covenant.

events.title: Josiah Removes Idolatry from Judah and Bethel

meta.description: Josiah removes pagan vessels, priests, images, altars, and shrines from the temple, Jerusalem, and throughout Judah. At Bethel he destroys Jeroboam's altar and preserves the tomb of the prophet who had foretold its desecration.

Josiah commands a Passover in Jerusalem according to the covenant book and removes mediums, household gods, and other forbidden practices. Despite his exceptional reform, judgment on Judah remains because of Manasseh's provocations.

events.title: The Book of the Law Is Found

meta.description: During repairs to the temple, Hilkiah finds the book of the law and Shaphan reads it to Josiah. The king tears his clothes and sends officials to seek divine guidance because Judah has not observed its commands.

events.title: Huldah's Oracle Leads to Covenant Renewal

meta.description: Huldah announces unavoidable judgment on Jerusalem but promises Josiah will not witness it because he humbled himself. Josiah gathers the people, reads the covenant book, renews the covenant, and removes idolatrous objects from Israelite territory.
Josiah goes to meet Pharaoh Neco as the Egyptian army moves toward the Euphrates. Neco kills him at Megiddo, and Josiah's servants return his body to Jerusalem for burial.

events.title: Jehoahaz Is Deposed by Pharaoh Neco

meta.description: After only three months as king, Jehoahaz is confined by Pharaoh Neco and taken to Egypt. Neco imposes tribute and installs Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim, renaming him Jehoiakim.
Josiah intercepts Pharaoh Neco despite the Egyptian king's warning and enters battle in disguise at Megiddo. Archers mortally wound him, Judah mourns, and Jeremiah composes a lament.
The people make Josiah's son Jehoahaz king, but his reign lasts only three months. Pharaoh Neco removes him, imposes tribute, takes him to Egypt, and installs his brother Jehoiakim.

events.title: Jehoiakim Serves and Rebels against Babylon

meta.description: Jehoiakim rules under foreign pressure, serving Nebuchadnezzar for three years before rebelling. Babylonian and allied raiders then attack Judah, whose destruction is attributed to Manasseh's violence and sins.
Jehoiakim rules wickedly until Nebuchadnezzar attacks and binds him for removal to Babylon. The Babylonian king also carries temple vessels to his palace.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar Besieges Jerusalem and Takes Exiles

meta.description: In Jehoiakim's third year, Nebuchadnezzar besieges Jerusalem and carries temple vessels to Babylon. Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah are selected from the Judean elite for three years of court education and receive Babylonian names.

events.title: Daniel and His Companions Undertake a Food Test

meta.description: Daniel obtains permission for the four Judeans to eat vegetables and drink water for ten days rather than consume the royal provisions. Their condition satisfies the guard, and they continue their diet while gaining knowledge and skill.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar Demands His Dream Be Revealed

meta.description: In Nebuchadnezzar's second year, a troubling dream leads him to demand both its content and interpretation from Babylon's experts. When they cannot comply, he orders the wise men killed, but Daniel secures time to seek an answer.

events.title: The Mystery Is Revealed to Daniel

meta.description: Daniel and his companions seek divine mercy concerning the king's demand. The mystery is disclosed to Daniel in a night vision, and he asks Arioch to spare the wise men and bring him before the king.

Daniel recounts a dream of a statue composed of successive materials and a stone that destroys it and fills the earth. He explains the image as a sequence of kingdoms ultimately displaced by an enduring kingdom established by God.

events.title: Daniel and His Companions Are Promoted

meta.description: Nebuchadnezzar honors Daniel with gifts and authority over the province and its wise men. At Daniel's request, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego receive provincial appointments while Daniel remains at court.

events.title: The Four Judeans Enter Royal Service

meta.description: At the end of their appointed education, the king examines the young men and finds Daniel and his three companions preeminent. They are stationed at court, where their wisdom surpasses that of the royal experts.

Nebuchadnezzar gathers imperial officials to dedicate a great golden statue on the plain of Dura and commands worship under threat of death. Chaldean officials accuse Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego of refusing to comply.
