events.title: The Three Judeans Are Delivered from the Furnace

meta.description: The three men refuse the king's demand and are cast into an overheated furnace. Nebuchadnezzar sees them walking unharmed with a fourth figure, then calls them out, acknowledges their deliverance, protects their worship, and promotes them.

After a three-month reign, Jehoiachin surrenders Jerusalem to Nebuchadnezzar. Babylon carries away the king, court, warriors, artisans, and temple and palace treasures, then installs his uncle Mattaniah under the name Zedekiah.
After a reign of three months and ten days, Jehoiachin is taken to Babylon in the spring along with precious temple vessels. Nebuchadnezzar appoints Zedekiah over Judah and Jerusalem.

events.title: Zedekiah Rebels and Judah Rejects the Prophets

meta.description: Zedekiah refuses to humble himself before Jeremiah and breaks his sworn loyalty to Nebuchadnezzar. Priests and people defile the temple and repeatedly mock God's messengers until judgment can no longer be delayed.

After Zedekiah rebels, Nebuchadnezzar surrounds Jerusalem with siegeworks until famine overwhelms the city. Zedekiah flees through a breach but is captured near Jericho, sees his sons killed, is blinded, and is taken to Babylon.

events.title: Jerusalem Is Destroyed and Judah Exiled

meta.description: Babylonian forces kill inhabitants, plunder the temple and royal treasures, burn the sanctuary and palaces, and break down Jerusalem's wall. Survivors are taken to Babylon, and the land lies desolate until Persian rule.

events.title: Jerusalem and the Temple Are Burned

meta.description: Nebuzaradan burns the temple, palace, and major houses, breaks Jerusalem's walls, and deports most survivors. Temple bronze and vessels are taken to Babylon, leading officials are executed at Riblah, and Judah goes into exile.

Babylon appoints Gedaliah governor over those remaining in Judah, and he urges military leaders to settle peacefully under imperial rule. Ishmael assassinates him at Mizpah, after which the surviving leaders and people flee to Egypt.

Nebuchadnezzar dreams of a vast tree cut down at a heavenly decree, with its stump left in the earth. Daniel identifies the tree with the king and warns that he will lose human society and royal power until he acknowledges divine sovereignty.
Twelve months after the dream, Nebuchadnezzar boasts over Babylon and immediately loses his kingdom and ordinary human life. He lives outdoors and eats grass as the announced judgment takes effect.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar's Reason and Kingdom Are Restored

meta.description: At the close of the appointed period, Nebuchadnezzar's reason returns as he acknowledges the sovereignty of the Most High. His officials receive him again, his kingdom is restored, and he publicly recounts his humbling.

In Jehoiachin's thirty-seventh year of exile, Evil-merodach releases him from prison. The former Judean king receives an honored place at the Babylonian court and a regular allowance for the rest of his life.

events.title: Daniel Sees Four Beasts and the Heavenly Court

meta.description: In Belshazzar's first year, Daniel dreams of four beasts arising from the sea, followed by a heavenly judgment and the grant of lasting dominion to a humanlike figure. An attendant explains the beasts as kingdoms and promises that the holy ones will finally receive the kingdom.

events.title: Daniel Sees the Ram and the Goat

meta.description: In Belshazzar's third year, Daniel sees a two-horned ram overcome by a swift goat whose great horn gives way to four others. Gabriel identifies the empires represented and explains the rise of a destructive ruler who attacks the sanctuary before being broken.

Belshazzar holds a great feast and uses vessels taken from the Jerusalem temple while honoring Babylonian gods. A hand writes on the palace wall, terrifying the king, and the queen directs him to summon Daniel when the court experts cannot explain it.

events.title: Daniel Interprets the Writing and Babylon Falls

meta.description: Daniel rebukes Belshazzar's pride and explains that the writing announces the end and division of his kingdom. Daniel is elevated to third rank, but Belshazzar is killed that night and Darius the Mede receives the realm.

After Judah's Babylonian exile, Israelites, priests, Levites, and temple servants again live in their towns and in Jerusalem. The record identifies leading families and describes the renewed duties of priests, gatekeepers, singers, and other sanctuary workers.
In his first year over Babylon, Cyrus of Persia issues a realm-wide proclamation authorizing the temple's reconstruction in Jerusalem. He invites members of God's people to return to Judah.

events.title: Cyrus Authorizes the Return and Rebuilding

meta.description: In his first year over Babylon, Cyrus issues an empire-wide proclamation permitting the people of the LORD to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple. Their neighbors are instructed to assist with goods, animals, and offerings.

The families of Judah and Benjamin, priests, and Levites prepare to return with gifts from their neighbors. Cyrus releases thousands of gold and silver temple vessels taken by Nebuchadnezzar and entrusts them to Sheshbazzar.

events.title: Officials Entrap Daniel with a Prayer Ban

meta.description: Darius appoints Daniel among the kingdom's chief administrators and considers placing him over the whole realm. Rival officials induce the king to prohibit petitions to anyone but himself for thirty days, then accuse Daniel when he continues his regular prayers.

events.title: Daniel Is Delivered from the Lions

meta.description: Darius reluctantly has Daniel sealed in a lions' den, but finds him unharmed the next morning. The king punishes Daniel's accusers, decrees reverence for Daniel's God, and Daniel prospers into the reign of Cyrus.

In the first year of Darius, Daniel studies Jeremiah's reference to seventy years of Jerusalem's desolation. He fasts, confesses the sins of Israel, and petitions for mercy upon Jerusalem and its ruined sanctuary.

Gabriel comes while Daniel is praying and gives him a timetable concerning his people and holy city. The message describes Jerusalem's rebuilding, an anointed figure, renewed destruction, and a final desolation.

events.title: The First Returnees Settle in Their Towns

meta.description: A register records the families, townspeople, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, temple servants, and others who return with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. The assembly contributes to the temple fund and settles throughout Jerusalem and Judah.

In the seventh month the returned community gathers at Jerusalem, rebuilds the altar on its foundation, and resumes morning and evening offerings. They keep the festival of booths and contract for cedar from Lebanon before the temple foundation is laid.

events.title: Neighboring Peoples Obstruct the Temple Work

meta.description: Zerubbabel and Israel's leaders refuse an offer of partnership from neighboring peoples, insisting that the returned community alone will carry out Cyrus's command. Opponents then intimidate the builders and bribe officials until work ceases through the early reign of Darius.

events.title: Daniel Receives a Vision beside the Tigris

meta.description: In Cyrus's third year, after three weeks of mourning, Daniel sees a radiant figure beside the Tigris on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. A heavenly messenger strengthens him and explains that spiritual opposition delayed his arrival.

events.title: The Messenger Reveals Conflicts of Future Kings

meta.description: The messenger describes coming Persian and Greek rulers, struggles between northern and southern kingdoms, and the campaigns of rulers associated with Antiochus. The revelation culminates in persecution of the covenant people and the oppressor's downfall.

The vision closes with a time of unparalleled distress, deliverance for Daniel's people, and the awakening of the dead to differing destinies. Daniel hears measured periods for the ordeal, is told to seal the words, and receives assurance that he will rest and rise at the appointed end.

events.title: The Second Temple Foundation Is Laid

meta.description: In the second year after the return, Zerubbabel and Jeshua appoint Levites to supervise construction. At the laying of the foundation, younger worshipers shout for joy while elders who remember the former temple weep aloud.

Encouraged by Haggai and Zechariah, Zerubbabel and Jeshua resume building. Governor Tattenai investigates but allows work to continue while asking Darius to verify the builders' appeal to Cyrus's original decree.

events.title: Darius Confirms Support for the Temple

meta.description: A search at Ecbatana locates Cyrus's decree. Darius orders Tattenai not only to leave the work undisturbed but to pay construction and sacrificial expenses from provincial revenue and threatens anyone who alters the edict.

events.title: The Second Temple Is Completed and Dedicated

meta.description: The elders prosper under prophetic encouragement and complete the temple in Darius's sixth year. The returned exiles dedicate it joyfully with sacrifices for all twelve tribes and organize priests and Levites for its service.
The purified priests and Levites prepare the Passover for the returned exiles and those who have joined them in worship. The community follows it with seven joyful days of unleavened bread.

events.title: Ahasuerus Displays His Wealth at Susa

meta.description: In the third year of his reign, Ahasuerus hosts officials, military leaders, and provincial nobles for an extended display of imperial wealth. He follows it with a seven-day banquet for Susa while Vashti separately entertains the women of the palace.

Vashti refuses the king's summons during the banquet. On his advisers' counsel, Ahasuerus bars her from his presence and circulates a decree throughout the empire concerning authority within each household.

events.title: Young Women Are Gathered for the King

meta.description: The king's attendants organize a search for a new queen and gather young women into the royal harem. Esther, an orphan raised by her cousin Mordecai, gains Hegai's favor while concealing her Jewish identity at Mordecai's direction.

Mordecai learns that two royal eunuchs are plotting against Ahasuerus and reports the danger through Esther. The conspirators are executed after an investigation, and Mordecai's service is entered in the royal annals.

After the prescribed year of preparation, Esther is brought to Ahasuerus in the tenth month of his seventh year. The king chooses her as queen and celebrates with a banquet, provincial relief, and royal gifts.

events.title: Haman Plots to Destroy the Jews

meta.description: After his promotion, Haman becomes enraged when Mordecai refuses to honor him and resolves to destroy Mordecai's entire people. In the first month of Ahasuerus's twelfth year, lots designate the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, and Haman gains the king's authority for his plan.

Mordecai and Jewish communities mourn and fast after learning of the decree. Through Hathach, Mordecai urges Esther to plead for her people, and she resolves to approach the king after a three-day fast despite the danger.

events.title: Esther Approaches the King and Hosts a Banquet

meta.description: On the third day Esther enters the inner court without a summons, and the king receives her favorably. She invites Ahasuerus and Haman to a banquet, then asks them to attend a second banquet where she will present her petition.

Royal secretaries prepare Haman's decree in the languages of the empire, ordering the annihilation of the Jews and seizure of their goods on the appointed day. Couriers carry the sealed command from Susa, leaving the city in confusion.

events.title: Haman Prepares a Gallows for Mordecai

meta.description: Haman leaves Esther's banquet elated but is again enraged by Mordecai's refusal to honor him. At the urging of his wife and friends, he erects a high gallows and plans to seek Mordecai's execution before the next banquet.

During a sleepless night, Ahasuerus hears from the annals that Mordecai's loyal service was never rewarded. Haman arrives seeking Mordecai's death but is instead ordered to robe him and lead him publicly through Susa in royal honor.

events.title: Esther Exposes Haman and Haman Is Executed

meta.description: At her second banquet, Esther reveals her Jewish identity and identifies Haman as the author of the threat against her people. The enraged king orders Haman executed on the gallows prepared for Mordecai.
Ahasuerus gives Haman's estate to Esther, who discloses her relationship to Mordecai. The king transfers the royal signet ring to Mordecai, and Esther appoints him over Haman's property.

events.title: Mordecai Issues an Edict of Jewish Defense

meta.description: Because the first royal decree cannot be revoked, Esther again petitions the king and receives authority for a countermeasure. Mordecai sends a sealed edict throughout the provinces permitting Jewish communities to assemble and defend themselves on the appointed day.

Mordecai leaves the king in royal attire as Susa celebrates. Across the empire, Jewish communities respond to the decree with feasting and honor, and many among the surrounding peoples identify themselves with the Jews.

Mordecai writes to Jewish communities directing annual observance of the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the twelfth month with feasting, mutual gifts, and aid to the poor. Esther joins him in confirming the practice and its associated fasts in writing.

events.title: Mordecai Serves as Second to Ahasuerus

meta.description: Mordecai rises to a rank second only to Ahasuerus. He uses his standing to seek the welfare of the Jewish people, and his prominence is recorded in the royal annals.

events.title: The Jews Defend Themselves Across the Empire

meta.description: On the day appointed by the decrees, Jewish communities assemble against those seeking their destruction and receive support from provincial officials influenced by Mordecai's power. They prevail throughout the provinces and in Susa but refrain from taking plunder.
At Esther's request, the king permits the Jews in Susa to assemble for a second day and orders Haman's ten sons displayed on the gallows. The Jews again defeat their enemies without taking plunder.

Jews in the provinces rest and feast on the fourteenth day, while those in Susa rest on the fifteenth after their additional day of defense. These differing celebrations shape the observance in villages and in Susa.

In a later account of opposition, provincial officials accuse Jerusalem before Artaxerxes of being historically rebellious and threatening royal revenue. After an archive search, the king orders rebuilding stopped, and the officials enforce the decree by force.

Ezra registers the family leaders and men traveling from Babylon, then camps for three days at the river Ahava. Finding no Levites, he sends leaders to Casiphia and receives Levites and temple servants for the journey.

events.title: The Caravan Fasts and Entrusts the Temple Gifts

meta.description: Ashamed to request a military escort after affirming God's protection, Ezra proclaims a fast for a safe journey. He weighs the silver, gold, and sacred vessels into the care of twelve leading priests until their delivery at Jerusalem.

Artaxerxes authorizes Ezra, a priest and scribe skilled in the law of Moses, to lead willing Israelites to Jerusalem. The decree supplies offerings, exempts temple personnel from taxes, and empowers Ezra to appoint judges and teach the law.

The caravan leaves Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month and arrives safely in Jerusalem. After three days the gifts are counted into temple custody, sacrifices are offered, and the king's commissions are delivered to provincial officials.

Officials report that returned Israelites, including priests and leaders, have intermarried with surrounding peoples. Ezra tears his garments, pulls out hair, and at the evening sacrifice confesses the community's guilt in light of the mercy shown to the remnant.

events.title: The Assembly Meets in Heavy Rain

meta.description: Judah and Benjamin assemble in the temple square trembling from the crisis and heavy rain. Because the cases are too numerous for immediate resolution, officials arrange for towns to appear in turn with their elders and judges.

Ezra and designated family heads examine the cases over three months. The book records priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and other Israelites who pledge to separate from foreign wives, with priestly offenders also presenting guilt offerings.

events.title: The Community Covenants to Address the Marriages

meta.description: A large weeping assembly gathers during Ezra's prayer, and Shecaniah proposes a covenant to send away the foreign wives and their children according to the community's understanding of the law. Ezra makes the leaders swear and summons all returnees to Jerusalem within three days.

The chronicler assembles genealogies from Adam through Israel's tribes, with particular attention to Judah, David's dynasty, Levi, Benjamin, and the families associated with Jerusalem. The record links the restored community with its ancestral, royal, and priestly past.
At Susa in Artaxerxes's twentieth year, Hanani tells Nehemiah that the survivors in Judah are suffering disgrace and that Jerusalem's wall and gates remain ruined.
Nehemiah mourns, fasts, and confesses Israel's sins before God. He appeals to the covenant promise of restoration and asks for favor before the king whom he serves as cupbearer.
The king notices Nehemiah's grief and grants him leave to rebuild Jerusalem. He supplies letters for safe passage and authorizes timber for the city gates, wall, and Nehemiah's residence.
Escorted by royal officers and cavalry, Nehemiah presents the king's letters to the provincial governors and reaches Jerusalem. Sanballat and Tobiah resent his mission on Israel's behalf.

events.title: Nehemiah Inspects the Walls at Night

meta.description: After three days in Jerusalem, Nehemiah secretly surveys the ruined walls and burned gates at night with a small group. He initially conceals his plans from the city's leaders and workers.

Nehemiah tells Jerusalem's leaders of royal support and urges them to end the city's disgrace by rebuilding. The people agree, while Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem mock the project and allege rebellion.

events.title: Families and Guilds Repair the Wall

meta.description: Priests, rulers, artisans, merchants, families, and residents of nearby towns rebuild successive gates and wall sections around Jerusalem. Eliashib and the priests begin at the Sheep Gate, and the assignments continue around the city.
Sanballat and Tobiah ridicule the builders as the wall reaches half its height, then a wider coalition plots an attack. The community responds with prayer and posts a continuous guard.

With workers exhausted and enemies threatening surprise attack, Nehemiah stations armed families at vulnerable places. Work resumes under guard, with laborers carrying weapons and remaining inside Jerusalem overnight.

Families protest that famine, taxation, debt, and enslavement are costing them their land and children. Nehemiah rebukes the nobles for exacting interest and binds them by oath to restore property and cancel their claims.

During twelve years as governor, Nehemiah refuses the customary food allowance because of the people's burden. He supports a large household at his own expense, acquires no land, and continues working on the wall.

The wall is finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul after fifty-two days of work, alarming the surrounding peoples. Tobiah nevertheless maintains influential family ties in Judah and continues sending intimidating letters.

events.title: Ezra Reads the Law to the Assembly

meta.description: The people gather at the Water Gate and ask Ezra to read the law. Levites explain it to the assembly, and the leaders turn the people's weeping into a communal celebration with provisions shared among those in need.

events.title: Nehemiah Refuses the Meetings at Ono

meta.description: Sanballat and Geshem repeatedly invite Nehemiah away from the work and circulate an accusation that he plans to become king. Recognizing their intent to harm and frighten him, Nehemiah refuses to leave Jerusalem.

events.title: The Community Keeps the Festival of Booths

meta.description: After leaders study the law, the returned community builds shelters throughout Jerusalem and observes the seven-day festival with great rejoicing. Ezra reads from the law each day, followed by a solemn assembly.

The Israelites assemble in fasting and mourning, hear the law, and confess their own sins and those of their ancestors. The Levites recount God's care from creation through the patriarchs, exodus, wilderness, conquest, monarchy, exile, and the community's present subjection.
Shemaiah urges Nehemiah to hide inside the temple from an alleged assassination attempt. Nehemiah recognizes that his opponents hired the prophet to frighten him into an act that could discredit him.

With the gates installed, Nehemiah appoints gatekeepers, singers, and Levites, places Hanani and Hananiah over Jerusalem, and establishes strict guarding procedures. He then prepares to register the sparsely populated city.

Nehemiah finds the genealogy of the first return under Zerubbabel and records its families, temple personnel, possessions, and gifts. People lacking proof of descent are restricted from priestly privileges pending a priestly ruling.

Nehemiah, priests, Levites, leaders, and the wider community bind themselves by a written agreement to obey the law. Their commitments address intermarriage, sabbath commerce, debt release, offerings, tithes, and support for temple service.

The leaders settle in Jerusalem, and lots select one in ten of the remaining people to join them, while volunteers are commended. A census records the city's residents and the communities occupied throughout Judah and Benjamin.

events.title: Priestly and Levitical Lines Are Recorded

meta.description: A record traces priests and Levites from the return with Zerubbabel through later high-priestly generations. It also identifies leaders responsible for praise, thanksgiving, and guarding temple storehouses in Nehemiah's time.

Levites and singers gather for the wall's dedication after priests, people, gates, and wall are purified. Two thanksgiving processions circle the wall in opposite directions and meet at the temple for sacrifices and a celebration heard far away.

Officials are appointed over storerooms for contributions, first fruits, and tithes. Judah provides the prescribed portions for priests, Levites, singers, and gatekeepers who conduct the temple service.
In Artaxerxes's thirty-second year, Nehemiah leaves Jerusalem and returns to the royal court. During his absence, Eliashib converts a temple storeroom for the use of his relative Tobiah.

events.title: Nehemiah Expels Tobiah from the Temple Rooms

meta.description: After obtaining leave to return to Jerusalem, Nehemiah discovers Tobiah's quarters in the temple courts. He removes Tobiah's belongings, orders the rooms purified, and restores the sacred vessels and offerings.

events.title: Nehemiah Restores Support for the Levites

meta.description: Nehemiah learns that unpaid Levites and singers have abandoned their posts for their fields. He rebukes the officials, restores the ministers to duty, resumes tithes, and appoints reliable treasurers.

Seeing agricultural work and commerce on the sabbath, Nehemiah rebukes Judah's nobles and closes Jerusalem's gates to merchandise. He posts guards and assigns purified Levites to preserve the weekly rest.

Nehemiah discovers Judeans married to women from neighboring peoples and children unable to speak Judah's language. He confronts the offenders, compels an oath against further marriages, and drives away a high priest's relative allied by marriage to Sanballat.
Nehemiah purifies the community from foreign influence, assigns priests and Levites to their duties, and establishes regular provision for wood offerings and first fruits.

events.title: Alexander Conquers the East and Dies

meta.description: Alexander of Macedon defeats Darius, extends his empire through many lands, and divides his kingdom among leading officers before his death. His successors establish rival dynasties that continue to rule after him.

events.title: Heliodorus Is Sent to Seize the Temple Treasury

meta.description: Simon disputes with the high priest Onias and reports Jerusalem's deposits to the royal governor. Seleucus sends Heliodorus to confiscate the funds despite Onias's explanation that much of the money belongs to widows and orphans.

events.title: Heliodorus Is Repelled from the Treasury

meta.description: Jerusalem prays while Heliodorus approaches the treasury. A terrifying horseman and two young men strike him down; Onias intercedes for his recovery, and Heliodorus returns to the king testifying that the temple is divinely protected.

events.title: Antiochus IV Takes the Seleucid Throne

meta.description: Antiochus Epiphanes, formerly a hostage at Rome, begins his reign in Seleucid year 137.
Jewish advocates of accommodation obtain royal approval for Gentile institutions. They build a gymnasium in Jerusalem, obscure circumcision, and abandon covenantal practices.

After Seleucus dies and Antiochus IV succeeds him, Onias's brother Jason purchases the high priesthood. Jason establishes a gymnasium and promotes Greek civic customs in Jerusalem, drawing priests and young elites away from ancestral practices.

Jason sends money to the games at Tyre, though his envoys redirect it from sacrifice to shipbuilding. During regional maneuvering involving Egypt, Antiochus visits Jerusalem and receives an elaborate welcome before proceeding into Phoenicia.

events.title: Menelaus Supplants Jason as High Priest

meta.description: Three years after Jason's appointment, Menelaus outbids him for the high priesthood while carrying royal payments. Jason flees to Ammon, and Menelaus falls behind on the sums he promised the crown.

Menelaus steals temple vessels and induces the royal deputy Andronicus to lure Onias from sanctuary and kill him. After Jews and Greeks protest, Antiochus orders Andronicus executed at the place of the murder.
Antiochus attacks Ptolemaic Egypt with a large combined force, defeats the Egyptian king, captures fortified cities, and plunders the country.

Lysimachus carries out further thefts from the temple under Menelaus's direction and attacks an angry crowd with armed men. The crowd kills him, but bribery secures Menelaus's acquittal and the execution of Jerusalem's three advocates.

Returning from Egypt in Seleucid year 143, Antiochus enters the sanctuary and carries away its vessels, furnishings, precious metals, and concealed treasures. Bloodshed and public mourning follow throughout Judea.

During Antiochus's second Egyptian campaign, a false report of the king's death prompts Jason to assault Jerusalem and drive Menelaus into the citadel. Jason fails to regain power and again flees, eventually dying in exile.

events.title: Antiochus Sacks Jerusalem and Plunders the Temple

meta.description: Antiochus interprets Jason's attack as a general revolt, storms Jerusalem, massacres and enslaves its inhabitants, and removes the temple vessels and treasury. Apollonius later attacks on a sabbath, while Judas and a small group escape into the wilderness.

events.title: Jerusalem Is Attacked and the Citadel Occupied

meta.description: A royal force enters Jerusalem under false assurances, kills inhabitants, plunders and burns the city, and enslaves families. The occupiers fortify the City of David as a citadel overlooking the sanctuary.

The king orders religious uniformity, prohibits temple worship and Jewish observances, and commands idolatrous sacrifices and practices. Inspectors enforce the decree town by town while faithful families seek refuge.

events.title: Mattathias Begins the Revolt at Modein

meta.description: Mattathias and his five sons reject the enforced sacrifices. He kills both a participant and the royal officer at Modein, tears down the altar, and calls supporters of the law to follow him into the hills.

events.title: Refugees Are Killed on the Sabbath

meta.description: Royal troops attack a community hiding in the wilderness on the Sabbath. The refugees do not resist and are killed with their families, prompting Mattathias's followers to permit defensive fighting on the Sabbath.
Hasideans and other fugitives join Mattathias. The growing force attacks apostate groups, destroys illicit altars, circumcises boys, and restores observance in the countryside.

A royal agent dedicates the Jerusalem temple to Olympian Zeus and prohibits sabbaths, festivals, and public Jewish identity. Jews are compelled to participate in foreign rites, and those who circumcise children or secretly keep the sabbath are killed.
The elderly scribe Eleazar refuses both prohibited food and a plan to pretend compliance. He accepts torture and death so that younger Jews will not be misled by his example.

On the fifteenth of Chislev in Seleucid year 145, an illicit cult object is erected on the altar, and ten days later sacrifice is offered there. Torah scrolls are destroyed and people who retain Jewish practices are executed, though many refuse to abandon the covenant.

events.title: Seven Brothers and Their Mother Are Martyred

meta.description: A mother and her seven sons refuse the king's demand that they eat prohibited meat. The brothers endure torture while affirming confidence in divine restoration and judgment, and their mother encourages the youngest before she too dies.
Judas Maccabeus gathers about six thousand faithful Jews from villages and conducts surprise attacks. His force captures strategic positions, defeats local opponents, and gains a widening reputation.

events.title: Mattathias Dies and Judas Takes Command

meta.description: Before dying in Seleucid year 146, Mattathias exhorts his sons to remain faithful, designates Simon as counselor and Judas as military leader, and is buried at Modein.
Judas succeeds his father and defeats Apollonius's Samaritan force, taking its commander's sword. He then routs Seron's larger army at the ascent of Beth-horon, increasing the revolt's reputation.

Nicanor and Gorgias bring a large army and merchants expecting to buy Jewish captives. Judas divides his smaller force, defeats the invaders, captures the slave purchasers' money, and halts pursuit to observe the sabbath.
Judas's forces defeat troops associated with Timothy and Bacchides, seize strongholds, and distribute plunder among the vulnerable. Nicanor escapes to Antioch after the collapse of his expedition.

events.title: Antiochus Leaves Lysias to Suppress Judea

meta.description: Facing depleted revenues, Antiochus departs for the eastern provinces in Seleucid year 147. He leaves Lysias responsible for the western kingdom, the young prince, and a campaign intended to destroy resistance in Judea.

events.title: Judas Defeats the Royal Army at Emmaus

meta.description: Nicanor and Gorgias bring a large army to Emmaus while merchants gather to purchase captives. Judas evades Gorgias's night attack, strikes the main camp at dawn, and drives the royal troops toward the coastal plain.
In the following year Lysias enters Idumea with a reinforced army. Judas meets him near Beth-zur and inflicts heavy losses, causing Lysias to withdraw to Antioch.

events.title: Royal and Roman Letters Confirm a Settlement

meta.description: Letters dated to the 148th Seleucid year record negotiations by Lysias, permission from Antiochus V for Jewish customs and temple restoration, and Roman support for the settlement. The correspondence grants an amnesty and provides for further consultation.

events.title: Mount Zion and Beth-zur Are Fortified

meta.description: Judas surrounds Mount Zion with walls and towers and stations a guard there. He also fortifies Beth-zur to protect Judea's southern approach.

events.title: Antiochus IV Dies during His Eastern Retreat

meta.description: After being repelled in Persia, Antiochus learns of defeats in Judea and sets out against Jerusalem. A painful illness overtakes him; he promises concessions and restitution, names his son as successor, and dies in a foreign land.

events.title: Antiochus V Eupator Succeeds His Father

meta.description: The young Antiochus V succeeds Antiochus IV, with Lysias governing on his behalf. Ptolemy Macron seeks a just settlement with the Jews but, accused of betrayal by rival courtiers, dies by poison.
Judas attacks Idumean fortresses used to harass Judea. After besiegers accept bribes to release some defenders, Judas executes the collaborators and captures the remaining towers.

events.title: The Temple Is Cleansed and Rededicated

meta.description: Judas appoints priests to cleanse and repair the sanctuary, replace the profaned altar, and restore its furnishings. Beginning on the twenty-fifth of Chislev in Seleucid year 148, the people celebrate the new dedication for eight days and establish an annual observance.

events.title: Judas Purifies and Rededicates the Temple

meta.description: Judas and his followers recover Jerusalem and the temple, remove foreign cult installations, build a new altar, and resume sacrifice after a two-year interruption. Beginning on the twenty-fifth of Chislev, the people celebrate for eight days and establish an annual observance.

events.title: Judas Defeats Timothy and Captures Gazara

meta.description: Timothy advances with mercenaries and cavalry, but Judas defeats his army after a fierce battle. The Jewish force then storms Gazara on the fifth day of its siege and kills Timothy and the fortress commanders.
Lysias invades Judea with a large combined force and presses the fortress at Beth-zur. Judas marches from Jerusalem, routs the royal army, and accepts Lysias's proposal for negotiated terms.

events.title: Judas and Simon Rescue Besieged Jewish Communities

meta.description: After attacks on Jewish communities beyond Judea, Simon campaigns in Galilee while Judas and Jonathan fight through Gilead. They defeat several armies and towns, then escort the threatened populations safely into Judea.

Joseph and Azariah attack Jamnia against Judas's instructions and suffer a severe defeat. Judas later campaigns through Hebron and the Philistine region, destroying pagan altars before returning to Judea.

events.title: Antiochus IV Dies in the East

meta.description: After failing to seize Elymais, Antiochus learns of the reverses in Judea, becomes gravely ill, and dies in Seleucid year 149. Lysias enthrones his young son as Antiochus Eupator.

events.title: Judas Retaliates against Joppa and Jamnia

meta.description: After people at Joppa drown Jewish families whom they invited onto boats, Judas burns the harbor and attacks those responsible. Learning of a similar plan at Jamnia, he burns its harbor and fleet as well.

events.title: Judas Defeats Arab Attackers and Captures Caspin

meta.description: Judas defeats an attacking Arab force and makes peace when the survivors offer aid. His army then assaults the fortified town of Caspin and captures it.

events.title: Judas Pursues Timothy through the Northeast

meta.description: Judas's commanders destroy a garrison left by Timothy, and Judas pursues the larger army toward Carnaim. Timothy is released to secure Jewish hostages, while Judas captures Carnaim and Ephron before peacefully passing through Scythopolis and returning for the festival of weeks.

After the festival of weeks, Judas fights Gorgias's infantry and cavalry. Gorgias escapes an attempted capture, but Judas rallies his weary force and drives the enemy troops away before keeping the sabbath at Adullam.

events.title: Judas Provides an Offering for the Fallen

meta.description: While recovering the Jewish dead, Judas's men discover prohibited cultic tokens beneath their clothing. The army prays, and Judas sends a collection to Jerusalem for a sin offering on behalf of those who fell.

In the 149th Seleucid year, Antiochus V and Lysias invade Judea with a large army. Menelaus joins the expedition, but the king holds him responsible for the unrest and has him executed in a tower filled with ashes.

events.title: Judas Raids the Royal Camp near Modein

meta.description: After three days of communal prayer, Judas camps near Modein and leads selected troops in a predawn assault. They kill many soldiers, strike a leading elephant and its rider, and withdraw after throwing the royal camp into confusion.

events.title: Antiochus V Makes Peace with the Jews

meta.description: The king fails to take Beth-zur by force and negotiates with its defenders. News of Philip's revolt in Antioch leads him to settle with Judas, affirm Jewish rights, honor the sanctuary, and return north despite opposition at Ptolemais.
In Seleucid year 150, Judas surrounds the hostile citadel and constructs siege works. Escapees appeal to Antiochus V, leading the king and Lysias to mobilize a major relief army.

events.title: The Royal Army Wins at Beth-zechariah

meta.description: The royal army advances with war elephants and defeats Judas near Beth-zechariah. Eleazar dies beneath an elephant he attacks, Beth-zur is evacuated, and famine weakens the defenders of the sanctuary.

A rival claim at Antioch prompts Lysias to negotiate. The king permits the Jews to live by their laws, though he subsequently breaks his oath by demolishing Jerusalem's fortifications before returning north.

events.title: Demetrius I Reigns and Installs Alcimus

meta.description: Demetrius escapes from Rome and takes the Seleucid throne in year 151 after Antiochus V and Lysias are killed. He sends Bacchides with Alcimus as high priest; Alcimus violates assurances of peace by killing sixty Hasideans.

events.title: Judas Makes an Alliance with Rome

meta.description: Having learned of Roman power, Judas sends Eupolemus and Jason to negotiate. The Roman senate records a mutual-defense agreement with the Jewish nation and warns Demetrius against further oppression.

events.title: Demetrius I Seizes the Seleucid Throne

meta.description: Three years after Eupator's campaign, Demetrius lands at Tripolis and removes Antiochus V and Lysias. In about the 151st Seleucid year, Alcimus approaches the new king and portrays Judas as the cause of continuing unrest.
Demetrius appoints Nicanor governor of Judea with orders to kill Judas, scatter his forces, and install Alcimus as high priest. Simon encounters Nicanor's army near Dessau but is temporarily checked.

Nicanor hesitates to decide the conflict by battle and negotiates a covenant with Judas. He remains peaceably in Jerusalem, develops a friendship with Judas, and encourages him to establish a household.

events.title: Nicanor Breaks the Covenant and Threatens the Temple

meta.description: Alcimus persuades Demetrius that Nicanor's accord is disloyal, and the king orders Judas sent to Antioch. Judas goes into hiding when Nicanor's behavior changes, after which Nicanor threatens the priests and the recently purified temple.

events.title: Razis Dies rather than Be Captured

meta.description: Nicanor sends more than five hundred soldiers to arrest Razis, a respected Jerusalem elder known for his commitment to Judaism. Surrounded in a tower, Razis takes his own life rather than submit to capture and abuse.

events.title: Judas Encourages His Army with a Vision

meta.description: Nicanor plans a sabbath attack, while Judas prepares his troops to defend the city and sanctuary. Judas recounts a dream in which the former high priest Onias prays for the people and Jeremiah gives him a sword for the coming battle.

After a failed attempt to seize Judas, Nicanor threatens the temple and marches against him. Judas's force defeats and kills Nicanor on the thirteenth of Adar, and the victory becomes an annual commemoration.

Judas's army defeats Nicanor's force and finds Nicanor dead after the battle. His head and arm are displayed at Jerusalem, and the people establish an annual celebration on the thirteenth of Adar, the day before Purim.

Bacchides returns with a large army in the first month of Seleucid year 152. Most of Judas's troops desert before battle at Elasa; Judas attacks with the remaining force and is killed, and his brothers bury him at Modein.
Amid famine and renewed persecution, Judas's supporters choose Jonathan to lead the resistance against Bacchides and local opponents.

events.title: Jonathan Escapes Bacchides across the Jordan

meta.description: Jonathan's group withdraws to the wilderness, avenges the killing of his brother John by the Jambri clan, and fights Bacchides at the Jordan. Jonathan's men swim across the river after inflicting substantial losses.

events.title: Alcimus Dies after Attacking the Temple Court

meta.description: After Bacchides fortifies Judean towns, Alcimus begins demolishing the inner sanctuary wall in the second month of Seleucid year 153. He is suddenly incapacitated and dies, and Bacchides leaves the country for two years.

events.title: Jonathan Forces Bacchides to Make Peace

meta.description: Bacchides returns after local opponents invite him to capture Jonathan. Jonathan and Simon defeat his siege at Bethbasi, after which Bacchides releases captives and withdraws under an oath of peace; Jonathan governs from Michmash.

events.title: Alexander Balas Appoints Jonathan High Priest

meta.description: Alexander Balas challenges Demetrius in Seleucid year 160, and both rivals seek Jonathan's support. Jonathan accepts Alexander's appointment as high priest and wears the sacred vestments at the festival of booths while restoring Jerusalem's defenses.
Alexander's forces defeat Demetrius after a prolonged battle, and Demetrius is killed.

In Seleucid year 162, Ptolemy VI gives his daughter Cleopatra to Alexander in a royal wedding at Ptolemais. Jonathan attends, receives public vindication against his accusers, and is honored as governor and a leading royal friend.

As Demetrius II challenges Alexander in Seleucid year 165, Apollonius provokes Jonathan into battle. Jonathan captures Joppa, survives a cavalry ambush, defeats the enemy near Azotus, and receives Ekron from Alexander.

events.title: Ptolemy VI and Alexander Balas Die

meta.description: Ptolemy seizes the Syrian coastal cities, transfers Cleopatra to Demetrius, and defeats Alexander. Alexander is killed in Arabia and Ptolemy dies soon afterward, leaving Demetrius II king in Seleucid year 167.
While Jonathan besieges Jerusalem's citadel, Demetrius summons him to Ptolemais. Gifts and negotiations secure Jonathan's offices and tax concessions for Judea and three attached districts.

events.title: Jonathan's Troops Save Demetrius in Antioch

meta.description: Jonathan sends three thousand soldiers to help Demetrius suppress an uprising at Antioch. The Jewish troops preserve the king's rule, but Demetrius later breaks his promises and treats Jonathan harshly.

Trypho installs the young Antiochus VI against Demetrius and confirms Jonathan's authority while appointing Simon over the coast. Jonathan secures Gaza, Simon takes Beth-zur, and Jonathan recovers from an ambush near Hazor to rout Demetrius's army.

events.title: Jonathan Renews Roman and Spartan Alliances

meta.description: Jonathan sends envoys to Rome and Sparta to renew formal friendship. His letter appeals to an earlier exchange that treated the Spartans and Jews as related peoples.
Jonathan prevents a night attack near Hamath and pursues the withdrawing enemy beyond the Eleutherus. He and Simon then strengthen Joppa, Jerusalem, and other fortifications.
Trypho lures Jonathan to Ptolemais with promises of territory after persuading him to dismiss most of his army. The gates close behind Jonathan, his escort is killed, and he is taken captive.
With Jonathan captive and invasion threatening, Simon rallies Jerusalem, is acclaimed as leader, completes the city's walls, and secures Joppa.

Trypho demands money and hostages but refuses to release Jonathan after Simon complies. Blocked from aiding Jerusalem's citadel, Trypho withdraws through Gilead and kills Jonathan near Baskama; Simon retrieves and buries his remains at Modein.

events.title: Judean Jews Write to Their Kindred in Egypt

meta.description: In the 169th Seleucid year, Jews in Jerusalem and Judea write to Jewish communities in Egypt during distress associated with Jason's revolt. They report restored worship and urge their recipients to observe the festival in Chislev.

events.title: Demetrius Grants Judea Independence under Simon

meta.description: After Trypho kills Antiochus VI and claims the throne, Simon aligns with Demetrius II. In Seleucid year 170, Demetrius cancels tribute and recognizes Simon's authority, and Judean documents begin dating by Simon's leadership.

events.title: Simon Captures Gazara and Jerusalem's Citadel

meta.description: Simon takes Gazara, removes its idolatrous institutions, and settles observant Jews there. Starvation then forces the Jerusalem citadel to surrender, and on the twenty-third of the second month in Seleucid year 171 its foreign garrison is expelled.
In Seleucid year 172, Demetrius campaigns in Media for support against Trypho. A general of Arsaces defeats him and takes him into captivity.

events.title: The Assembly Appoints Simon Ethnarch and High Priest

meta.description: On the eighteenth of Elul in Seleucid year 172, a national assembly records Simon's achievements and grants him hereditary leadership, military command, and the high priesthood until a trustworthy prophet should arise.

events.title: Rome and Sparta Renew Their Alliances with Simon

meta.description: News of Jonathan's death and Simon's rule reaches Rome and Sparta. Both renew their friendship with Judea, and Simon sends a costly gold shield to Rome to confirm the alliance.
Antiochus VII initially confirms Simon's privileges, including tax relief and local coinage. In Seleucid year 174 he lands with a large force, wins widespread support, and besieges Trypho at Dor.
Numenius returns with a consular letter acknowledging the Jewish alliance and directing Mediterranean rulers not to attack Judea or shelter its enemies.

Antiochus rejects Simon's troops and supplies, demands Joppa, Gazara, and heavy payments, and refuses Simon's counteroffer. He appoints Cendebeus to fortify Kedron and raid Judea while continuing his pursuit of Trypho.
Simon gives command to his sons John and Judas against Cendebeus. John leads the army across a stream, routs the coastal force, and burns its positions before returning safely to Judea.
The narrative closes by directing readers to the annals of John's high priesthood for his subsequent wars, fortifications, and achievements after succeeding his father.

events.title: Simon and Two Sons Are Assassinated at Dok

meta.description: In the eleventh month of Seleucid year 177, Simon's son-in-law Ptolemy hosts him and his sons Mattathias and Judas at Dok near Jericho, then murders them during the banquet. John learns of the plot against him at Gazara and kills the would-be assassins.

events.title: Antiochus Is Killed at the Temple of Nanea

meta.description: A letter to Aristobulus recounts how Antiochus and his companions entered the temple of Nanea in Persia seeking its treasure. The temple priests trapped and killed the party, an account distinct from the book's earlier narrative of Antiochus IV's death.

events.title: Jerusalem Announces the Festival of Purification

meta.description: In the 188th Seleucid year, Jerusalem's leaders invite Egyptian Jews to celebrate the temple's purification. The letter supports the observance with traditions about Nehemiah's altar fire, Jeremiah's concealment of sacred objects, and collections of ancestral writings.

While Zechariah offers incense in the sanctuary, Gabriel announces that Elizabeth will bear a son who will prepare Israel for the Lord. Because Zechariah doubts the message, he is unable to speak until its fulfillment.
Gabriel visits Mary in Nazareth and announces that she will conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear the promised Davidic ruler. Mary accepts the calling despite her initial perplexity.

Mary travels to the Judean hill country, where Elizabeth recognizes the significance of her pregnancy. Mary praises God for overturning human status and remembering the covenant before returning home after about three months.

Elizabeth gives birth, and at the child’s circumcision she and Zechariah insist on the name John. Zechariah’s speech returns, and he prophesies about God’s deliverance and his son’s work of preparation.
Matthew traces Jesus' ancestry through Abraham and David, organizing the generations around Israel's monarchy and Babylonian exile.

events.title: Joseph Receives a Dream About Jesus' Birth

meta.description: When Mary is found to be pregnant, Joseph plans a quiet separation. An angel explains the child's divine conception and mission, so Joseph takes Mary as his wife and names her son Jesus.
Visitors from the East follow a star to Judea, consult Herod's court, and find the child with Mary at Bethlehem. They offer valuable gifts and return home by another route after a warning in a dream.
Warned in a dream that Herod intends to kill the child, Joseph takes Jesus and Mary to Egypt by night. They remain there until Herod's death.

events.title: Herod Kills the Children Around Bethlehem

meta.description: Enraged that the eastern visitors did not return, Herod orders the killing of young boys in Bethlehem and its vicinity according to the timeframe he had learned.
A registration brings Joseph and the pregnant Mary from Nazareth to Bethlehem. Mary gives birth to her firstborn son and places him in a manger because ordinary lodging is unavailable.
Angels announce the child’s birth to shepherds watching nearby flocks. The shepherds find Mary, Joseph, and the infant, spread the news they received, and return praising God.

events.title: Jesus Is Presented in the Temple

meta.description: After Jesus is circumcised and named, his parents present him in Jerusalem according to the law. Simeon and Anna recognize the child’s significance for Israel and the nations, and the family later returns to Nazareth.

John introduces the divine Word as the source of creation, life, and light, then identifies his coming into human life with Jesus Christ. The incarnate Son reveals the unseen God and brings grace and truth.

events.title: Jesus' Family Returns and Settles in Nazareth

meta.description: After Herod's death, Joseph brings the family back to Israel. Fear of Archelaus and another dream lead them away from Judea to Nazareth in Galilee.

events.title: The Boy Jesus Remains in the Temple

meta.description: At age twelve Jesus remains in Jerusalem after Passover while his parents begin traveling home. They find him after three days among the temple teachers, and he then returns obediently to Nazareth and continues to mature.

events.title: John the Baptist Calls Judea to Repentance

meta.description: John preaches in the Judean wilderness and baptizes people confessing their sins in the Jordan. He warns religious leaders to produce the fruit of repentance and announces one who will come with greater power.
Jesus comes from Galilee to be baptized by John in the Jordan. As he emerges, the Spirit descends upon him and a heavenly voice identifies him as God's beloved Son.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness

meta.description: After fasting for forty days and nights, Jesus resists three temptations concerning provision, divine protection, and dominion. The devil departs and angels attend him.
After John's arrest, Jesus moves to Capernaum and begins proclaiming repentance and the nearness of heaven's kingdom throughout Galilee.
Beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus calls Simon Peter and Andrew, then James and John. The four leave their fishing work to follow him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Heals Throughout Galilee

meta.description: Jesus travels through Galilee teaching in synagogues, announcing the kingdom, and healing many illnesses. His reputation spreads beyond the region and large crowds follow him.
John appears in the Judean wilderness calling people to repentance and baptizing them in the Jordan. He announces that a more powerful successor will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptized by John. As he emerges from the water, the Spirit descends upon him and a heavenly voice identifies him as the beloved Son.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness

meta.description: The Spirit drives Jesus into the wilderness for forty days, where Satan tests him among the wild animals and angels attend him.
After John is arrested, Jesus enters Galilee announcing the nearness of God's kingdom and calling for repentance and trust in the good news.
Beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus calls Simon and Andrew, then James and John, away from their fishing work. All four leave their nets and families to follow him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Exorcises at Capernaum

meta.description: Jesus teaches in the Capernaum synagogue with striking authority and commands an unclean spirit to leave a man. News of the encounter spreads throughout Galilee.
Jesus raises Simon's feverish mother-in-law, who resumes serving the household. After sunset the town gathers at the door, and Jesus heals many sick people and casts out demons.

After praying alone, Jesus travels through Galilee preaching in synagogues and expelling demons. He cleanses a man with a skin disease, whose widespread report makes public entry into towns difficult.

events.title: A Paralytic Is Forgiven and Healed

meta.description: Four people lower a paralyzed man through the roof of a crowded Capernaum house. Jesus first declares his sins forgiven and then heals him, answering scribes who question his authority.

events.title: Jesus Calls Levi and Eats with Outcasts

meta.description: Jesus calls Levi from the tax booth and later shares a meal with many tax collectors and sinners. He answers critics by describing his mission as a summons to those who need restoration.

Asked why his disciples do not fast, Jesus compares his presence to a wedding celebration and anticipates a future absence. Images of unshrunk cloth and new wine emphasize the incompatibility of old forms and the new moment.

events.title: The Disciples Pluck Grain on the Sabbath

meta.description: Pharisees challenge the disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath. Jesus appeals to David's need and teaches that the Sabbath serves humanity under the authority of the Son of Man.
In a synagogue Jesus restores a man's withered hand after confronting observers about doing good on the Sabbath. Pharisees and Herodians then begin plotting against him.
Large crowds from Galilee and surrounding regions press toward Jesus because of his healings. He cures many and silences unclean spirits that recognize him.
On a mountain Jesus selects twelve companions to remain with him and to be sent out to preach with authority over demons. Mark names the group, including Judas Iscariot.

events.title: Jesus Answers Charges about His Power

meta.description: Jesus' family seeks to restrain him while Jerusalem scribes attribute his exorcisms to the ruler of demons. Jesus exposes the charge as self-defeating and identifies those who do God's will as his true family.

events.title: John Calls the Jordan Region to Repentance

meta.description: In Tiberius’s fifteenth year John proclaims a baptism of repentance, gives practical ethical directions to crowds, and announces a more powerful successor. Herod later imprisons him after John condemns the ruler’s wrongdoing.

events.title: Jesus Is Baptized and His Ancestry Recounted

meta.description: As Jesus prays after baptism, the Spirit descends and a heavenly voice identifies him as the beloved Son. Luke then traces his ancestry through David and Abraham back to Adam and God.

events.title: Jesus Is Tested in the Wilderness

meta.description: Filled with the Spirit, Jesus spends forty days in the wilderness and resists tests concerning food, political dominion, and a public display of divine protection.

Jesus reads from Isaiah in his hometown synagogue and presents the passage as fulfilled in their hearing. When he recalls prophetic aid given to outsiders, the congregation attempts to kill him, but he escapes.

events.title: Jesus Teaches and Heals at Capernaum

meta.description: Jesus expels a spirit in the synagogue, heals Simon’s feverish mother-in-law, and cures many who gather after sunset. He then departs to proclaim God’s kingdom in other towns.

events.title: A Great Catch Leads Fishermen to Follow Jesus

meta.description: After teaching from Simon’s boat, Jesus directs the fishermen to a catch so large that two boats begin to sink. Simon, James, and John leave their work to follow him and gather people.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses a Leper and Heals a Paralytic

meta.description: Jesus touches and cleanses a man with a skin disease, then forgives and heals a paralyzed man lowered through a roof. The second act provokes questions about his authority to forgive sins.

events.title: Jesus Calls Levi and Answers Critics

meta.description: Levi leaves his tax booth and hosts a banquet for Jesus, prompting criticism over his company. Jesus describes his mission to sinners and uses wedding, garment, and wineskin images to answer a question about fasting.

events.title: John the Baptist Testifies About Jesus

meta.description: Priests and Levites question John about his identity and baptism at Bethany across the Jordan. John denies being the Messiah and identifies Jesus as God's Son, whose mission removes sin and brings the Holy Spirit.

Two of John's disciples follow Jesus, and Andrew brings his brother Simon, whom Jesus renames Peter. Jesus then calls Philip, who brings Nathanael; Nathanael's encounter leads him to recognize Jesus as Israel's king.

events.title: Jesus Turns Water Into Wine at Cana

meta.description: At a wedding in Cana, Jesus directs servants to fill purification jars with water, which becomes wine. This first sign reveals his glory to the disciples, who deepen their trust in him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Character of Kingdom Life

meta.description: On a mountain Jesus teaches his disciples and the crowds about those who receive divine favor amid humility, mercy, peacemaking, persecution, and longing for righteousness. He describes his followers' public vocation through images of salt and light.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Fulfillment of the Law

meta.description: Jesus presents his mission as fulfilling the law and prophets. He applies righteousness to anger, desire, marriage, truthful speech, retaliation, and love for enemies.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Hidden Piety and Prayer

meta.description: Jesus instructs his hearers to give, pray, forgive, and fast for God rather than public admiration. He gives them a pattern of prayer centered on God's holiness, kingdom, provision, forgiveness, and deliverance.

events.title: Jesus Teaches Trust Beyond Possessions and Anxiety

meta.description: Jesus contrasts heavenly treasure with divided service to wealth. He directs his hearers away from anxiety over daily needs and toward trust in the Father's care and pursuit of God's kingdom.

events.title: Jesus Concludes the Sermon With a Call to Obedience

meta.description: Jesus addresses judgment, prayer, treatment of others, false prophets, and the paths leading to life or destruction. He closes by comparing those who act on his teaching to a house built on rock, and the crowds recognize his authority.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses a Leper and Heals a Centurion's Servant

meta.description: Jesus touches and cleanses a man with leprosy, then heals a centurion's paralyzed servant from a distance. He commends the Gentile officer's confidence in his authority.

events.title: Jesus Heals Peter's Mother-in-Law and Many Others

meta.description: At Peter's house Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law, who rises and serves him. That evening he releases many from demons and diseases.

events.title: Jesus Stills a Storm and Frees Two Demoniacs

meta.description: After warning would-be followers about the cost of discipleship, Jesus crosses the lake, rebukes a violent storm, and amazes his companions. On the far shore he drives demons from two men into a herd of pigs, after which the local people ask him to leave.

events.title: Jesus Forgives a Paralytic and Calls Matthew

meta.description: Jesus forgives and heals a paralyzed man despite scribal objections to his authority. He then calls Matthew from the tax booth and shares a meal with tax collectors and sinners.

events.title: Jesus Answers a Question About Fasting

meta.description: Asked why his disciples do not fast like other groups, Jesus compares his presence to a wedding celebration and uses images of new cloth and wine to describe the new situation.

events.title: Jesus Restores a Girl and Heals a Suffering Woman

meta.description: While Jesus goes to a leader's dead daughter, a woman suffering twelve years touches his garment and is healed. Jesus then takes the girl by the hand and raises her.

events.title: Jesus Heals Two Blind Men and a Mute Man

meta.description: Two blind men appeal to Jesus and receive sight, and a demonized man is enabled to speak. The crowds marvel while Pharisees attribute the exorcisms to demonic authority.

events.title: Jesus Sends the Twelve to Israel

meta.description: Moved by the distressed crowds, Jesus appoints and sends twelve disciples to proclaim the kingdom and heal. He instructs them about dependence, rejection, persecution, courage, divided loyalties, and the welcome given to his messengers.

events.title: Jesus Responds to John the Baptist's Messengers

meta.description: From prison John sends disciples to ask about Jesus' identity. Jesus points to his works, then honors John's prophetic role while comparing the generation's rejection of both John's austerity and his own table fellowship.

events.title: Jesus Rebukes Unrepentant Towns and Invites the Weary

meta.description: Jesus denounces towns that witnessed his deeds without repenting, gives thanks for revelation granted to the humble, and invites the burdened to learn his gentle way.

events.title: Jesus Faces Disputes Over the Sabbath

meta.description: Pharisees challenge Jesus when his disciples pluck grain and when he heals a man's withered hand on the Sabbath. Jesus defends mercy and his authority, then withdraws as opponents plan his destruction.

events.title: Jesus Answers Charges About His Power

meta.description: After Jesus heals a demonized man, opponents claim that he works through the ruler of demons. Jesus argues that his exorcisms demonstrate God's kingdom, warns about hardened speech, and gives the sign of Jonah to those demanding a sign.
When his mother and brothers seek him, Jesus points to his disciples and defines his family by doing the will of his heavenly Father.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Parables by the Sea

meta.description: From a boat Jesus teaches a large crowd through parables of soils, a lamp, secretly growing seed, and a mustard seed. He later explains the purpose of parables and the sower's meaning to his disciples.
A violent windstorm threatens the disciples' boat while Jesus sleeps. He stills the wind and sea, then challenges their fear and lack of faith.

In Gentile territory Jesus expels a multitude of demons from a man living among tombs; the spirits enter pigs that rush into the sea. The restored man is sent home to report God's mercy throughout the Decapolis.

events.title: A Woman Is Healed and Jairus's Daughter Raised

meta.description: While Jesus goes to help Jairus's dying daughter, a woman suffering twelve years touches his clothing and is healed. Despite news of the girl's death, Jesus enters her room and restores her to life.
People in Jesus' hometown take offense at the familiar craftsman and his family despite his synagogue teaching. Their unbelief limits his works there, though he heals a few sick people.

events.title: The Twelve Are Sent in Pairs

meta.description: Jesus sends the twelve out two by two with authority over unclean spirits and instructions to travel lightly. They preach repentance, expel demons, and heal the sick.
Herod recalls imprisoning John for condemning his marriage to Herodias. Bound by a banquet oath after Herodias's daughter dances, he orders John beheaded and the disciples bury the body.
The returning apostles withdraw with Jesus, but a large crowd reaches the deserted place first. Jesus teaches them and multiplies five loaves and two fish so that all eat and twelve baskets remain.

After praying alone, Jesus approaches the disciples' struggling boat by walking on the water and the wind ceases when he joins them. At Gennesaret, people bring the sick from across the region and those who touch his cloak are healed.

Pharisees and scribes criticize the disciples' unwashed hands. Jesus condemns traditions that displace God's commands and teaches that harmful intentions arising from within, rather than food entering the body, defile a person.

events.title: A Gentile Woman's Daughter Is Freed

meta.description: In the region of Tyre, a Syrophoenician woman persistently asks Jesus to expel a demon from her daughter. Jesus grants her request, and she finds the child restored at home.

In the Decapolis people bring Jesus a man who cannot hear and speaks with difficulty. Jesus privately restores his hearing and speech, and the astonished crowd spreads the news despite being told not to.
Jesus has compassion on a crowd that has remained with him for three days without food. Seven loaves and a few fish feed four thousand people, with seven baskets left over.

events.title: Jesus Refuses a Sign and Warns the Disciples

meta.description: Jesus refuses the Pharisees' demand for a heavenly sign. In the boat he warns against the influence of the Pharisees and Herod, while the disciples misunderstand him as speaking about their lack of bread.

events.title: A Blind Man at Bethsaida Is Healed in Stages

meta.description: Jesus leads a blind man outside Bethsaida and restores his sight through two acts of healing. Once the man sees clearly, Jesus sends him directly home.

Jesus defends his disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath and declares his authority over the day. On another Sabbath he restores a man’s withered hand while opponents begin considering action against him.

events.title: Jesus Chooses the Twelve and Teaches on a Plain

meta.description: After a night of prayer Jesus names twelve apostles and heals people gathered from a wide region. He teaches about blessings and woes, love of enemies, generosity, judgment, character, and obedience.
Jewish elders appeal to Jesus for a Roman centurion’s gravely ill servant. The officer expresses confidence that Jesus can heal by command from a distance, and the servant recovers.

events.title: Jesus Raises a Widow’s Son at Nain

meta.description: At Nain Jesus encounters the funeral of a widow’s only son. Moved by compassion, he stops the procession and restores the young man to life, prompting widespread reports.

John sends disciples to ask about Jesus’ identity, and Jesus directs them to the healings and proclamation they have witnessed. He then honors John’s prophetic role and exposes the generation’s inconsistent rejection of them both.

events.title: A Woman Anoints Jesus at a Pharisee’s Table

meta.description: At Simon the Pharisee’s meal, a woman known as a sinner washes and anoints Jesus’ feet. Through a story of canceled debts, Jesus contrasts her grateful love with the host’s reception and confirms her forgiveness.
Jesus travels through towns and villages proclaiming God’s kingdom with the twelve. Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Susanna, and other women accompany the group and provide from their resources.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Hearing God’s Word

meta.description: Jesus tells and explains the parable of seed falling on four kinds of ground, then adds instruction about bringing light into view. When his relatives seek him, he defines his family as those who hear and obey God’s word.

events.title: Jesus Calms a Storm and Frees a Gerasene Man

meta.description: Jesus stills a dangerous storm during a lake crossing. On the opposite shore he drives many demons from a tormented man into pigs, and sends the restored man home to report what God has done.

events.title: A Woman Is Healed and Jairus’s Daughter Raised

meta.description: A woman suffering twelve years is healed after touching Jesus while he travels to Jairus’s house. Although word arrives that Jairus’s daughter has died, Jesus restores the girl to life.

events.title: Jesus Clears Commerce From the Temple

meta.description: At Passover Jesus drives merchants and money changers from the temple precincts. Challenged for a sign, he points cryptically to the destruction and raising of his body, an image the disciples understand after his resurrection.

Nicodemus, a Pharisee and Jewish leader, visits Jesus by night. Jesus teaches him about birth through the Spirit, the Son's heavenly origin and coming exaltation, and God's saving purpose for a world divided by its response to the light.

Jesus' disciples baptize in Judea while John continues his work near Salim. When John's followers worry about Jesus' growing audience, John accepts his own diminishing role and renews his witness to the Son's heavenly authority.

events.title: Jesus Speaks With a Samaritan Woman

meta.description: Traveling through Samaria, Jesus speaks with a woman at Jacob's well about living water, her life, true worship, and his identity. Her testimony brings people from Sychar, and many come to believe during Jesus' two-day stay.

events.title: Jesus Heals an Official's Son From Afar

meta.description: At Cana a royal official pleads for his dying son in Capernaum. Jesus assures him that the child will live, and the recovery at that same hour brings the official and his household to faith.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Disabled Man at Beth-zatha

meta.description: During a Jerusalem festival Jesus heals a man who has been disabled for thirty-eight years and tells him to carry his mat. Because the healing occurs on the Sabbath and Jesus describes God as his Father, hostility against him intensifies.

Jesus teaches that the Son acts in unity with the Father and has authority to give life, judge, and raise the dead. He appeals to John's witness, his own works, the Father's testimony, and the writings of Moses against those who refuse him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches the Crowds in Kingdom Parables

meta.description: From a boat Jesus tells parables of soils, weeds, mustard seed, and leaven. He explains that the parables both disclose and conceal the kingdom's growth and mixed reception.

events.title: Jesus Explains the Kingdom to His Disciples

meta.description: In private Jesus explains the weeds and adds parables of hidden treasure, a valuable pearl, and a net. He describes final separation and the responsibility of those instructed for the kingdom.
Jesus teaches in his hometown synagogue, but residents take offense because they know his family and ordinary background. Their unbelief limits the deeds he performs there.
Matthew recounts how Herod imprisoned John for condemning his marriage and then ordered his beheading after a banquet pledge. John's disciples bury him and report the death to Jesus.

Jesus withdraws to a deserted place but compassionately heals the pursuing crowds. With five loaves and two fish he feeds more than five thousand people, and the disciples collect twelve baskets of remnants.

During a night crossing Jesus approaches the disciples' battered boat on the water. Peter briefly walks toward him before faltering, and after Jesus enters the boat the wind stops; healings follow at Gennesaret.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Defilement and Answers a Canaanite Woman

meta.description: Jesus challenges traditions that neglect God's commands and teaches that defiling conduct proceeds from the heart. In the region of Tyre and Sidon, a Canaanite woman's persistent appeal leads to her daughter's healing.

events.title: Jesus Heals Crowds and Feeds Four Thousand

meta.description: On a mountain near the Sea of Galilee Jesus heals many people over three days. He then feeds more than four thousand with seven loaves and a few fish.

After refusing opponents' demand for a sign and warning the disciples about corrupting teaching, Jesus asks who they believe him to be. Peter identifies him as the Messiah and Son of God, and Jesus declares a foundational role for him.

events.title: Jesus First Predicts His Death and Resurrection

meta.description: Jesus begins to tell the disciples that he must suffer, be killed, and rise. He rebukes Peter's resistance and teaches that following him entails self-denial and willingness to lose one's life.

events.title: Jesus Is Transfigured Before Three Disciples

meta.description: Six days later Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where his appearance changes and Moses and Elijah appear. A heavenly voice identifies him as the Son to whom they must listen.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Boy and Provides the Temple Tax

meta.description: Jesus frees a boy whom the disciples could not heal and teaches them about inadequate faith. After again predicting his death and resurrection, he arranges payment of the temple tax without conceding that the sons are obligated.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Life in the Community

meta.description: Jesus uses a child to teach humility, warns against causing others to stumble, and describes seeking the straying member. He also gives procedures for reconciliation and teaches extravagant forgiveness through a parable of an unforgiving servant.
Near Caesarea Philippi, the disciples report public opinions about Jesus. Peter identifies him as the Messiah, and Jesus orders them not to publicize the conclusion.

events.title: Jesus Foretells His Death and Defines Discipleship

meta.description: Jesus teaches that he will be rejected, killed, and rise after three days. He rebukes Peter's resistance and summons the crowd to costly, self-denying discipleship.

Six days later Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a mountain, where his appearance changes and Elijah and Moses appear. A cloud identifies him as the beloved Son, and afterward he discusses Elijah's coming with the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Frees a Boy from a Spirit

meta.description: Jesus returns to find the disciples unable to expel a destructive spirit from a boy. He responds to the father's struggling faith, commands the spirit to leave, and later teaches the disciples about prayer.

While traveling quietly through Galilee, Jesus again predicts his betrayal, death, and resurrection. In Capernaum he counters the disciples' argument about greatness by placing a child among them and teaching humble service.

events.title: Jesus Teaches about Allies and Stumbling

meta.description: Jesus tells the disciples not to stop an outsider who uses his name to expel demons. He warns strongly against causing vulnerable believers or oneself to stumble and urges the group to live at peace.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Judea about Marriage and Children

meta.description: In Judea Jesus answers a test about divorce by appealing to God's purpose in creation and later explains the matter privately. He welcomes children whom the disciples try to turn away and presents them as models for receiving God's kingdom.

A man seeking eternal life tells Jesus he has kept the commandments, but grieves when asked to relinquish his wealth and follow. Jesus teaches the disciples about wealth's danger and God's ability to accomplish what humans cannot.

events.title: Jesus Foretells His Death a Third Time

meta.description: On the road toward Jerusalem, Jesus privately gives the twelve a detailed prediction of his condemnation, abuse, execution by Gentiles, and resurrection after three days.

events.title: James and John Seek Places of Honor

meta.description: James and John ask for prominent positions in Jesus' glory, angering the other disciples. Jesus contrasts domineering rulers with a community in which greatness consists in service and his own life is given for many.
As Jesus leaves Jericho, the blind beggar Bartimaeus repeatedly appeals to him as David's son. Jesus credits his faith, restores his sight, and Bartimaeus follows on the road.

events.title: The Twelve Are Sent and Five Thousand Are Fed

meta.description: Jesus sends the twelve to announce the kingdom and heal with little travel equipment. After their return he welcomes a crowd near Bethsaida and feeds about five thousand men with five loaves and two fish.

events.title: Peter Confesses Jesus and Three Disciples See His Glory

meta.description: Peter identifies Jesus as God’s Messiah, after which Jesus predicts his rejection, death, and resurrection and defines costly discipleship. About eight days later his appearance changes on a mountain as Moses and Elijah speak with him.

events.title: Jesus Heals a Boy and Corrects the Disciples

meta.description: Jesus frees a boy after the disciples fail to do so and again foretells his betrayal. He counters their dispute about greatness with a child and tells them not to stop an outsider expelling demons in his name.
Jesus decisively begins the journey toward Jerusalem. He rebukes disciples who want to punish an unreceptive Samaritan village and warns would-be followers about the journey’s demands.

events.title: Seventy Disciples Are Sent and Return

meta.description: Jesus sends seventy disciples in pairs to heal and announce God’s approaching kingdom. They return joyful at their authority over spirits, and Jesus redirects their joy toward belonging to God.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Good Samaritan

meta.description: When a legal expert asks how to inherit life and who qualifies as a neighbor, Jesus describes a robbed traveler ignored by religious figures but aided generously by a Samaritan. He directs the questioner to practice the same mercy.

events.title: Martha Welcomes Jesus as Mary Listens

meta.description: Martha hosts Jesus but becomes distracted by serving while her sister Mary listens at his feet. Jesus affirms Mary’s attention to his teaching as the better priority.

events.title: Jesus Teaches His Disciples to Pray

meta.description: Jesus gives his disciples a pattern of prayer centered on God’s name, kingdom, provision, forgiveness, and deliverance. A story about a persistent friend and comparisons with parental generosity encourage confident persistence.

events.title: Jesus Answers Opponents and Denounces Hypocrisy

meta.description: After an exorcism Jesus refutes claims that his power comes from the ruler of demons and rejects demands for a sign beyond Jonah’s. At a Pharisee’s meal he pronounces woes against outward piety, neglected justice, and burdensome religious leadership.

events.title: Jesus Warns Against Hypocrisy and Greed
