meta.description: Jesus urges fearless public faithfulness and warns that possessions do not secure life. The parable of a rich landowner whose life ends after he enlarges his barns leads into teaching about trust, generosity, and heavenly treasure.

Through images of waiting servants, a thief, and a responsible manager, Jesus urges readiness and faithful stewardship. He also warns that his mission will expose division and calls the crowds to recognize the present moment.

events.title: Jesus Calls for Repentance and Heals a Bent Woman

meta.description: Jesus rejects the idea that victims of violence or disaster were uniquely sinful and tells of an unfruitful fig tree given more time. In a synagogue he frees a woman disabled for eighteen years and defends healing her on the Sabbath.

events.title: Jesus Teaches on the Narrow Door and Laments Jerusalem

meta.description: Traveling toward Jerusalem, Jesus warns that familiarity does not replace entering God’s kingdom and foresees people arriving from every direction. He refuses intimidation by Herod and laments Jerusalem’s rejection of God’s messengers.

events.title: Jesus Heals and Teaches at a Pharisee’s Dinner

meta.description: Jesus heals a man with edema on the Sabbath and silences objections. Observing the meal, he teaches humility and generous hospitality, then tells of invited guests whose excuses lead a host to fill his banquet with marginalized people.

events.title: Jesus Describes the Cost of Discipleship

meta.description: Jesus tells the traveling crowds that following him requires loyalty beyond family ties, acceptance of the cross, and surrender of possessions. Images of an unfinished tower and an outmatched king stress deliberate commitment.

events.title: Jesus Tells Three Parables About the Lost

meta.description: Responding to criticism that he welcomes sinners, Jesus tells of a recovered sheep, a recovered coin, and a wayward son welcomed by his father. Each story emphasizes joy over restoration while the elder son’s resentment mirrors the critics.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Wealth and Faithfulness

meta.description: A parable about a dishonest but shrewd manager leads to teaching on faithful use of wealth and undivided service to God. Jesus then contrasts a rich man’s luxury with poor Lazarus’s suffering and their reversed conditions after death.

events.title: Jesus Cleanses Ten People with Leprosy

meta.description: After teaching about forgiveness, faith, and humble obedience, Jesus cleanses ten people while traveling between Samaria and Galilee. Only a Samaritan returns to thank him and praise God.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Kingdom and the Son of Man

meta.description: Jesus tells Pharisees that God’s kingdom is already among them rather than arriving through easily observed signs. He warns disciples that the Son of Man’s revelation will be sudden and will follow suffering and rejection.

events.title: Jesus Feeds Five Thousand Near Passover

meta.description: Near Passover a large crowd follows Jesus beside the Sea of Galilee. He multiplies five barley loaves and two fish to feed them, but withdraws when they intend to force kingship upon him.
After dark the disciples row toward Capernaum through rough water. Jesus approaches their boat by walking on the sea, calms their fear, and they reach their destination.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Bread of Life

meta.description: The crowd finds Jesus at Capernaum after the feeding. He redirects their pursuit from temporary food to trust in the one sent by God and presents himself as the life-giving bread from heaven, provoking dispute over his claims.

events.title: Many Disciples Turn Away From Jesus

meta.description: Many followers reject Jesus' difficult teaching and cease traveling with him. Peter affirms the Twelve's trust in Jesus, while Jesus warns that one among them will betray him.

events.title: Jesus Teaches at the Festival of Booths

meta.description: Jesus travels privately to Jerusalem for the Festival of Booths and begins teaching publicly midway through it. Crowds debate his identity, authorities attempt to arrest him, and Jesus defends his Sabbath healing and divine commission.

events.title: Jesus Offers Living Water at the Festival

meta.description: On the festival's final day Jesus uses thirst and flowing water to describe the Spirit believers will receive. The declaration divides the crowd, temple police decline to arrest him, and Nicodemus challenges the leaders to grant him a hearing.

events.title: Jesus Refuses to Condemn an Accused Woman

meta.description: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman accused of adultery before Jesus as a test. He confronts the accusers with their own sin; they depart, and he releases the woman with a charge to abandon sin.

events.title: Jesus Debates His Opponents About Truth and Abraham

meta.description: Teaching in the temple, Jesus presents himself as the world's light and grounds his testimony in the Father who sent him. Debate over freedom, ancestry, and divine sonship escalates until his claim to precede Abraham prompts an attempt to stone him.

events.title: Jesus Gives Sight to a Man Born Blind

meta.description: Jesus makes mud and sends a man born blind to wash at Siloam, restoring his sight on the Sabbath. Repeated questioning leads the healed man to defend Jesus and be expelled, after which Jesus finds him and receives his worship.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Good Shepherd

meta.description: Using the images of a sheepfold, gate, flock, and shepherd, Jesus contrasts his protective self-giving with thieves and hired hands. His claim to lay down and take up his life again divides his hearers.

events.title: Jesus Faces Threats at the Festival of Dedication

meta.description: During winter at the Festival of Dedication, Jesus identifies his works as testimony and describes the unity of his action with the Father. Opponents attempt to stone and arrest him, but he escapes across the Jordan, where many believe.

events.title: Jesus Teaches in Judea About Marriage and Children

meta.description: After entering Judea, Jesus answers a test about divorce by appealing to God's purpose in creation. He then welcomes children brought for his blessing despite the disciples' objections.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Wealth and Kingdom Reward

meta.description: A wealthy man turns away after Jesus tells him to relinquish his possessions and follow. Jesus warns about wealth, promises renewal to his followers, and tells of vineyard workers who receive equal generosity despite differing hours of labor.

events.title: Jesus Predicts His Death and Redefines Greatness

meta.description: On the road to Jerusalem Jesus gives a detailed prediction of his betrayal, condemnation, crucifixion, and resurrection. When the sons of Zebedee seek places of honor, he teaches that greatness among his followers is expressed through service.

events.title: Jesus Heals Two Blind Men Near Jericho

meta.description: Two blind men beside the road repeatedly appeal to Jesus as David's son despite the crowd's rebuke. Jesus compassionately restores their sight, and they follow him.
Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey and colt as crowds spread garments and branches before him. The stirred city asks who he is, and the crowds identify him as the prophet from Nazareth.

events.title: Jesus Clears the Temple and Judges a Fig Tree

meta.description: Jesus drives merchants from the temple, heals blind and lame people there, and defends children's acclamation. The next morning he causes a fruitless fig tree to wither and teaches the disciples about faithful prayer.

events.title: Jesus Challenges Jerusalem's Leaders Through Parables

meta.description: When leaders question his authority, Jesus counters with a question about John's baptism. He tells parables of two sons, murderous tenants, and a wedding banquet that expose refusal of God's summons and warn of judgment.

events.title: Jesus Answers Tests About Tax, Resurrection, and the Law

meta.description: Jesus answers attempts to trap him concerning imperial taxation and resurrection, then identifies love of God and neighbor as the law's central commands. He closes by questioning how the Messiah can be both David's descendant and lord.

Jesus warns the crowds and disciples against leaders who seek status while burdening others. He pronounces woes on scribes and Pharisees for hypocrisy, neglected justice, and participation in violence against God's messengers, then laments over Jerusalem.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About the Temple's Fall and His Coming

meta.description: On the Mount of Olives Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and describes conflict, deception, persecution, upheaval, and the coming of the Son of Man. He urges watchfulness because the timing is unknown.

events.title: Jesus Teaches Readiness and Final Judgment

meta.description: Jesus tells parables of waiting attendants and entrusted wealth to stress preparedness and faithful action. He concludes with a scene in which the nations are separated according to their treatment of vulnerable people identified with him.

events.title: Leaders Plot as Jesus Is Anointed and Judas Bargains

meta.description: Jesus predicts his crucifixion while chief priests and elders plan his secret arrest. At Bethany a woman anoints him in anticipation of burial, and Judas agrees to betray him for thirty silver pieces.

events.title: Jesus Shares the Last Supper With the Twelve

meta.description: The disciples prepare the Passover meal, where Jesus identifies an impending betrayal. He gives bread and a cup to interpret his approaching death in relation to his body, covenant blood, and forgiveness.

After predicting the disciples' desertion and Peter's denials, Jesus prays three times in deep distress while his companions repeatedly fall asleep. He submits to the Father's will and announces the betrayer's approach.

events.title: Judas Betrays Jesus and the Disciples Flee

meta.description: Judas identifies Jesus with a kiss, and an armed crowd arrests him. Jesus rejects armed resistance, explains that events fulfill scripture, and is abandoned by all the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Is Condemned as Peter Denies Him

meta.description: The council hears testimony against Jesus and condemns him after the high priest questions him about being Messiah and Son of God. In the courtyard Peter denies knowing Jesus three times, then leaves in bitter grief.

events.title: Judas Dies and the Priests Buy a Burial Field

meta.description: The leaders hand Jesus to Pilate. Judas returns the betrayal money and hangs himself; the priests use the silver to purchase a field for burying foreigners.
Jesus remains largely silent before Pilate. Pressured by leaders and the crowd, Pilate releases Barabbas and hands Jesus over for flogging and crucifixion, after which soldiers mock him as a king.

Simon of Cyrene carries Jesus' cross to Golgotha, where Jesus is crucified between two bandits and mocked. Darkness covers the land before his death; the temple curtain tears, the earth shakes, tombs open, and the guards acknowledge his divine sonship.

events.title: Jesus Is Buried and His Tomb Is Guarded

meta.description: Joseph of Arimathea places Jesus' body in his new rock-cut tomb while women watch. The following day religious leaders secure the sealed tomb with Pilate's authorization and a guard.

events.title: Women Find the Empty Tomb and Meet the Risen Jesus

meta.description: At dawn after the Sabbath, an earthquake accompanies an angel's opening of the tomb. Mary Magdalene and the other Mary receive news that Jesus has risen, then meet and worship him as they go to tell the disciples.

events.title: The Guards Are Bribed to Report a Theft

meta.description: Some guards report the tomb's events to the chief priests. The leaders pay them to claim that the disciples stole Jesus' body while they slept and promise protection from the governor.

events.title: Jesus Commissions the Eleven in Galilee

meta.description: The eleven meet the risen Jesus on a Galilean mountain, where they worship though some hesitate. Claiming universal authority, he sends them to make and baptize disciples among all nations and to teach obedience to his commands.
Jesus approaches Jerusalem on a colt while crowds spread cloaks and branches and acclaim the coming Davidic kingdom. He surveys the temple and returns to Bethany with the twelve.

events.title: Jesus Drives Commerce from the Temple

meta.description: Jesus condemns a fruitless fig tree and then disrupts buying, selling, and money changing in the temple, teaching that the sanctuary should serve all nations in prayer. The withered tree later becomes an occasion to teach about faith, prayer, and forgiveness.
Chief priests, scribes, and elders demand the source of Jesus' authority. He answers with a question about John's baptism that they decline to resolve for fear of the crowd.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Violent Tenants

meta.description: Jesus describes tenants who abuse a landowner's servants and kill his beloved son before losing the vineyard. The leaders recognize the parable as directed against them but withdraw because they fear the crowd.

events.title: Jesus Answers Questions about Tax and Resurrection

meta.description: Jesus avoids a trap about imperial tax by distinguishing what belongs to the emperor from what belongs to God. He then answers Sadducees by teaching that resurrection life differs from marriage and that God is God of the living.
A scribe asks which commandment is foremost. Jesus joins wholehearted love of God with love of one's neighbor, and the scribe agrees that these surpass sacrifices.

events.title: Jesus Teaches about David, Scribes, and a Widow

meta.description: Jesus questions how the Messiah can be merely David's son, warns against status-seeking scribes who exploit widows, and points to a poor widow whose two small coins constitute her whole livelihood.

On the Mount of Olives Jesus predicts the temple's destruction and warns his disciples of deception, conflict, persecution, and severe distress. He promises the gathering of the elect and repeatedly urges vigilance because the final hour is unknown.

events.title: A Woman Anoints Jesus at Bethany

meta.description: Two days before Passover, leaders seek a discreet way to kill Jesus. At Simon's house a woman pours costly perfume on Jesus, which he interprets as preparation for burial; Judas then arranges to betray him.

The disciples prepare Passover in an upper room, where Jesus identifies an impending betrayal. He distributes bread and a cup as signs of his body and covenant blood and anticipates sharing wine anew in God's kingdom.

After predicting that the disciples will desert him and Peter will deny him, Jesus prays in deep anguish at Gethsemane. Three times his closest disciples fall asleep while he submits to the Father's will.

events.title: Judas Betrays and Jesus Is Arrested

meta.description: Judas identifies Jesus with a kiss to an armed group sent by Jerusalem authorities. Jesus is seized, one bystander wounds the high priest's servant, and all the disciples flee.

events.title: The Council Condemns Jesus as Peter Denies Him

meta.description: The council struggles to establish consistent testimony before condemning Jesus after the high priest questions him about his identity. In the courtyard Peter denies knowing Jesus three times and weeps when the rooster confirms the prediction.

events.title: Pilate Hands Jesus Over for Crucifixion

meta.description: Jerusalem's leaders deliver Jesus to Pilate and accuse him as king of the Jews. Pilate releases Barabbas at the crowd's demand, has Jesus flogged, and turns him over to soldiers who mock and abuse him.

Simon of Cyrene is compelled to carry the cross before Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two bandits. Darkness covers the land, Jesus dies, the temple curtain tears, and a centurion identifies him as God's Son while women followers watch.

Before the Sabbath, Joseph of Arimathea obtains Jesus' body from Pilate, wraps it in linen, and places it in a rock-cut tomb sealed with a stone. Mary Magdalene and Mary mother of Joses observe the burial place.

After the Sabbath, Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome find the tomb open and Jesus' body absent. A young man announces that Jesus has risen and directs them toward Galilee, but they flee in fear and amazement.

events.title: The Longer Ending Recounts Appearances and Commission

meta.description: The longer textual ending reports appearances to Mary Magdalene, two travelers, and the eleven, followed by a worldwide commission. It concludes with Jesus' ascension and the disciples' preaching accompanied by signs.

events.title: Jesus Tells Parables About Persistent and Humble Prayer

meta.description: A persistent widow eventually receives justice from an unjust judge, encouraging continued prayer. A second story contrasts a self-satisfied Pharisee with a tax collector who humbly seeks mercy.

events.title: Jesus Welcomes Children and Challenges a Rich Ruler

meta.description: Jesus welcomes infants whom the disciples try to prevent from approaching and presents childlike reception as necessary for the kingdom. A wealthy ruler grieves when told to distribute his property and follow, prompting teaching about wealth and salvation.

events.title: Jesus Predicts His Death and Heals a Blind Man

meta.description: Jesus privately tells the twelve that he will be abused, killed, and raised in Jerusalem, though they do not understand. Near Jericho he restores sight to a persistent blind beggar who then follows him.

At Jericho Jesus calls the wealthy chief tax collector Zacchaeus down from a tree and stays at his house. Zacchaeus promises substantial generosity and restitution, and Jesus declares that restoration has reached the household.

events.title: Jesus Tells the Parable of the Ten Pounds

meta.description: Because listeners expect God’s kingdom to appear immediately near Jerusalem, Jesus describes a nobleman who departs to receive royal authority. On returning, he rewards servants who traded entrusted money and judges resistance and inactivity.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem and Clears the Temple

meta.description: Jesus rides toward Jerusalem on a colt amid his disciples’ praise, then weeps over the city and foretells its siege. He drives sellers from the temple and teaches there daily while leaders seek to kill him.

events.title: Jesus Answers an Authority Challenge and Warns Leaders

meta.description: When leaders demand the source of his authority, Jesus asks whether John’s baptism came from heaven or human beings. He then tells of tenants who kill a vineyard owner’s son, and the leaders recognize the warning against them.

Jesus avoids a trap about imperial taxes by distinguishing obligations to the emperor and to God. He answers Sadducees about resurrection, questions assumptions about David’s son, and warns against scribes who pursue honor while exploiting widows.

events.title: Jesus Observes a Widow and Foretells the Temple’s Fall

meta.description: Jesus highlights a poor widow’s small offering as greater than gifts from abundance. He predicts the temple’s destruction, persecution, Jerusalem’s distress, and the Son of Man’s coming, urging alertness and endurance.
As leaders seek a way to kill Jesus without provoking the crowd, Judas agrees to betray him for money. Jesus sends Peter and John to prepare the Passover meal in an upstairs room.

At Passover Jesus gives bread and a cup to interpret his approaching death and identifies a betrayer at the table. He corrects the apostles’ rivalry, foretells Peter’s denials, and prepares them for the coming crisis.

events.title: Jesus Prays and Is Arrested on the Mount of Olives

meta.description: Jesus prays in anguish while his disciples sleep, submitting his will to the Father. Judas leads an armed group to arrest him, and Jesus heals the high priest’s servant after a disciple cuts off his ear.

events.title: Peter Denies Jesus and the Council Questions Him

meta.description: Peter follows to the high priest’s house but denies knowing Jesus three times and leaves weeping after the rooster crows. Jesus’ captors mock him, and at daybreak the council questions him about being Messiah and Son of God.

events.title: Pilate and Herod Examine Jesus Before His Sentence

meta.description: The council accuses Jesus before Pilate, who sends the Galilean to Herod and receives him back after mockery. Though Pilate repeatedly finds no capital offense, the crowd’s demand prevails, Barabbas is released, and Jesus is handed over.

Simon of Cyrene carries the cross as Jesus is led to the place of execution with two criminals. Jesus is crucified between them; darkness covers the land, the temple curtain tears, and he dies as followers watch from a distance.

Joseph of Arimathea receives Jesus’ body and places it in a previously unused rock-cut tomb before the Sabbath. The Galilean women observe the location, prepare burial spices, and rest on the Sabbath.

At dawn on the first day of the week, women find the stone moved and Jesus’ body absent. Two heavenly messengers announce his resurrection; the apostles initially dismiss the report, but Peter runs to inspect the tomb.

events.title: The Risen Jesus Appears on the Emmaus Road

meta.description: Jesus joins two grieving disciples traveling to Emmaus, explains the scriptures concerning the Messiah, and remains unrecognized until breaking bread with them. They immediately return to Jerusalem to report the encounter.

events.title: The Risen Jesus Appears to the Gathered Disciples

meta.description: Jesus appears among the gathered disciples, shows them his hands and feet, and eats fish to assure them that he is bodily present. He opens their understanding of scripture and commissions worldwide proclamation beginning in Jerusalem.
Jesus leads the disciples toward Bethany, blesses them, and is carried into heaven. They worship him, return joyfully to Jerusalem, and continue praising God in the temple.

events.title: Jesus Raises Lazarus From the Dead

meta.description: After Lazarus dies at Bethany, Jesus arrives when he has been entombed four days. He comforts Martha and Mary, weeps with the mourners, then calls Lazarus from the tomb alive.

Lazarus's restoration leads many to believe, while others report it to the Pharisees. Caiaphas persuades the council that Jesus should die for the nation, and Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches.

Six days before Passover, Mary anoints Jesus' feet with costly perfume at a dinner in Bethany. Jesus connects her act with his burial, while the chief priests expand their plot to include Lazarus because his survival draws believers.

events.title: Jesus Enters Jerusalem as a King

meta.description: Festival crowds welcome Jesus with palm branches as he enters Jerusalem on a young donkey. Witnesses spread news of Lazarus's raising, and the Pharisees fear the breadth of his appeal.

events.title: Greeks Seek Jesus as His Public Ministry Closes

meta.description: Greek worshipers ask to see Jesus, who announces that his glorifying hour has arrived and compares fruitful death to a planted grain. A heavenly voice answers his prayer, and he gives a final public appeal to believe in the light despite widespread resistance.
During supper before Passover, Jesus washes the disciples' feet despite Peter's objection. He presents his humble service as the pattern they should practice toward one another.
Troubled at supper, Jesus announces that one disciple will betray him and gives a morsel to Judas as the identifying sign. Judas departs into the night to carry out the betrayal.

events.title: Jesus Commands Love and Predicts Peter's Denial

meta.description: After Judas leaves, Jesus commands the disciples to love one another in the pattern of his own love. Peter promises to follow him at any cost, but Jesus predicts that Peter will deny him three times before morning.

events.title: Jesus Promises the Father's Presence and the Spirit

meta.description: Jesus comforts his disciples with the promise of a place with the Father and identifies himself as their way to God. He promises that the Holy Spirit will teach and remind them, and leaves them peace before his departure.

events.title: Jesus Teaches About Abiding, Love, and Witness

meta.description: Jesus depicts himself as a vine whose branches bear fruit by remaining in him. He calls the disciples friends, commands mutual love, warns of the world's hostility, and commissions them to testify alongside the Spirit.

events.title: Jesus Prepares the Disciples for Sorrow and Joy

meta.description: Jesus warns that the disciples will face expulsion and persecution, yet says his departure enables the Spirit's coming. He promises that their approaching grief will turn to joy and encourages them to find peace in his victory.

events.title: Jesus Prays for His Disciples and Future Believers

meta.description: Jesus prays that the Father will glorify him as his earthly work reaches completion. He asks protection, holiness, unity, and shared glory for his disciples and for those who will believe through their witness.

events.title: Jesus Is Arrested in the Garden

meta.description: Judas leads soldiers and temple police to the garden across the Kidron. Jesus steps forward and submits to arrest while securing the disciples' release, and Peter cuts off the ear of the high priest's servant Malchus.

events.title: Annas Questions Jesus as Peter Denies Him

meta.description: Jesus is questioned about his teaching before Annas and then sent bound to Caiaphas. Meanwhile Peter denies association with Jesus three times beside a charcoal fire before the rooster crows.

The authorities bring Jesus to Pilate early in the morning and seek a Roman judgment against him. Pilate questions Jesus about kingship and truth, finds no case against him, and offers to release him, but the crowd chooses Barabbas.

Soldiers flog and mock Jesus with royal dress and a thorny crown. Though Pilate repeatedly presents him as innocent and tries to release him, political pressure from the chief priests leads him to authorize crucifixion.

Jesus is crucified at Golgotha between two others under Pilate's inscription naming him king of the Jews. He entrusts his mother to the beloved disciple, dies, and is confirmed dead when a soldier pierces his side.
Joseph of Arimathea receives permission to remove Jesus' body, and Nicodemus brings a large quantity of burial spices. They wrap the body and place it in a nearby new garden tomb before the Sabbath.

events.title: Peter and the Beloved Disciple Find the Tomb Empty

meta.description: Before dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene finds the tomb open and alerts Peter and the beloved disciple. They run to the tomb and find the burial cloths without Jesus' body.

Mary remains weeping near the empty tomb and initially mistakes the risen Jesus for the gardener. When he addresses her personally, she recognizes him and carries news of the encounter to the disciples.

events.title: Jesus Appears to the Gathered Disciples

meta.description: On the evening of the resurrection, Jesus appears among disciples gathered behind locked doors. He shows his wounds, commissions them as the Father sent him, and breathes the Holy Spirit upon them.

Thomas doubts the other disciples' report because he was absent from Jesus' first appearance. A week later Jesus appears again and invites Thomas to examine his wounds, prompting Thomas's confession of faith.

events.title: Jesus Provides a Catch and Breakfast by the Sea

meta.description: Seven disciples fish overnight on the Sea of Tiberias without success. At daybreak the risen Jesus directs them to a great catch and serves them bread and fish on the shore.

events.title: Jesus Entrusts His Flock to Peter

meta.description: After breakfast Jesus asks Peter three times about his love and entrusts him with care for the community. He foretells Peter's costly death, calls him again to follow, and corrects speculation about the beloved disciple's future.

events.title: Jesus Ascends from the Mount of Olives

meta.description: After appearing to the apostles for forty days, Jesus instructs them to await the Holy Spirit and commissions them as witnesses from Jerusalem to the ends of the earth. They watch him ascend and then return to Jerusalem in prayer.

Peter leads about one hundred twenty believers in choosing a replacement for Judas from among those who accompanied Jesus' ministry. After prayer and casting lots, Matthias is added to the eleven apostles.

events.title: The Holy Spirit Comes at Pentecost

meta.description: At Pentecost the disciples are filled with the Holy Spirit and speak in languages understood by pilgrims from many nations. Peter explains the event through Israel's scriptures and proclaims Jesus' resurrection, after which about three thousand people are baptized.

events.title: The Jerusalem Community Shares Its Life

meta.description: The growing community devotes itself to apostolic teaching, fellowship, shared meals, and prayer. Believers share possessions according to need, gather in the temple and homes, and continue gaining new members.

events.title: Peter Heals a Man at the Temple

meta.description: Peter restores a man unable to walk since birth at the temple's Beautiful Gate. As a crowd gathers in amazement, Peter attributes the healing to Jesus and calls Israel to turn back to God.

events.title: Peter and John Testify before the Council

meta.description: Temple authorities arrest Peter and John for proclaiming resurrection in Jesus. The council cannot deny the healed man's recovery, so it threatens the apostles and releases them, while the number of believing men has grown to about five thousand.

After hearing of the council's threats, the believers pray together and are filled anew with the Holy Spirit. Their common life includes generous distribution of property proceeds, exemplified by Barnabas's gift of a field.

events.title: Ananias and Sapphira Die after Deception

meta.description: Ananias and Sapphira secretly retain part of a property's proceeds while presenting their gift as complete. Peter exposes their deception, and each dies in turn, bringing fear upon the whole church.
The apostles perform many signs among people gathered at Solomon's Portico. Growing crowds bring sick and tormented people from Jerusalem and neighboring towns, and all are healed.

events.title: The Apostles Are Freed and Flogged

meta.description: The high priest has the apostles imprisoned, but an angel releases them to resume teaching in the temple. Brought again before the council, they escape execution after Gamaliel urges restraint, receive a flogging, and continue proclaiming Jesus.

events.title: Seven Are Appointed for the Daily Distribution

meta.description: A complaint that Greek-speaking widows are neglected prompts the community to select seven Spirit-filled men to oversee the daily distribution. The apostles pray and lay hands on them while the Jerusalem movement continues to grow.

Opponents seize Stephen and bring false testimony before the council. He recounts Israel's history, accuses his hearers of resisting God, sees a heavenly vision, and is stoned while Saul approves the killing.

A severe persecution follows Stephen's death, scattering believers through Judea and Samaria while the apostles remain in Jerusalem. Saul enters homes, imprisons believers, and those dispersed carry the message into new places.

events.title: Philip Proclaims the Messiah in Samaria

meta.description: Philip's preaching and signs bring many Samaritans to baptism, including the magician Simon. Peter and John come from Jerusalem and pray for the converts to receive the Holy Spirit, then rebuke Simon when he tries to buy apostolic power.

Directed to the Gaza road, Philip meets an Ethiopian court official reading Isaiah and explains the passage in relation to Jesus. He baptizes the traveler, is carried away by the Spirit, and continues preaching from Azotus to Caesarea.

While traveling to arrest disciples in Damascus, Saul is struck blind by a heavenly encounter with Jesus. The disciple Ananias lays hands on him despite his fear, and Saul regains sight, receives the Holy Spirit, and is baptized.

events.title: Saul Preaches in Damascus and Jerusalem

meta.description: Saul immediately proclaims Jesus in Damascus and escapes a plot against him by being lowered through the city wall. Barnabas introduces him to wary Jerusalem believers, and another threat leads the community to send him through Caesarea to Tarsus.

events.title: Peter Heals Aeneas and Raises Tabitha

meta.description: At Lydda Peter heals Aeneas after eight years of paralysis. In Joppa he prays over the dead disciple Tabitha and restores her to life, leading many in the region to believe.

events.title: Cornelius and Peter Receive Coordinated Visions

meta.description: An angel directs the Roman centurion Cornelius to summon Peter from Joppa. Meanwhile Peter sees a vision overturning distinctions of ritual impurity and is instructed to accompany the centurion's messengers without hesitation.

events.title: The Spirit Falls on Cornelius's Household

meta.description: Peter enters Cornelius's Gentile household and announces God's impartial welcome through Jesus. The Holy Spirit falls on the listeners while Peter is speaking, and he orders them baptized.

Jerusalem believers criticize Peter for eating with uncircumcised people. He recounts the visions and the Spirit's arrival, and the assembly concludes that God has granted life-giving repentance to Gentiles as well.

events.title: A Church Forms among Greeks at Antioch

meta.description: Scattered believers proclaim Jesus to Greeks in Antioch, and Barnabas is sent to encourage the growing church. He brings Saul from Tarsus for a year of teaching, while the community also prepares famine relief for Judea after Agabus's warning.

events.title: Herod Kills James and Peter Escapes Prison

meta.description: Herod Agrippa executes James son of Zebedee and arrests Peter during the festival season. An angel leads Peter past his guards, and he reaches believers praying at Mary's house before leaving for another place.

During a public address at Caesarea, Herod accepts divine acclaim from the crowd and is struck down. Barnabas and Saul complete their relief mission and return with John Mark as the movement continues to spread.
While Antioch's prophets and teachers worship and fast, the Holy Spirit directs the church to set apart Barnabas and Saul. The community prays, lays hands on them, and sends them out.

Barnabas, Saul, and John Mark preach across Cyprus from Salamis to Paphos. Saul, now also called Paul, confronts the magician Elymas, whose temporary blindness contributes to the proconsul Sergius Paulus becoming a believer.

After John Mark leaves the mission at Perga, Paul and Barnabas enter Pisidian Antioch and address the synagogue. Their proclamation attracts much of the city, but opposition drives them onward after they announce a widening mission to Gentiles.

events.title: Division at Iconium Forces the Mission onward

meta.description: Paul and Barnabas gain Jewish and Greek believers at Iconium and remain there as signs accompany their teaching. When a divided city turns toward violence and stoning, they escape into Lycaonia and continue preaching.

events.title: Paul Heals a Man and Is Stoned at Lystra

meta.description: Paul heals a man unable to walk from birth, prompting the crowd to mistake him and Barnabas for gods and attempt sacrifice. Opponents later turn the crowd against Paul and stone him, but he rises and departs for Derbe.

events.title: Paul and Barnabas Return to Antioch

meta.description: After making disciples at Derbe, Paul and Barnabas retrace their route, strengthen the new churches, and appoint elders. They sail from Attalia to Syrian Antioch and report how their mission opened faith to Gentiles.

Disagreement over requiring circumcision brings Paul and Barnabas to meet the apostles and elders in Jerusalem. Peter, Paul, Barnabas, and James support welcoming Gentiles without imposing the full law, and a letter communicates limited communal requirements to Antioch.

events.title: Paul and Barnabas Begin Separate Journeys

meta.description: A sharp disagreement over John Mark divides the former partners. Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus, while Paul chooses Silas and travels through Syria and Cilicia strengthening churches.
At Lystra Paul recruits the well-regarded disciple Timothy and has him circumcised in view of local Jewish communities. The travelers deliver Jerusalem's decisions and strengthen the churches.

events.title: A Vision Directs Paul toward Macedonia

meta.description: Prevented from preaching in several regions of Asia Minor, the group reaches Troas. Paul's night vision of a Macedonian requesting help convinces them to cross into Europe.

events.title: Lydia and Her Household Are Baptized

meta.description: At Philippi Paul speaks to women gathered for prayer beside the river. Lydia, a merchant from Thyatira, responds to the message, receives baptism with her household, and hosts the missionaries.

events.title: Paul and Silas Are Jailed at Philippi

meta.description: After Paul frees an enslaved girl from a divining spirit, her owners have him and Silas beaten and imprisoned. An earthquake opens the prison, but they remain and prevent the jailer's suicide; he and his household are baptized before the magistrates apologize to the Roman citizens.

events.title: The Mission Faces Opposition in Macedonia

meta.description: Paul's synagogue teaching gains adherents in Thessalonica, but a hostile crowd attacks Jason's house and forces the missionaries onward. Beroeans receive the message eagerly until opponents arrive from Thessalonica, prompting Paul's departure for Athens.

Distressed by Athens's many idols, Paul debates in its synagogue and marketplace and is brought before the Areopagus. He presents the creator as transcending human temples and calls for repentance in light of resurrection, winning a small group of believers.

events.title: Paul Establishes a Ministry in Corinth

meta.description: Paul works with the recently displaced Aquila and Priscilla and teaches in Corinth for eighteen months. After synagogue opposition he focuses on Gentiles, while Crispus and many Corinthians believe and are baptized.

events.title: Gallio Dismisses the Case against Paul

meta.description: Opponents bring Paul before Gallio's tribunal and accuse him over unlawful worship. The proconsul treats the dispute as an internal question of Jewish law and dismisses the case.

events.title: Paul Returns through Ephesus to Antioch

meta.description: Paul leaves Corinth with Priscilla and Aquila, briefly teaches at Ephesus, and sails onward while promising to return if possible. After visiting Caesarea and Jerusalem, he reaches Antioch and later begins strengthening disciples through Galatia and Phrygia.

The eloquent Alexandrian teacher Apollos arrives in Ephesus knowing only John's baptism. Priscilla and Aquila explain the movement more fully, and he then travels to Achaia and publicly argues that Jesus is the Messiah.

events.title: Paul Baptizes Twelve Disciples at Ephesus

meta.description: At Ephesus Paul meets about twelve disciples acquainted only with John's baptism. They are baptized in Jesus' name and receive the Holy Spirit when Paul lays hands on them.

events.title: Paul Teaches throughout His Ephesian Ministry

meta.description: Paul first teaches in the synagogue and then spends two years in the lecture hall of Tyrannus, allowing the message to spread across Asia. Extraordinary healings, a failed imitation by Sceva's sons, and a public burning of magical books mark the ministry's impact.

events.title: The Ephesian Theater Erupts over Artemis

meta.description: Silversmiths fearing loss of trade stir a crowd in defense of Artemis and drag Paul's companions into the theater. Friends prevent Paul from entering, and the town clerk disperses the assembly by directing complaints toward the courts.

events.title: Paul Travels through Macedonia and Greece

meta.description: Paul leaves Ephesus, encourages believers through Macedonia, and spends three months in Greece. A plot changes his planned voyage to Syria, so he returns through Macedonia with representatives from several churches.

During an extended nighttime meeting at Troas, the young Eutychus falls asleep at a window and drops three stories. Paul embraces him and restores him alive before continuing the gathering until dawn.

events.title: Paul Bids Farewell to the Ephesian Elders

meta.description: Hurrying toward Jerusalem, Paul summons the Ephesian elders to Miletus. He reviews his ministry, warns of future dangers, entrusts them with care of the church, and shares an emotional farewell.

events.title: Warnings Accompany Paul's Journey to Jerusalem

meta.description: Paul's party sails along the eastern Mediterranean toward Jerusalem. Disciples at Tyre warn him, and at Caesarea Agabus symbolically predicts his arrest, but Paul continues despite his companions' pleas.

events.title: Paul Meets James and Enters Purification

meta.description: Jerusalem's elders welcome Paul's report of his Gentile ministry but describe rumors that he rejects Jewish customs. At their advice he joins four men completing vows and enters the temple purification rites.

Jews from Asia accuse Paul of teaching against Israel and falsely suppose he brought a Gentile into the temple. A Roman tribune rescues him from the violent crowd, arrests him, and permits him to address the people from the barracks steps.

events.title: Paul Defends His Mission to the Crowd

meta.description: Paul recounts his former persecution, encounter near Damascus, and commission to Gentiles. The crowd erupts at the mention of Gentiles, but Paul avoids examination by flogging when he reveals his Roman citizenship.

events.title: Paul Divides the Council over Resurrection

meta.description: Before the council, Paul identifies his hope in resurrection as the issue, provoking conflict between Pharisees and Sadducees. Soldiers remove him from the violence, and that night he receives assurance that he will also testify in Rome.

events.title: A Murder Plot Sends Paul to Caesarea

meta.description: More than forty conspirators plan to ambush and kill Paul, but his nephew reports the plot to the Roman tribune. A large escort transfers Paul by night to Governor Felix at Caesarea.

events.title: Paul Answers His Accusers before Felix

meta.description: The attorney Tertullus accuses Paul of sedition and temple profanation, while Paul denies stirring any disturbance and locates the dispute in resurrection hope. Felix postpones judgment and repeatedly summons Paul while hoping for a bribe.

events.title: Felix Leaves Paul Imprisoned for Two Years

meta.description: Paul remains in Caesarean custody for two years. When Porcius Festus succeeds Felix, the outgoing governor leaves Paul imprisoned as a concession to Judean leaders.
Festus hears renewed charges against Paul and proposes a Jerusalem trial. Paul invokes his right as a Roman citizen to appeal to the emperor, and Festus agrees to send him.

Festus presents Paul's unresolved case to Agrippa and Bernice before sending him to Rome. Paul recounts his calling and resurrection hope; Agrippa and the officials conclude that he has done nothing deserving imprisonment or death.

events.title: Paul's Voyage Is Driven across the Mediterranean

meta.description: Paul sails for Italy under the centurion Julius, but the ship leaves Crete too late in the season and is caught in a violent northeaster. After fourteen days adrift, Paul reports divine assurance that all aboard will survive and encourages the passengers to eat.

The vessel runs aground and breaks apart, yet all 276 people reach Malta alive. Paul survives a viper bite, heals the father of the island's leading man, and cures other sick residents during the three-month stay.

After wintering on Malta, the party sails through Syracuse, Rhegium, and Puteoli. Roman believers travel out to meet Paul, who enters the capital under guard but is permitted to live in private quarters.

Paul explains his appeal and innocence to local Jewish leaders, who arrange a fuller hearing. Some accept his scriptural case for Jesus while others reject it, and Paul declares that Gentiles will receive the message.

events.title: Paul Teaches Freely under Guard in Rome

meta.description: For two years Paul supports his own lodging and welcomes everyone who visits him. Though still in custody, he openly proclaims God's kingdom and teaches about Jesus without hindrance.
